One who reduces them to a degree by which his body becomes weak and unable to perform what is obligatory upon him, whether acts of worship or earning for himself and those he supports, opposes what God has commanded and guided to. One who is extravagant in spending in a manner that only the foolish and wasteful do opposes what God has prescribed for His servants and falls under the Qur'anic prohibition. Likewise, one who prohibits what is lawful or permits what is unlawful enters among the extravagant and leaves the moderate.

Among extravagance is eating without need, and at a time of being full.

His saying: ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has brought forth for His servants?﴾ Zeenah is what a person adorns himself with, whether clothing or other permissible things, such as metals about which no prohibition has come concerning adorning oneself with them, jewels, and the like. It has been said that it refers only to clothing, but there is no basis for this. Rather, it is among what the verse includes. There is no blame on one who wears fine, expensive clothing so long as it is not something God has forbidden, and no blame on one who adorns himself with any of the things that have a place in adornment and which no legal impediment prevents. Whoever claims that this contradicts asceticism has clearly erred.

We have already presented in this what is sufficient. Likewise the good things (al-tayyibat) of foods, drinks, and the like that people eat: there is no asceticism in abandoning the good of them. For this reason the verse came framed by a question that implies denunciation of those who forbid that for themselves or for others.

How excellent is what Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: "He has erred greatly who prefers wearing hair and wool over wearing cotton and linen, when the way to them is lawful and available; and who eats herbs and lentils and chooses them over wheat bread; and who abandons eating meat out of fear of the onset of desire." We have already quoted something similar from him at length.

The good things (al-tayyibat) are the enjoyable foods. It has been said that it is a general term for what is good in earnings and in food.

His saying: ﴿Say: They are for those who believed in the life of this world﴾, meaning that they belong to them originally, even if the disbelievers share them with them as long as they are in this life. ﴿Exclusively on the Day of Resurrection﴾, meaning specifically for them on the Day of Resurrection, with the disbelievers not sharing them.

Nafi' read khalisatan (exclusively) with the raf' (nominative), which is the reading of Ibn 'Abbas, as a predicate after a predicate. The rest read it with the nasb (accusative), as a circumstantial state (hal).

Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: "It is not permissible to pause at al-dunya (the world), because what follows it is connected to His saying ﴿for those who believed﴾, and khalisatan is a circumstantial state from it, with the sense: Say, it is established for those who believed in the life of this world, while it is pure for them on the Day of Resurrection."

His saying: ﴿Thus do We detail the verses for a people who know﴾, meaning, in this manner of detail, We detail the verses containing what is lawful and what is forbidden.

His saying: ﴿Say: My Lord has only forbidden the indecencies﴾. Fawahish is the plural of fahishah, and its explanation has already been given: ﴿what is apparent of them and what is concealed﴾, meaning what is openly done and what is secretly done. It has been said that it is specific to the indecencies of adultery, but there is no basis for this. Ithm (sin) encompasses every disobedience that causes sin. It has been said that it refers specifically to wine. From this is the poet's saying:

"I drank sin until my reason was lost; so sin takes away the intellects."

Similar is the saying of another:

"He drinks sin openly from the cup."

A group of scholars have denied the view of those who restricted ithm to wine. Al-Nahhas said: "As for ithm being wine, this is not known. Its reality is that it encompasses all acts of disobedience, as the poet said:

'I found that the best course is the fear of God, and its worst is sin.'"

Al-Farra' said: "Ithm is what falls short of the truth, and domineering over people." End.

There is nothing in applying the word ithm to wine that indicates it is restricted to it. Rather, it is one of the acts of disobedience to which it truly applies.

In al-Sihah it is said: "Wine is sometimes called ithm," and he recited:

"I drank the sin, the verse..."

Al-Harawi also recited it before him in his Gharibah.

His saying: ﴿and transgression without right﴾. Al-baghy is the injustice that exceeds its limit. He singled it out for mention after its inclusion in what preceded because it is a grave sin, as in His saying: ﴿He forbids indecency, wrongdoing, and transgression﴾ (al-Nahl: 90). ﴿And that you associate with God that for which He has sent down no authority﴾, meaning that you make for God a partner for whom He has not sent down any proof upon you. The intent is to mock the polytheists, because God does not send down evidence that another is a partner to Him. ﴿And that you say about God what you do not know﴾, of its reality and that God said it. This is like what they used to attribute to God, glorified is He, of permissions and prohibitions that He had not authorized.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Muslim, al-Nasa'i, and others narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that the women used to circumambulate the House naked, except that a woman would place a rag over her private part, and say:

"Today some of it, or all of it, will appear; and what appears of it, I will not make lawful."

So God revealed: ﴿Take your adornment at every mosque﴾.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him concerning the verse that he said: "The men used to circumambulate the House naked, so God commanded them to adorn themselves."

Zeenah is clothing, what conceals the private parts, and what else there is of good wheat and goods.

Ibn 'Adi, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Take the adornment of prayer." They said: "And what is the adornment of prayer?" He said: "Wear your sandals and pray in them."

al-'Uqayli, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn 'Asakir narrated from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning God's saying: ﴿Take your adornment at every mosque﴾, that he said: "Pray in your sandals."

The hadiths on the legitimacy of praying in sandals are very numerous. As for whether that is the interpretation of the verse, as is narrated in these two hadiths, I do not know the status of their chains.

It has been reported that the prohibition applies to a man praying in a single garment with nothing of it on his shoulders, and this is in the two Sahihs and elsewhere, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.

'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated from Ibn 'Abbas who said: God permitted eating and drinking as long as it is not extravagance or self-conceit.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed, He does not love the extravagant﴾ that he said: "In food and drink."

'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated through 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Eat, drink, give charity, and dress without self-conceit or extravagance, for God, glorified is He, loves to see the effect of His blessing upon His servant."

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas who said: Quraysh used to circumambulate the House while naked, whistling and clapping. So God revealed: ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God﴾, and they were commanded to wear clothing. ﴿Say: They are for those who believed in the life of this world, exclusively on the Day of Resurrection.﴾ He said: "They benefit from them in this world, and no sin will follow them concerning them on the Day of Resurrection."

'Abd ibn Humayd and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Dahhak concerning ﴿Say: They are for those who believed in the life of this world﴾ that he said: "The polytheists share with the believers the splendor of this world, and it is exclusively for the believers on the Day of Resurrection, not for the polytheists."

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿and the good things of provision﴾ that he said: "Fat, meat, and clarified butter."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him who said: "The people of the Jahiliyyah used to forbid things that God had made lawful, of clothing and other things, and this is God's saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision, and you made from it what is forbidden and what is lawful?﴾ (Yunus: 59). And this is this. So God revealed: ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has brought forth for His servants and the good things of provision? Say: They are for those who believed in the life of this world﴾, meaning, the Muslims shared with the disbelievers in the good things in the life of this world, so they ate from the good foods of it, wore from the fine clothing of it, and married from its righteous women. Then God will make the good things pure in the Hereafter for those who believed, and the disbelievers will have no share in them."

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "What appeared of them is nakedness, and what was concealed is fornication. They used to circumambulate the House naked."

Ibn Jarir narrated from Mujahid concerning the verse, who said: "What appeared of them is the circumambulation of the Jahiliyyah while naked, and what was concealed is fornication."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Suddi, concerning His saying: "And sin," he said: "Disobedience." "And transgression," he said: "That he transgresses against people without right."

The commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on Surah al-A'raf, verses 34–39:

﴿For every nation there is a term (ajal)﴾, meaning a specific, appointed time in which their punishment from Allah descends upon them, or in which He causes them to die. It is also possible to read the verse as covering both matters together. The pronoun in "ajaluhum" refers to "every nation." That is: when the term of each nation among the nations comes, what He has decreed for them will take place at that term, and they will not delay from it by an hour or advance from it by an hour.

Abu al-Su'ud said, in substance: His words "nor can they advance (yastaqdimun)" are conjoined to "delay (yasta'khirun)," but not to show the negation of advancing while advancing is possible in itself, as with delaying. Rather, it is for emphasis in negating delay, by placing it in the category of what is rationally impossible. It has also been said that the meaning of "coming" is approaching, to the point where advancing is possible in general, like the arrival of the day that was set for their destruction, an hour of which could be advanced. But this is not the right view.

Ibn Sirin read "ajalahum" in the plural (ajalahum as "their terms"). The hour was singled out for mention because it is the smallest of the names of time periods.

The majority of scholars have used this verse as evidence that every dead person dies at his appointed term, even if his death was by killing, falling from a height, or the like. The discussion of this is very lengthy. Similar to this verse is His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿No nation can advance its term, nor can they delay﴾ (al-Hijr: 5).

His words: ﴿O children of Adam, if messengers come to you﴾, to the end of the verse. "In" (in) is the conditional particle, and "ma" is an added particle for emphasis. For this reason the energetic nun (al-nun al-mu'akkidah) is attached to the verb. The "qasas" (narratives, accounts) has already had its meaning explained. The meaning is: if messengers come to you from among yourselves, who inform you of My rulings and explain them to you, then whoever fears Allah (ittaqa) and makes things right (aslaha), meaning he guards against the disobedience of Allah and sets right the condition of his own soul by following the messengers and responding to them, ﴿there shall be no fear upon them, nor shall they grieve﴾. This conditional sentence is the answer to the first condition. It has also been said that its answer is what the speech implies: that is, if messengers from among you come to you relating My signs to you, then obey them.

The first view is preferable, and al-Zajjaj held it.

As for those who denied Our signs, which Our messengers recite to them, and were arrogant toward accepting them and acting upon what they contain: ﴿those are the companions of the Fire; therein they will abide forever﴾, not leaving it because of their disbelief in denying the signs and the messengers.

﴿Who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah or denies His signs?﴾ That is, no one is more unjust than him. Its verification has already been mentioned. The reference in His words "those" is to the deniers who were arrogant, who will receive ﴿their portion from the Book﴾, that is, from what Allah has written for them of good and evil. It has also been said that it means they will receive a share of the punishment according to the measure of their disbelief. It has also been said that "the Book" here is the Qur'an, because the punishment of the disbelievers is mentioned in it. And it has been said that it is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

His words: ﴿until, when Our messengers come to them﴾, that is, up to a limit which is this. The clause ﴿taking their souls﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal).

The "messengers" here means the Angel of Death and his helpers. It has been said that "hatta" (until) here is the one used for beginning (ibtida'iyyah, i.e., introducing a new sentence). But it is not hidden that its being used to begin a speech after it does not preclude its being a limit for what came before it. The interrogation in His words: ﴿Where are those you used to call upon besides Allah?﴾ is for rebuke and reproach: that is, where are the deities you used to call upon besides Allah and worship? The clause "They will say: they have strayed from us" is a resumptive clause (isti'nafiyyah), presupposing a question, to which it is the answer: that is, they have gone away from us and vanished, so we do not know where they are. ﴿And they will bear witness against themselves that they were disbelievers﴾, that is, they will acknowledge their disbelief against themselves.

His words: ﴿He will say: Enter among nations that have passed away before you﴾. The speaker is Allah, mighty and majestic. The "fi" (in) here means "ma'a" (with): that is, with nations. It has also been said that it keeps its original meaning, and the sense is: enter into their company. It has also been said that this is the statement of Malik, the keeper of the Fire. By "the nations that have passed away before them" from among the jinn and mankind are meant the disbelievers of the two groups, from the earlier nations. ﴿Whenever a nation enters, it curses its sister﴾, that is, the earlier nation that preceded it into the Fire. It is called its "sister" with regard to religion, or misguidance, or being in the Fire. ﴿Until, when they have overtaken one another therein﴾, that is, have caught up with one another. The "tadarruk" means successive arrival, following one another, and gathering together in the Fire.

al-A'mash read "tadarakû" in its original form without idgham (assimilation of the letters).

Ibn Mas'ud read "hatta idha adraku" (until, when they overtook), meaning some of them overtook others.

It is related from Abu 'Amr that he recited with the cutting of the connecting alif (qat' alif al-wasl). It is as if he paused on "idha" for recollection, and when his pause was long, he cut the connecting alif as one beginning with it. This is like the verse of the poet:

"O self, be patient; every living thing will meet (its end), and every two will part."

﴿The last of them will say to the first of them﴾, that is, the last of them to enter says to the first of them to enter. It has been said: "the last of them" means the lowest of them and their followers, saying to "the first of them," meaning their leaders and elders. This is preferable, as His words "Our Lord, these are the ones who misled us" indicate, since the misleaders are the leaders.

It is possible that what is meant is that they misled them because they followed them and took their religion as a model after them, so the first interpretation is valid, because the last of them followed the religion of the first of them.

His words: ﴿So give them a double punishment from the Fire﴾. "Dif" (double) means an amount exceeding its equal once or several times. A similar statement is His, exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, give them double punishment and curse them with a great curse﴾. It has been said that "double" here means serpents and vipers. The clause ﴿He will say: for each is double﴾ is a resumptive clause, an answer to an implied question. The meaning: for each group among you there is a double punishment, that is, for the first group and for the last group; but you do not know what each kind of punishment entails.

39. ﴿And the first of them will say to the last of them﴾, that is, the earlier ones say to the later ones, or the followed say to the followers: ﴿So you had no superiority over us﴾. Rather, we are equal in disbelief in Allah and in deserving His punishment. ﴿So taste the punishment of the Fire for what you used to earn﴾ of the disobedience of Allah and disbelief in Him.

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Khatib, and Ibn al-Najjar have related from Abu al-Darda', who said: "We discussed the lengthening of life (ziyadat al-'umr) in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and we said: whoever keeps the ties of kinship, his term is lengthened (unsi'a fi ajalih). He said: It does not actually add to his lifespan. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿When their term comes, they cannot delay an hour, nor can they advance﴾. But a man may have righteous offspring who supplicate to Allah after him, and that reaches him; this is the one whose term is lengthened."

In another wording: "Their supplication reaches him in his grave, and that is the lengthening of his life."

This hadith should be examined for its chain of narration, for there is strangeness in it, and authentic hadiths in the two Sahihs and others have come contrary to it.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, who said: al-Hasan used to say: "How foolish these people are! They say: O Allah, prolong his life. And Allah says: ﴿When their term comes, they cannot delay an hour, nor can they advance﴾."

'Abd al-Razzaq, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn al-Mundhir related, through the route of al-Zuhri from Ibn al-Musayyab, who said: When 'Umar was stabbed, Ka'b said: "If he supplicated to Allah, He would delay his term." It was said to him: "Did not Allah say: ﴿When their term comes, they cannot delay an hour, nor can they advance﴾?" Ka'b said: "And Allah has also said: ﴿No one is granted a long life, nor is his life shortened, except that it is in a Book﴾" (Fatir: 11).

al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh related from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Those will receive their portion from the Book﴾, that he said: "What has been decreed for them of good and evil."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him regarding the verse, that he said: "Of the deeds: whoever does good is rewarded for it, and whoever does evil is rewarded for it."

Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh also related from him, that he said: "Their portion of wretchedness and happiness."

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Mujahid regarding the verse, that he said: "What has preceded from the Book."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Muhammad ibn Ka'b regarding the verse, that he said: "His provision, his term, and his deeds."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh related from Abu Salih regarding the verse, that he said: "Of the punishment."

'Abd ibn Humayd related the same from al-Hasan.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh related from al-Suddi, regarding His words "have passed away" (khalat), that he said: "have gone by." ﴿Whenever a nation enters, it curses its sister﴾, he said: "Whenever a people of a religion enters, they curse their companions for that. The polytheists curse the polytheists, the Jews the Jews, the Christians the Christians, the Sabians the Sabians, and the Magians the Magians; the later curses the earlier." ﴿Until, when they have overtaken one another therein altogether, the last of them will say﴾, those who were at the end of time, ﴿to their first, those who established that religion for them: "Our Lord, these are the ones who misled us, so give them a double punishment from the Fire." He will say: "For each is double"﴾, the first and the last. ﴿And the first of them will say to the last of them: "So you had no superiority over us," for you too went astray as we went astray.﴾

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh related from Mujahid regarding His words "a double punishment," that he said: "multiplied." And regarding "for each is double," he said: "multiplied." And regarding His words "So you had no superiority over us," he said: "a lightening of the punishment."

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on Surah 7, verses 40–42:**

His saying: ﴿They will not have the gates of heaven opened for them﴾.

Ibn ʿAbbas, Hamzah and al-Kisai recited *tuftahu* with a *yāʾ* (*bi-faṭḥi al-taḥtiyyah*), because the feminine marking of the plural (*taʾnīth al-jamʿ*) is not real (*ghayr ḥaqīqī*), so it may be made masculine.

The rest recited it with a *tāʾ* (*bi-l-fawqiyyah*), for the feminine.

Abu ʿAmr, Hamzah and al-Kisai recited *tuftaḥu* with the light form (*bi-l-takhfīf*).

The rest recited it with the doubled form (*bi-l-tashdīd*). The meaning is that the gates of heaven will not be opened for their souls when they die. What indicates this meaning, and that it is what is intended by the verse, is what has come in the authentic hadiths: that when the angels bring the soul of the disbeliever to the lowest heaven and ask for it to be opened, it is not opened for them.

It was also said: the gates of heaven will not be opened for their supplications when they call upon God. This was said by Mujahid and al-Nakhaʿi.

It was said: [it is not opened] for their deeds, i.e., they will not be accepted; rather they will be returned to them and struck in their faces with them.

It was also said: the meaning is that the gates of Paradise will not be opened for them to enter, because Paradise is in heaven. On this view, the clause ﴿nor will they enter Paradise﴾ is an explanatory coordination (*ʿaṭf al-tafsīr*).

There is no obstacle to understanding the verse as encompassing souls, supplications and deeds together. The occurrence of what has come concerning the gates of heaven not being opened for one of these does not contradict this, since that does not indicate their being opened for other things that fall under the generality of the verse.

His saying: ﴿Nor will they enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle﴾. That is: these disbelievers, who denied and were arrogant, will not enter Paradise under any circumstances. For this reason He made it contingent on something impossible, saying "until the camel passes through the eye of the needle," and it never passes through.

The camel is singled out for mention because it is used as a proverbial example of the size of a body (*kibar al-dhāt*). The "eye of the needle" (*samm al-khiyāṭ*), which is the hole of the needle, is singled out because it is the extreme of narrowness.

The *jamal* is the male of the camels; its plurals are *jimāl*, *ajmāl* and *jimālāt*. It is called *jamal* only once it has reached four years.

Ibn ʿAbbas recited *al-Jummal* with a *ḍamma* on the *jīm* and a *fatḥa* on the doubled *mīm*. It is the cable of a ship, which is called the *qals*, and it is a bundle of ropes; this was said by Thaʿlab. It was also said: it is a thick rope made of hemp (*al-qunnab*). It was also said: it is the rope by which one climbs up a palm tree.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr recited *al-Jumal* with a *ḍamma* on the *jīm* and a light *mīm*, and it is also the *qals*.

Abu al-Simak recited *al-Jumlu* with a *ḍamma* on the *jīm* and a sukun on the *mīm*. It was also read with both vowelled with *ḍamma*.

ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud recited: *ḥattā yalija al-jamalu al-aṣghar fī samm al-khiyāṭ* ("until the smaller camel passes through the eye of the needle"). And *fī samm* was read with all three vowels (*al-ḥarakāt al-thalāth*).

*Al-samm* is every fine hole, and from it is the hole of the needle. *Al-khiyāṭ* is that with which one sews; it is said *khiyāṭ* and *makhīṭ*.

His saying: ﴿Thus do We recompense the criminals﴾, that is: like that dreadful recompense, We recompense the criminals, i.e., every kind of one who commits crime. Its verification has already preceded.

*Al-mihād* is the bedding, and *al-ghawāsh* is the plural of *ghāshiyah*, i.e., fires that envelop them from above them like coverings. ﴿Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers﴾, that is: like that great recompense, We recompense whoever is characterized by the attribute of wrongdoing.

His saying: ﴿We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity﴾. That is: We do not burden the servants except with what falls within their capacity and they are able to do, and We do not burden them with what does not fall within their capacity. This sentence is parenthetical between the subject and the predicate. A similar statement is ﴿God does not burden a soul beyond what He has given it﴾ (al-Talaq: 7).

Al-Aʿmash recited *tukallafu* with the *tāʾ* (*bi-l-fawqiyyah*) and *nafsun* in the nominative. The pointer in His saying "those" (*ulāʾika*) refers to the relative pronoun (*al-mawṣūl*); its predicate is "companions of Paradise," and the clause is the predicate of the relative pronoun. The clause ﴿they will abide therein forever﴾ is in a position of accusative (*naṣb*) as a circumstantial clause (*ḥāl*).

His saying: ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts﴾. This is among the blessings that God bestows upon the people of Paradise: that God will remove what is in their hearts of resentment towards one another, so that their hearts become pure and they love one another. For if resentment remained in their breasts as it was in this world, that would be a disturbance to the bliss of Paradise, because those who bear enmity cannot enjoy life while the other is present.

*Al-ghill* is the rancour that lies hidden in the breasts. It was also said: the removal of resentment in Paradise means that they will not envy one another regarding the differences in ranks.

They said: ﴿Praise be to God, who guided us to this﴾, i.e., to this great reward, which is eternal abiding in Paradise and the removal of resentment from their breasts. This guidance to this is the guidance to its cause from faith and righteous deeds in the world. ﴿And we would not have been guided had it not been for God's guidance of us.﴾

Ibn ʿAmir recited without the *wāw* (*bi-isqāṭ al-wāw*), and the rest recited with it. The meaning: "We would not have been able to be guided to this matter had it not been for God's guidance of us." It was said: [it is not opened] for their deeds, i.e., they will not be accepted; rather they will be returned to them and struck in their faces with them.

[p. 476] The calling out by the people of Paradise to the people of the Fire was not meant to inform them of what they called out about. Rather, it was meant to rebuke them and to plant regret in their hearts. The phrase "أنْ قَدْ وجَدْنا" ("that we have found") is itself the call: that is, "We have indeed reached what Allah promised us of bliss. Have you reached what Allah promised you of the painful punishment?" The interrogative is for reproach and censure. The second object of "وعَدَ" (promised) is omitted because the promise was not specifically for them but for all people, such as the Resurrection, the Reckoning and the punishment. It was also said that it is omitted to remove the disbelievers from the rank of being addressed with honour at the promise. "قالُوا نَعَمْ" ("They say: Yes") means: we have found that what our Lord promised is true.

Al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i read "نَعِمْ" with a kasra on the ʿayn.

Makki said: whoever reads "نَعِمْ" with a kasra on the ʿayn seems to intend to distinguish the "نَعَمْ" that is an answer from the "نَعِمْ" that is a noun meaning camels, cattle and sheep.

Al-Mu'adhdhin means the caller, i.e. "فَنادى مُنادٍ بَيْنَهم" ("then a caller called out among them"), that is, between the two groups. It was said that he is one of the angels: "أنْ لَعْنَةَ اللَّهِ عَلى الظّالِمِينَ" ("that the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers"). Ibn ʿĀmir, Hamza, al-Kisa'i and al-Bazzi read "أنْ" with a shadda (intensive form), which is the original form.

The rest read it with a light pronunciation, taking it as the light form of the heavy "أنَّ" or as the explanatory particle.

Al-A'mash read "إنْ" with a kasra on the hamza, supposing an implied verb of saying.

The clause "الَّذِينَ يَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ" ("who bar from the way of Allah") is a qualifier of "الظّالِمِينَ" (the wrongdoers). It is permissible to read it in the nominative or accusative, with an implied "هم" (they) or "أعْنِي" (I mean).

Al-Sadd means prevention: they prevent people from following the path of truth, and they seek to make it crooked ("ويَبْغُونَها عِوَجًا"), i.e. they seek its crookedness. They repel people from it and disparage its straightness by saying that it is not the truth and that the truth is what they are upon. "العِوَجُ" with a kasra (ʿiwaj) applies to meanings and to things that are not upright, while with a fatḥa (ʿawaj) it applies to what is upright, such as a spear. The clause "وهم بِالآخِرَةِ كافِرُونَ" ("and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter") is in a place of accusative as a circumstantial clause.

Allah's statement: ﴿وبَيْنَهُما حِجابٌ﴾ ("and between them is a barrier"): that is, between the two groups, or between Paradise and the Fire.

The barrier ("al-Hijab") is the wall mentioned in His statement: ﴿فَضُرِبَ بَيْنَهم بِسُورٍ﴾ ("So a wall with a gate will be set up between them") (al-Hadid: 13).

Allah's statement: ﴿وعَلى الأعْرافِ رِجالٌ﴾ ("and upon the heights are men"). "Al-A'raf" (the Heights) is the plural of "ʿurf", which refers to the battlements of the wall set up between them; from it come "ʿurf al-faras" (the mane of the horse) and "ʿurf al-dik" (the comb of the rooster). In language, al-A'raf means an elevated place. This statement is in the form of praise, as in His statement: ﴿رِجالٌ لا تُلْهِيهِمْ تِجارَةٌ ولا بَيْعٌ عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ﴾ ("men whom neither commerce nor trade distracts from the remembrance of Allah") (al-Nur: 37).

The scholars differed about who the people of al-A'raf are. It was said: they are the martyrs; this was mentioned by al-Qushayri and Shuraḥbil ibn Saʿd. It was said: they are the excellent believers who have finished with the concern for themselves and have freed themselves to observe the conditions of people; this was mentioned by Mujahid. It was said: they are a people of prophets; this was mentioned by al-Zajjaj. It was said: they are a people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal; this was said by Ibn Mas'ud, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Shaʿbi, al-Dahhak and Saʿid ibn Jubayr. It was said: they are al-ʿAbbas, Hamza, ʿAli and Jaʿfar al-Tayyar, who recognise their lovers by the whiteness of their faces and their haters by the blackness of them; this is related from Ibn ʿAbbas. It was said: they are the witnesses of the Resurrection who testify against people for their deeds, and they exist in every nation; al-Nahhas chose this view. It was said: they are the sons of fornication; this is related from Ibn ʿAbbas. It was said: they are angels appointed over these walls who distinguish the disbelievers from the believers before they are admitted to Paradise or the Fire; this was mentioned by Abu Mijlaz.

The clause "يَعْرِفُونَ كُلًّا بِسِيماهم" ("they recognise each by their marks") is a qualifier of "رِجالٌ" (men).

Al-Sima means the mark: that is, they recognise each of the people of Paradise and the Fire by their signs, such as the whiteness and blackness of faces, or the traces of ablution in believers, or a sign that Allah will set for each group in that place by which the men of al-A'raf recognise the happy from the wretched.

﴿ونادَوْا أصْحابَ الجَنَّةِ﴾ ("And they call out to the companions of Paradise"): that is, the men of al-A'raf call out to the companions of Paradise when they see them, saying: ﴿أنْ سَلامٌ عَلَيْكم﴾ ("Peace be upon you"). That is, they call to them with the words "Peace be upon you" as a greeting, honour and good tidings, or they inform them of their safety from the punishment.

Allah's statement: ﴿لَمْ يَدْخُلُوها وهم يَطْمَعُونَ﴾ ("They have not entered it, though they aspire"): that is, the men of al-A'raf had not entered Paradise, while they were hoping to enter it. It was said: the meaning of "yaṭmaʿūn" is that they know they will enter it; this is known among the lexicographers, as "ṭamiʿa" can mean "ʿalima" (to know). This was mentioned by al-Nahhas.

This view, namely that they are the people of al-A'raf, is related from a group including Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Mas'ud.

Abu Mijlaz said: they are the people of Paradise. That is, the people of al-A'raf said to them: "Peace be upon you," while the people of Paradise had not entered it, and they were hoping to enter it.

Allah's statement: ﴿وإذا صُرِفَتْ أبْصارُهم تِلْقاءَ أصْحابِ النّارِ﴾ ("And when their sights are turned toward the companions of the Fire"): that is, when the sights of the people of al-A'raf are turned toward the companions of the Fire, that is, toward their direction. The original meaning of "تِلْقاءَ" is the direction of meeting, which is the direction of facing. No noun of the pattern "tifāl" with a kasra on its first letter comes except two verbal nouns: this one, and "tibyān"; all others have a fatḥa. ﴿قالُوا﴾ ("they say"): that is, the people of al-A'raf say: ﴿رَبَّنا لا تَجْعَلْنا مَعَ القَوْمِ الظّالِمِينَ﴾ ("Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people"). They ask Allah not to make them among them.

﴿ونادى أصْحابُ الأعْرافِ رِجالًا﴾ ("And the companions of al-A'raf call out to men") from the disbelievers, whom they recognise by their marks, i.e. by their signs. "قالُوا" ("they say") is a substitute for "نادى" (called out). ﴿ما أغْنى عَنْكم جَمْعُكُمْ﴾ ("What did your gathering avail you") that you used to gather for barring from the way of Allah? The interrogative is for reproach and censure. Allah's statement: ﴿وما كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ ("and what you used to be arrogant"): "مَا" here is a verbal noun, i.e. "and what your arrogance availed you."

﴿أهَؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ أقْسَمْتُمْ لا يَنالُهُمُ اللَّهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ﴾ ("Are these the ones you swore Allah would not reach with mercy?"). This is from the speech of the people of al-A'raf: that is, they said to the disbelievers, pointing to the Muslims who had gone to Paradise, this statement.

The disbelievers used to swear this oath in the world when they saw the weak Muslims, and this is a rebuke to the disbelievers and a cause of their regret.

Allah's statement: ﴿ادْخُلُوا الجَنَّةَ لا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكم ولا أنْتُمْ تَحْزَنُونَ﴾ ("Enter Paradise; no fear will be upon you, nor will you grieve"). This is the completion of the speech of the people of al-A'raf: that is, they said to the Muslims, "Enter Paradise," for fear and grief have been removed from you after entering.

Talha ibn Musarrif read "أدْخِلُوا" ("admit") with a kasra on the khāʾ.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding Allah's statement: ﴿أنْ قَدْ وجَدْنا ما وعَدَنا رَبُّنا حَقًّا﴾ ("that we have found what our Lord promised to be true"), that he said: "of bliss and honour." ﴿فَهَلْ وجَدْتُمْ ما وعَدَ رَبُّكم حَقًّا﴾ ("Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?"), he said: "of disgrace, humiliation and punishment."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn ʿUmar that the Prophet (ﷺ), when he stood at the well of Badr, recited this verse.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related from al-Suddi, regarding Allah's statement: ﴿وبَيْنَهُما حِجابٌ﴾ ("and between them is a barrier"), that he said: it is the wall, and it is al-A'raf. It was named al-A'raf because its people recognise the people.

Saʿid ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Hudhayfah that he said: al-A'raf is a wall between Paradise and the Fire.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Baʿth wa al-Nushur related from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: al-A'raf is an elevated thing.

al-Firyabi, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh related from him that he said: al-A'raf is a wall with a crest like the crest of the rooster.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related from Saʿid ibn Jubayr that he said: al-A'raf are mountains between Paradise and the Fire, so they are upon its heights, meaning upon its peaks.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn ʿAbbas that it is a hill between Paradise and the Fire, on which some people of sins are held.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Jurayj that he said: they claim it is the Sirat (the bridge).

Ibn Jarir related from Hudhayfah that he said: the companions of al-A'raf are a people who had deeds by which Allah saved them from the Fire, and they are the last to enter Paradise; they knew the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn Mas'ud that they are those whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal; they stand on the Sirat.

Ibn Jarir related from Hudhayfah something similar.

Likewise, ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Saʿid ibn Mansur, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related something similar from him.

Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn ʿAsakir related from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah something similar.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Abu Zurʿah ibn ʿAmr ibn Jarir, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the companions of al-A'raf. He said: 'They are the last of the servants to be separated between. When the Lord of the worlds has finished separating between the servants, He says: You are a people whose good deeds have brought you out of the Fire, but you have not entered Paradise; so you are my freed ones. Graze in Paradise wherever you wish.'"

Ibn Kathir said: this is a good mursal (a hadith whose chain omits the Companion).

Al-Bayhaqi in al-Baʿth related from Hudhayfah, I think he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection. The people of Paradise are commanded to go to Paradise, and the people of the Fire are commanded to go to the Fire. Then it is said to the companions of al-A'raf: What are you waiting for? They say: We are waiting for your command. So it is said to them: Your good deeds have carried you past the Fire so that you do not enter it, and your sins have stood between you and Paradise. So enter by My forgiveness and My mercy."

Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn Manīʿ, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Baʿth related from ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Muzani, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the companions of al-A'raf. He said: They are a people who were killed in the way of Allah while in disobedience to their fathers; their killing in the way of Allah prevented them from the Fire, and their disobedience to their fathers prevented them from Paradise."

Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh related with a weak chain from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, marfuʿ (traced to the Prophet), something similar.

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Baʿth related from Abu Hurayrah, marfuʿ, something similar as well.

al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah in his Musnad, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh related from ʿAbd Allah ibn Malik al-Hilali, from his father, marfuʿ, something similar.

Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn ʿAbbas, marfuʿ, something similar.

Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh related from a man of Muzaynah, marfuʿ, something similar.

Abu al-Shaykh related from Abu ʿUbaydah ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAmmar that he was asked about Allah's statement: ﴿لَمْ يَدْخُلُوها وهم يَطْمَعُونَ﴾ ("They have not entered it, though they aspire"). He said: The angels greeted them while they had not entered it and were hoping to enter it when they greeted them.

Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh related from al-Suddi, who said: The companions of al-A'raf recognise people by their marks: the people of the Fire by the blackness of their faces, and the people of Paradise by the whiteness of their faces. When they pass by a group that is being taken to Paradise, they say: "Peace be upon you." When they pass by a group that is being taken to the Fire, they say: ﴿رَبَّنا لا تَجْعَلْنا مَعَ القَوْمِ الظّالِمِينَ﴾ ("Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people").

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding ﴿ونادى أصْحابُ الأعْرافِ رِجالًا﴾ ("And the companions of al-A'raf call out to men"), that he said: "in the Fire." ﴿يَعْرِفُونَهم بِسِيماهم قالُوا ما أغْنى عَنْكم جَمْعُكم وما كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ ("They recognise them by their marks, and say: What did your gathering avail you, and your arrogance?"). Allah said to the people of arrogance: ﴿أهَؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ أقْسَمْتُمْ لا يَنالُهُمُ اللَّهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ﴾ ("Are these the ones you swore Allah would not reach with mercy?"), meaning the companions of al-A'raf. ﴿ادْخُلُوا الجَنَّةَ لا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكم ولا أنْتُمْ تَحْزَنُونَ﴾ ("Enter Paradise; no fear will be upon you, nor will you grieve").

Allah's statement: ﴿ادْخُلُوا الجَنَّةَ لا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكم ولا أنْتُمْ تَحْزَنُونَ﴾ ("Enter Paradise; no fear will be upon you, nor will you grieve"). This is the completion of the speech of the people of al-A'raf: that is, they said to the Muslims, "Enter Paradise," for fear and grief have been removed from you after entering.

Talha ibn Musarrif read "أدْخِلُوا" ("admit") with a kasra on the khāʾ.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding Allah's statement: ﴿أنْ قَدْ وجَدْنا ما وعَدَنا رَبُّنا حَقًّا﴾ ("that we have found what our Lord promised to be true"), that he said: "of bliss and honour." ﴿فَهَلْ وجَدْتُمْ ما وعَدَ رَبُّكم حَقًّا﴾ ("Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?"), he said: "of disgrace, humiliation and punishment."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn ʿUmar that the Prophet (ﷺ), when he stood at the well of Badr, recited this verse.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related from al-Suddi, regarding Allah's statement: ﴿وبَيْنَهُما حِجابٌ﴾ ("and between them is a barrier"), that he said: it is the wall, and it is al-A'raf. It was named al-A'raf because its people recognise the people.

Saʿid ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Hudhayfah that he said: al-A'raf is a wall between Paradise and the Fire.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Baʿth wa al-Nushur related from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: al-A'raf is an elevated thing.

al-Firyabi, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh related from him that he said: al-A'raf is a wall with a crest like the crest of the rooster.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related from Saʿid ibn Jubayr that he said: al-A'raf are mountains between Paradise and the Fire, so they are upon its heights, meaning upon its peaks.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn ʿAbbas that it is a hill between Paradise and the Fire, on which some people of sins are held.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Jurayj that he said: they claim it is the Sirat (the bridge).

Ibn Jarir related from Hudhayfah that he said: the companions of al-A'raf are a people who had deeds by which Allah saved them from the Fire, and they are the last to enter Paradise; they knew the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn Mas'ud that they are those whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal; they stand on the Sirat.

Ibn Jarir related from Hudhayfah something similar.

Likewise, ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Saʿid ibn Mansur, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related something similar from him.

Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn ʿAsakir related from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah something similar.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Abu Zurʿah ibn ʿAmr ibn Jarir, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the companions of al-A'raf. He said: 'They are the last of the servants to be separated between. When the Lord of the worlds has finished separating between the servants, He says: You are a people whose good deeds have brought you out of the Fire, but you have not entered Paradise; so you are my freed ones. Graze in Paradise wherever you wish.'"

Ibn Kathir said: this is a good mursal (a hadith whose chain omits the Companion).

Al-Bayhaqi in al-Baʿth related from Hudhayfah, I think he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection. The people of Paradise are commanded to go to Paradise, and the people of the Fire are commanded to go to the Fire. Then it is said to the companions of al-A'raf: What are you waiting for? They say: We are waiting for your command. So it is said to them: Your good deeds have carried you past the Fire so that you do not enter it, and your sins have stood between you and Paradise. So enter by My forgiveness and My mercy."

Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn Manīʿ, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Baʿth related from ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Muzani, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the companions of al-A'raf. He said: They are a people who were killed in the way of Allah while in disobedience to their fathers; their killing in the way of Allah prevented them from the Fire, and their disobedience to their fathers prevented them from Paradise."

Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh related with a weak chain from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, marfuʿ (traced to the Prophet), something similar.

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Baʿth related from Abu Hurayrah, marfuʿ, something similar as well.

al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah in his Musnad, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh related from ʿAbd Allah ibn Malik al-Hilali, from his father, marfuʿ, something similar.

Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn ʿAbbas, marfuʿ, something similar.

Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh related from a man of Muzaynah, marfuʿ, something similar.

Abu al-Shaykh related from Abu ʿUbaydah ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAmmar that he was asked about Allah's statement: ﴿لَمْ يَدْخُلُوها وهم يَطْمَعُونَ﴾ ("They have not entered it, though they aspire"). He said: The angels greeted them while they had not entered it and were hoping to enter it when they greeted them.

Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh related from al-Suddi, who said: The companions of al-A'raf recognise people by their marks: the people of the Fire by the blackness of their faces, and the people of Paradise by the whiteness of their faces. When they pass by a group that is being taken to Paradise, they say: "Peace be upon you." When they pass by a group that is being taken to the Fire, they say: ﴿رَبَّنا لا تَجْعَلْنا مَعَ القَوْمِ الظّالِمِينَ﴾ ("Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people").

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding ﴿ونادى أصْحابُ الأعْرافِ رِجالًا﴾ ("And the companions of al-A'raf call out to men"), that he said: "in the Fire." ﴿يَعْرِفُونَهم بِسِيماهم قالُوا ما أغْنى عَنْكم جَمْعُكم وما كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ ("They recognise them by their marks, and say: What did your gathering avail you, and your arrogance?"). Allah said to the people of arrogance: ﴿أهَؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ أقْسَمْتُمْ لا يَنالُهُمُ اللَّهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ﴾ ("Are these the ones you swore Allah would not reach with mercy?"), meaning the companions of al-A'raf. ﴿ادْخُلُوا الجَنَّةَ لا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكم ولا أنْتُمْ تَحْزَنُونَ﴾ ("Enter Paradise; no fear will be upon you, nor will you grieve").

[p. 476] The calling out by the people of Paradise to the people of the Fire was not meant to inform them of what they called out about. Rather, it was meant to rebuke them and to plant regret in their hearts. The phrase "أنْ قَدْ وجَدْنا" ("that we have found") is itself the call: that is, "We have indeed reached what Allah promised us of bliss. Have you reached what Allah promised you of the painful punishment?" The interrogative is for reproach and censure. The second object of "وعَدَ" (promised) is omitted because the promise was not specifically for them but for all people, such as the Resurrection, the Reckoning and the punishment. It was also said that it is omitted to remove the disbelievers from the rank of being addressed with honour at the promise. "قالُوا نَعَمْ" ("They say: Yes") means: we have found that what our Lord promised is true.

Al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i read "نَعِمْ" with a kasra on the ʿayn.

Makki said: whoever reads "نَعِمْ" with a kasra on the ʿayn seems to intend to distinguish the "نَعَمْ" that is an answer from the "نَعِمْ" that is a noun meaning camels, cattle and sheep.

Al-Mu'adhdhin means the caller, i.e. "فَنادى مُنادٍ بَيْنَهم" ("then a caller called out among them"), that is, between the two groups. It was said that he is one of the angels: "أنْ لَعْنَةَ اللَّهِ عَلى الظّالِمِينَ" ("that the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers"). Ibn ʿĀmir, Hamza, al-Kisa'i and al-Bazzi read "أنْ" with a shadda (intensive form), which is the original form.

The rest read it with a light pronunciation, taking it as the light form of the heavy "أنَّ" or as the explanatory particle.

Al-A'mash read "إنْ" with a kasra on the hamza, supposing an implied verb of saying.

The clause "الَّذِينَ يَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ" ("who bar from the way of Allah") is a qualifier of "الظّالِمِينَ" (the wrongdoers). It is permissible to read it in the nominative or accusative, with an implied "هم" (they) or "أعْنِي" (I mean).

Al-Sadd means prevention: they prevent people from following the path of truth, and they seek to make it crooked ("ويَبْغُونَها عِوَجًا"), i.e. they seek its crookedness. They repel people from it and disparage its straightness by saying that it is not the truth and that the truth is what they are upon. "العِوَجُ" with a kasra (ʿiwaj) applies to meanings and to things that are not upright, while with a fatḥa (ʿawaj) it applies to what is upright, such as a spear. The clause "وهم بِالآخِرَةِ كافِرُونَ" ("and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter") is in a place of accusative as a circumstantial clause.

Allah's statement: ﴿وبَيْنَهُما حِجابٌ﴾ ("and between them is a barrier"): that is, between the two groups, or between Paradise and the Fire.

The barrier ("al-Hijab") is the wall mentioned in His statement: ﴿فَضُرِبَ بَيْنَهم بِسُورٍ﴾ ("So a wall with a gate will be set up between them") (al-Hadid: 13).

Allah's statement: ﴿وعَلى الأعْرافِ رِجالٌ﴾ ("and upon the heights are men"). "Al-A'raf" (the Heights) is the plural of "ʿurf", which refers to the battlements of the wall set up between them; from it come "ʿurf al-faras" (the mane of the horse) and "ʿurf al-dik" (the comb of the rooster). In language, al-A'raf means an elevated place. This statement is in the form of praise, as in His statement: ﴿رِجالٌ لا تُلْهِيهِمْ تِجارَةٌ ولا بَيْعٌ عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ﴾ ("men whom neither commerce nor trade distracts from the remembrance of Allah") (al-Nur: 37).

The scholars differed about who the people of al-A'raf are. It was said: they are the martyrs; this was mentioned by al-Qushayri and Shuraḥbil ibn Saʿd. It was said: they are the excellent believers who have finished with the concern for themselves and have freed themselves to observe the conditions of people; this was mentioned by Mujahid. It was said: they are a people of prophets; this was mentioned by al-Zajjaj. It was said: they are a people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal; this was said by Ibn Mas'ud, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Shaʿbi, al-Dahhak and Saʿid ibn Jubayr. It was said: they are al-ʿAbbas, Hamza, ʿAli and Jaʿfar al-Tayyar, who recognise their lovers by the whiteness of their faces and their haters by the blackness of them; this is related from Ibn ʿAbbas. It was said: they are the witnesses of the Resurrection who testify against people for their deeds, and they exist in every nation; al-Nahhas chose this view. It was said: they are the sons of fornication; this is related from Ibn ʿAbbas. It was said: they are angels appointed over these walls who distinguish the disbelievers from the believers before they are admitted to Paradise or the Fire; this was mentioned by Abu Mijlaz.

The clause "يَعْرِفُونَ كُلًّا بِسِيماهم" ("they recognise each by their marks") is a qualifier of "رِجالٌ" (men).

Al-Sima means the mark: that is, they recognise each of the people of Paradise and the Fire by their signs, such as the whiteness and blackness of faces, or the traces of ablution in believers, or a sign that Allah will set for each group in that place by which the men of al-A'raf recognise the happy from the wretched.

﴿ونادَوْا أصْحابَ الجَنَّةِ﴾ ("And they call out to the companions of Paradise"): that is, the men of al-A'raf call out to the companions of Paradise when they see them, saying: ﴿أنْ سَلامٌ عَلَيْكم﴾ ("Peace be upon you"). That is, they call to them with the words "Peace be upon you" as a greeting, honour and good tidings, or they inform them of their safety from the punishment.

Allah's statement: ﴿لَمْ يَدْخُلُوها وهم يَطْمَعُونَ﴾ ("They have not entered it, though they aspire"): that is, the men of al-A'raf had not entered Paradise, while they were hoping to enter it. It was said: the meaning of "yaṭmaʿūn" is that they know they will enter it; this is known among the lexicographers, as "ṭamiʿa" can mean "ʿalima" (to know). This was mentioned by al-Nahhas.

This view, namely that they are the people of al-A'raf, is related from a group including Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Mas'ud.

Abu Mijlaz said: they are the people of Paradise. That is, the people of al-A'raf said to them: "Peace be upon you," while the people of Paradise had not entered it, and they were hoping to enter it.

Allah's statement: ﴿وإذا صُرِفَتْ أبْصارُهم تِلْقاءَ أصْحابِ النّارِ﴾ ("And when their sights are turned toward the companions of the Fire"): that is, when the sights of the people of al-A'raf are turned toward the companions of the Fire, that is, toward their direction. The original meaning of "تِلْقاءَ" is the direction of meeting, which is the direction of facing. No noun of the pattern "tifāl" with a kasra on its first letter comes except two verbal nouns: this one, and "tibyān"; all others have a fatḥa. ﴿قالُوا﴾ ("they say"): that is, the people of al-A'raf say: ﴿رَبَّنا لا تَجْعَلْنا مَعَ القَوْمِ الظّالِمِينَ﴾ ("Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people"). They ask Allah not to make them among them.

﴿ونادى أصْحابُ الأعْرافِ رِجالًا﴾ ("And the companions of al-A'raf call out to men") from the disbelievers, whom they recognise by their marks, i.e. by their signs. "قالُوا" ("they say") is a substitute for "نادى" (called out). ﴿ما أغْنى عَنْكم جَمْعُكُمْ﴾ ("What did your gathering avail you") that you used to gather for barring from the way of Allah? The interrogative is for reproach and censure. Allah's statement: ﴿وما كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ ("and what you used to be arrogant"): "مَا" here is a verbal noun, i.e. "and what your arrogance availed you."

﴿أهَؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ أقْسَمْتُمْ لا يَنالُهُمُ اللَّهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ﴾ ("Are these the ones you swore Allah would not reach with mercy?"). This is from the speech of the people of al-A'raf: that is, they said to the disbelievers, pointing to the Muslims who had gone to Paradise, this statement.

This is the completion of the speech of the people of al-A'raf: that is, they said to the Muslims, "Enter Paradise," for fear and grief have been removed from you after entering.

Al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i read "نَعِمْ" with a kasra on the ʿayn.

Makki said: whoever reads "نَعِمْ" with a kasra on the ʿayn seems to intend to distinguish the "نَعَمْ" that is an answer from the "نَعِمْ" that is a noun meaning camels, cattle and sheep.

Al-Sadd means prevention: they prevent people from following the path of truth, and they seek to make it crooked ("ويَبْغُونَها عِوَجًا"), i.e. they seek its crookedness. They repel people from it and disparage its straightness by saying that it is not the truth and that the truth is what they are upon. "العِوَجُ" with a kasra (ʿiwaj) applies to meanings and to things that are not upright, while with a fatḥa (ʿawaj) it applies to what is upright, such as a spear. The clause "وهم بِالآخِرَةِ كافِرُونَ" ("and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter") is in a place of accusative as a circumstantial clause.

Allah's statement: ﴿وبَيْنَهُما حِجابٌ﴾ ("and between them is a barrier"): that is, between the two groups, or between Paradise and the Fire.

The barrier ("al-Hijab") is the wall mentioned in His statement: ﴿فَضُرِبَ بَيْنَهم بِسُورٍ﴾ ("So a wall with a gate will be set up between them") (al-Hadid: 13).

Allah's statement: ﴿وعَلى الأعْرافِ رِجالٌ﴾ ("and upon the heights are men"). "Al-A'raf" (the Heights) is the plural of "ʿurf", which refers to the battlements of the wall set up between them; from it come "ʿurf al-faras" (the mane of the horse) and "ʿurf al-dik" (the comb of the rooster). In language, al-A'raf means an elevated place. This statement is in the form of praise, as in His statement: ﴿رِجالٌ لا تُلْهِيهِمْ تِجارَةٌ ولا بَيْعٌ عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ﴾ ("men whom neither commerce nor trade distracts from the remembrance of Allah") (al-Nur: 37).

It was said: they are the excellent believers who have finished with the concern for themselves and have freed themselves to observe the conditions of people; this was mentioned by Mujahid. It was said: they are a people of prophets; this was mentioned by al-Zajjaj. It was said: they are a people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal; this was said by Ibn Mas'ud, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Shaʿbi, al-Dahhak and Saʿid ibn Jubayr. It was said: they are al-ʿAbbas, Hamza, ʿAli and Jaʿfar al-Tayyar, who recognise their lovers by the whiteness of their faces and their haters by the blackness of them; this is related from Ibn ʿAbbas. It was said: they are the witnesses of the Resurrection who testify against people for their deeds, and they exist in every nation; al-Nahhas chose this view. It was said: they are the sons of fornication; this is related from Ibn ʿAbbas. It was said: they are angels appointed over these walls who distinguish the disbelievers from the believers before they are admitted to Paradise or the Fire; this was mentioned by Abu Mijlaz.

Al-Sima means the mark: that is, they recognise each of the people of Paradise and the Fire by their signs, such as the whiteness and blackness of faces, or the traces of ablution in believers, or a sign that Allah will set for each group in that place by which the men of al-A'raf recognise the happy from the wretched.

﴿ونادَوْا أصْحابَ الجَنَّةِ﴾ ("And they call out to the companions of Paradise"): that is, the men of al-A'raf call out to the companions of Paradise when they see them, saying: ﴿أنْ سَلامٌ عَلَيْكم﴾ ("Peace be upon you"). That is, they call to them with the words "Peace be upon you" as a greeting, honour and good tidings, or they inform them of their safety from the punishment.

Allah's statement: ﴿لَمْ يَدْخُلُوها وهم يَطْمَعُونَ﴾ ("They have not entered it, though they aspire"): that is, the men of al-A'raf had not entered Paradise, while they were hoping to enter it. It was said: the meaning of "yaṭmaʿūn" is that they know they will enter it; this is known among the lexicographers, as "ṭamiʿa" can mean "ʿalima" (to know). This was mentioned by al-Nahhas.

This view, namely that they are the people of al-A'raf, is related from a group including Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Mas'ud.

Abu Mijlaz said: they are the people of Paradise. That is, the people of al-A'raf said to them: "Peace be upon you," while the people of Paradise had not entered it, and they were hoping to enter it.

The original meaning of "تِلْقاءَ" is the direction of meeting, which is the direction of facing. No noun of the pattern "tifāl" with a kasra on its first letter comes except two verbal nouns: this one, and "tibyān"; all others have a fatḥa. ﴿قالُوا﴾ ("they say"): that is, the people of al-A'raf say: ﴿رَبَّنا لا تَجْعَلْنا مَعَ القَوْمِ الظّالِمِينَ﴾ ("Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people"). They ask Allah not to make them among them.

﴿ونادى أصْحابُ الأعْرافِ رِجالًا﴾ ("And the companions of al-A'raf call out to men") from the disbelievers, whom they recognise by their marks, i.e. by their signs. The interrogative is for reproach and censure. Allah's statement: ﴿وما كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ ("and what you used to be arrogant"): "مَا" here is a verbal noun, i.e. "and what your arrogance availed you."

﴿أهَؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ أقْسَمْتُمْ لا يَنالُهُمُ اللَّهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ﴾ ("Are these the ones you swore Allah would not reach with mercy?"). This is from the speech of the people of al-A'raf: that is, they said to the disbelievers, pointing to the Muslims who had gone to Paradise, this statement.

The disbelievers used to swear this oath in the world when they saw the weak Muslims, and this is a rebuke to the disbelievers and a cause of their regret.

Allah's statement: ﴿ادْخُلُوا الجَنَّةَ لا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكم ولا أنْتُمْ تَحْزَنُونَ﴾ ("Enter Paradise; no fear will be upon you, nor will you grieve"). This is the completion of the speech of the people of al-A'raf: that is, they said to the Muslims, "Enter Paradise," for fear and grief have been removed from you after entering.

Talha ibn Musarrif read "أدْخِلُوا" ("admit") with a kasra on the khāʾ.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn ʿUmar that the Prophet (ﷺ), when he stood at the well of Badr, recited this verse.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related from al-Suddi, regarding Allah's statement: ﴿وبَيْنَهُما حِجابٌ﴾ ("and between them is a barrier"), that he said: it is the wall, and it is al-A'raf. It was named al-A'raf because its people recognise the people.

Saʿid ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Hudhayfah that he said: al-A'raf is a wall between Paradise and the Fire.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Baʿth wa al-Nushur related from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: al-A'raf is an elevated thing.

al-Firyabi, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh related from him that he said: al-A'raf is a wall with a crest like the crest of the rooster.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related from Saʿid ibn Jubayr that he said: al-A'raf are mountains between Paradise and the Fire, so they are upon its heights, meaning upon its peaks.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn ʿAbbas that it is a hill between Paradise and the Fire, on which some people of sins are held.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Jurayj that he said: they claim it is the Sirat (the bridge).

Ibn Jarir related from Hudhayfah that he said: the companions of al-A'raf are a people who had deeds by which Allah saved them from the Fire, and they are the last to enter Paradise; they knew the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn Mas'ud that they are those whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal; they stand on the Sirat.

Ibn Jarir related from Hudhayfah something similar.

Likewise, ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Saʿid ibn Mansur, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related something similar from him.

Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn ʿAsakir related from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah something similar.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Abu Zurʿah ibn ʿAmr ibn Jarir, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the companions of al-A'raf. He said: 'They are the last of the servants to be separated between. When the Lord of the worlds has finished separating between the servants, He says: You are a people whose good deeds have brought you out of the Fire, but you have not entered Paradise; so you are my freed ones. Graze in Paradise wherever you wish.'"

Ibn Kathir said: this is a good mursal (a hadith whose chain omits the Companion).

Al-Bayhaqi in al-Baʿth related from Hudhayfah, I think he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection. The people of Paradise are commanded to go to Paradise, and the people of the Fire are commanded to go to the Fire. Then it is said to the companions of al-A'raf: What are you waiting for? They say: We are waiting for your command. So it is said to them: Your good deeds have carried you past the Fire so that you do not enter it, and your sins have stood between you and Paradise. So enter by My forgiveness and My mercy."

Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn Manīʿ, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Baʿth related from ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Muzani, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the companions of al-A'raf. He said: They are a people who were killed in the way of Allah while in disobedience to their fathers; their killing in the way of Allah prevented them from the Fire, and their disobedience to their fathers prevented them from Paradise."

Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh related with a weak chain from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, marfuʿ (traced to the Prophet), something similar.

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Baʿth related from Abu Hurayrah, marfuʿ, something similar as well.

al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah in his Musnad, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh related from ʿAbd Allah ibn Malik al-Hilali, from his father, marfuʿ, something similar.

Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn ʿAbbas, marfuʿ, something similar.

Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh related from a man of Muzaynah, marfuʿ, something similar.

He said: The angels greeted them while they had not entered it and were hoping to enter it when they greeted them.

When they pass by a group that is being taken to Paradise, they say: "Peace be upon you." When they pass by a group that is being taken to the Fire, they say: ﴿رَبَّنا لا تَجْعَلْنا مَعَ القَوْمِ الظّالِمِينَ﴾ ("Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people").

Allah said to the people of arrogance: ﴿أهَؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ أقْسَمْتُمْ لا يَنالُهُمُ اللَّهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ﴾ ("Are these the ones you swore Allah would not reach with mercy?"), meaning the companions of al-A'raf. ﴿ادْخُلُوا الجَنَّةَ لا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكم ولا أنْتُمْ تَحْزَنُونَ﴾ ("Enter Paradise; no fear will be upon you, nor will you grieve").
