This is the completion of the speech of the people of al-A'raf: that is, they said to the Muslims, "Enter Paradise," for fear and grief have been removed from you after entering.

Talha ibn Musarrif read "أدْخِلُوا" ("admit") with a kasra on the khāʾ.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding Allah's statement: ﴿أنْ قَدْ وجَدْنا ما وعَدَنا رَبُّنا حَقًّا﴾ ("that we have found what our Lord promised to be true"), that he said: "of bliss and honour." ﴿فَهَلْ وجَدْتُمْ ما وعَدَ رَبُّكم حَقًّا﴾ ("Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?"), he said: "of disgrace, humiliation and punishment."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn ʿUmar that the Prophet (ﷺ), when he stood at the well of Badr, recited this verse.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related from al-Suddi, regarding Allah's statement: ﴿وبَيْنَهُما حِجابٌ﴾ ("and between them is a barrier"), that he said: it is the wall, and it is al-A'raf. It was named al-A'raf because its people recognise the people.

Saʿid ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Hudhayfah that he said: al-A'raf is a wall between Paradise and the Fire.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Baʿth wa al-Nushur related from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: al-A'raf is an elevated thing.

al-Firyabi, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh related from him that he said: al-A'raf is a wall with a crest like the crest of the rooster.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related from Saʿid ibn Jubayr that he said: al-A'raf are mountains between Paradise and the Fire, so they are upon its heights, meaning upon its peaks.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn ʿAbbas that it is a hill between Paradise and the Fire, on which some people of sins are held.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Jurayj that he said: they claim it is the Sirat (the bridge).

Ibn Jarir related from Hudhayfah that he said: the companions of al-A'raf are a people who had deeds by which Allah saved them from the Fire, and they are the last to enter Paradise; they knew the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn Mas'ud that they are those whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal; they stand on the Sirat.

Ibn Jarir related from Hudhayfah something similar.

Likewise, ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Saʿid ibn Mansur, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related something similar from him.

Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn ʿAsakir related from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah something similar.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Abu Zurʿah ibn ʿAmr ibn Jarir, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the companions of al-A'raf. He said: 'They are the last of the servants to be separated between. When the Lord of the worlds has finished separating between the servants, He says: You are a people whose good deeds have brought you out of the Fire, but you have not entered Paradise; so you are my freed ones. Graze in Paradise wherever you wish.'"

Ibn Kathir said: this is a good mursal (a hadith whose chain omits the Companion).

Al-Bayhaqi in al-Baʿth related from Hudhayfah, I think he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection. The people of Paradise are commanded to go to Paradise, and the people of the Fire are commanded to go to the Fire. Then it is said to the companions of al-A'raf: What are you waiting for? They say: We are waiting for your command. So it is said to them: Your good deeds have carried you past the Fire so that you do not enter it, and your sins have stood between you and Paradise. So enter by My forgiveness and My mercy."

Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn Manīʿ, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Baʿth related from ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Muzani, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the companions of al-A'raf. He said: They are a people who were killed in the way of Allah while in disobedience to their fathers; their killing in the way of Allah prevented them from the Fire, and their disobedience to their fathers prevented them from Paradise."

Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh related with a weak chain from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, marfuʿ (traced to the Prophet), something similar.

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Baʿth related from Abu Hurayrah, marfuʿ, something similar as well.

al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah in his Musnad, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh related from ʿAbd Allah ibn Malik al-Hilali, from his father, marfuʿ, something similar.

Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn ʿAbbas, marfuʿ, something similar.

Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh related from a man of Muzaynah, marfuʿ, something similar.

Abu al-Shaykh related from Abu ʿUbaydah ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAmmar that he was asked about Allah's statement: ﴿لَمْ يَدْخُلُوها وهم يَطْمَعُونَ﴾ ("They have not entered it, though they aspire"). He said: The angels greeted them while they had not entered it and were hoping to enter it when they greeted them.

Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh related from al-Suddi, who said: The companions of al-A'raf recognise people by their marks: the people of the Fire by the blackness of their faces, and the people of Paradise by the whiteness of their faces. When they pass by a group that is being taken to Paradise, they say: "Peace be upon you." When they pass by a group that is being taken to the Fire, they say: ﴿رَبَّنا لا تَجْعَلْنا مَعَ القَوْمِ الظّالِمِينَ﴾ ("Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people").

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding ﴿ونادى أصْحابُ الأعْرافِ رِجالًا﴾ ("And the companions of al-A'raf call out to men"), that he said: "in the Fire." ﴿يَعْرِفُونَهم بِسِيماهم قالُوا ما أغْنى عَنْكم جَمْعُكم وما كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ ("They recognise them by their marks, and say: What did your gathering avail you, and your arrogance?"). Allah said to the people of arrogance: ﴿أهَؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ أقْسَمْتُمْ لا يَنالُهُمُ اللَّهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ﴾ ("Are these the ones you swore Allah would not reach with mercy?"), meaning the companions of al-A'raf. ﴿ادْخُلُوا الجَنَّةَ لا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكم ولا أنْتُمْ تَحْزَنُونَ﴾ ("Enter Paradise; no fear will be upon you, nor will you grieve").

[p. 476] The calling out by the people of Paradise to the people of the Fire was not meant to inform them of what they called out about. Rather, it was meant to rebuke them and to plant regret in their hearts. The phrase "أنْ قَدْ وجَدْنا" ("that we have found") is itself the call: that is, "We have indeed reached what Allah promised us of bliss. Have you reached what Allah promised you of the painful punishment?" The interrogative is for reproach and censure. The second object of "وعَدَ" (promised) is omitted because the promise was not specifically for them but for all people, such as the Resurrection, the Reckoning and the punishment. It was also said that it is omitted to remove the disbelievers from the rank of being addressed with honour at the promise. "قالُوا نَعَمْ" ("They say: Yes") means: we have found that what our Lord promised is true.

Al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i read "نَعِمْ" with a kasra on the ʿayn.

Makki said: whoever reads "نَعِمْ" with a kasra on the ʿayn seems to intend to distinguish the "نَعَمْ" that is an answer from the "نَعِمْ" that is a noun meaning camels, cattle and sheep.

Al-Mu'adhdhin means the caller, i.e. "فَنادى مُنادٍ بَيْنَهم" ("then a caller called out among them"), that is, between the two groups. It was said that he is one of the angels: "أنْ لَعْنَةَ اللَّهِ عَلى الظّالِمِينَ" ("that the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers"). Ibn ʿĀmir, Hamza, al-Kisa'i and al-Bazzi read "أنْ" with a shadda (intensive form), which is the original form.

The rest read it with a light pronunciation, taking it as the light form of the heavy "أنَّ" or as the explanatory particle.

Al-A'mash read "إنْ" with a kasra on the hamza, supposing an implied verb of saying.

The clause "الَّذِينَ يَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ" ("who bar from the way of Allah") is a qualifier of "الظّالِمِينَ" (the wrongdoers). It is permissible to read it in the nominative or accusative, with an implied "هم" (they) or "أعْنِي" (I mean).

Al-Sadd means prevention: they prevent people from following the path of truth, and they seek to make it crooked ("ويَبْغُونَها عِوَجًا"), i.e. they seek its crookedness. They repel people from it and disparage its straightness by saying that it is not the truth and that the truth is what they are upon. "العِوَجُ" with a kasra (ʿiwaj) applies to meanings and to things that are not upright, while with a fatḥa (ʿawaj) it applies to what is upright, such as a spear. The clause "وهم بِالآخِرَةِ كافِرُونَ" ("and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter") is in a place of accusative as a circumstantial clause.

Allah's statement: ﴿وبَيْنَهُما حِجابٌ﴾ ("and between them is a barrier"): that is, between the two groups, or between Paradise and the Fire.

The barrier ("al-Hijab") is the wall mentioned in His statement: ﴿فَضُرِبَ بَيْنَهم بِسُورٍ﴾ ("So a wall with a gate will be set up between them") (al-Hadid: 13).

Allah's statement: ﴿وعَلى الأعْرافِ رِجالٌ﴾ ("and upon the heights are men"). "Al-A'raf" (the Heights) is the plural of "ʿurf", which refers to the battlements of the wall set up between them; from it come "ʿurf al-faras" (the mane of the horse) and "ʿurf al-dik" (the comb of the rooster). In language, al-A'raf means an elevated place. This statement is in the form of praise, as in His statement: ﴿رِجالٌ لا تُلْهِيهِمْ تِجارَةٌ ولا بَيْعٌ عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ﴾ ("men whom neither commerce nor trade distracts from the remembrance of Allah") (al-Nur: 37).

The scholars differed about who the people of al-A'raf are. It was said: they are the martyrs; this was mentioned by al-Qushayri and Shuraḥbil ibn Saʿd. It was said: they are the excellent believers who have finished with the concern for themselves and have freed themselves to observe the conditions of people; this was mentioned by Mujahid. It was said: they are a people of prophets; this was mentioned by al-Zajjaj. It was said: they are a people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal; this was said by Ibn Mas'ud, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Shaʿbi, al-Dahhak and Saʿid ibn Jubayr. It was said: they are al-ʿAbbas, Hamza, ʿAli and Jaʿfar al-Tayyar, who recognise their lovers by the whiteness of their faces and their haters by the blackness of them; this is related from Ibn ʿAbbas. It was said: they are the witnesses of the Resurrection who testify against people for their deeds, and they exist in every nation; al-Nahhas chose this view. It was said: they are the sons of fornication; this is related from Ibn ʿAbbas. It was said: they are angels appointed over these walls who distinguish the disbelievers from the believers before they are admitted to Paradise or the Fire; this was mentioned by Abu Mijlaz.

The clause "يَعْرِفُونَ كُلًّا بِسِيماهم" ("they recognise each by their marks") is a qualifier of "رِجالٌ" (men).

Al-Sima means the mark: that is, they recognise each of the people of Paradise and the Fire by their signs, such as the whiteness and blackness of faces, or the traces of ablution in believers, or a sign that Allah will set for each group in that place by which the men of al-A'raf recognise the happy from the wretched.

﴿ونادَوْا أصْحابَ الجَنَّةِ﴾ ("And they call out to the companions of Paradise"): that is, the men of al-A'raf call out to the companions of Paradise when they see them, saying: ﴿أنْ سَلامٌ عَلَيْكم﴾ ("Peace be upon you"). That is, they call to them with the words "Peace be upon you" as a greeting, honour and good tidings, or they inform them of their safety from the punishment.

Allah's statement: ﴿لَمْ يَدْخُلُوها وهم يَطْمَعُونَ﴾ ("They have not entered it, though they aspire"): that is, the men of al-A'raf had not entered Paradise, while they were hoping to enter it. It was said: the meaning of "yaṭmaʿūn" is that they know they will enter it; this is known among the lexicographers, as "ṭamiʿa" can mean "ʿalima" (to know). This was mentioned by al-Nahhas.

This view, namely that they are the people of al-A'raf, is related from a group including Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Mas'ud.

Abu Mijlaz said: they are the people of Paradise. That is, the people of al-A'raf said to them: "Peace be upon you," while the people of Paradise had not entered it, and they were hoping to enter it.

Allah's statement: ﴿وإذا صُرِفَتْ أبْصارُهم تِلْقاءَ أصْحابِ النّارِ﴾ ("And when their sights are turned toward the companions of the Fire"): that is, when the sights of the people of al-A'raf are turned toward the companions of the Fire, that is, toward their direction. The original meaning of "تِلْقاءَ" is the direction of meeting, which is the direction of facing. No noun of the pattern "tifāl" with a kasra on its first letter comes except two verbal nouns: this one, and "tibyān"; all others have a fatḥa. ﴿قالُوا﴾ ("they say"): that is, the people of al-A'raf say: ﴿رَبَّنا لا تَجْعَلْنا مَعَ القَوْمِ الظّالِمِينَ﴾ ("Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people"). They ask Allah not to make them among them.

﴿ونادى أصْحابُ الأعْرافِ رِجالًا﴾ ("And the companions of al-A'raf call out to men") from the disbelievers, whom they recognise by their marks, i.e. by their signs. "قالُوا" ("they say") is a substitute for "نادى" (called out). ﴿ما أغْنى عَنْكم جَمْعُكُمْ﴾ ("What did your gathering avail you") that you used to gather for barring from the way of Allah? The interrogative is for reproach and censure. Allah's statement: ﴿وما كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ ("and what you used to be arrogant"): "مَا" here is a verbal noun, i.e. "and what your arrogance availed you."

﴿أهَؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ أقْسَمْتُمْ لا يَنالُهُمُ اللَّهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ﴾ ("Are these the ones you swore Allah would not reach with mercy?"). This is from the speech of the people of al-A'raf: that is, they said to the disbelievers, pointing to the Muslims who had gone to Paradise, this statement.

The disbelievers used to swear this oath in the world when they saw the weak Muslims, and this is a rebuke to the disbelievers and a cause of their regret.

This is the completion of the speech of the people of al-A'raf: that is, they said to the Muslims, "Enter Paradise," for fear and grief have been removed from you after entering.

Al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i read "نَعِمْ" with a kasra on the ʿayn.

Makki said: whoever reads "نَعِمْ" with a kasra on the ʿayn seems to intend to distinguish the "نَعَمْ" that is an answer from the "نَعِمْ" that is a noun meaning camels, cattle and sheep.

Al-Mu'adhdhin means the caller, i.e. "فَنادى مُنادٍ بَيْنَهم" ("then a caller called out among them"), that is, between the two groups. It was said that he is one of the angels: "أنْ لَعْنَةَ اللَّهِ عَلى الظّالِمِينَ" ("that the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers"). Ibn ʿĀmir, Hamza, al-Kisa'i and al-Bazzi read "أنْ" with a shadda (intensive form), which is the original form.

The rest read it with a light pronunciation, taking it as the light form of the heavy "أنَّ" or as the explanatory particle.

Al-A'mash read "إنْ" with a kasra on the hamza, supposing an implied verb of saying.

The clause "الَّذِينَ يَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ" ("who bar from the way of Allah") is a qualifier of "الظّالِمِينَ" (the wrongdoers). It is permissible to read it in the nominative or accusative, with an implied "هم" (they) or "أعْنِي" (I mean).

Al-Sadd means prevention: they prevent people from following the path of truth, and they seek to make it crooked ("ويَبْغُونَها عِوَجًا"), i.e. they seek its crookedness. They repel people from it and disparage its straightness by saying that it is not the truth and that the truth is what they are upon. "العِوَجُ" with a kasra (ʿiwaj) applies to meanings and to things that are not upright, while with a fatḥa (ʿawaj) it applies to what is upright, such as a spear. The clause "وهم بِالآخِرَةِ كافِرُونَ" ("and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter") is in a place of accusative as a circumstantial clause.

Allah's statement: ﴿وبَيْنَهُما حِجابٌ﴾ ("and between them is a barrier"): that is, between the two groups, or between Paradise and the Fire.

The barrier ("al-Hijab") is the wall mentioned in His statement: ﴿فَضُرِبَ بَيْنَهم بِسُورٍ﴾ ("So a wall with a gate will be set up between them") (al-Hadid: 13).

Allah's statement: ﴿وعَلى الأعْرافِ رِجالٌ﴾ ("and upon the heights are men"). "Al-A'raf" (the Heights) is the plural of "ʿurf", which refers to the battlements of the wall set up between them; from it come "ʿurf al-faras" (the mane of the horse) and "ʿurf al-dik" (the comb of the rooster). In language, al-A'raf means an elevated place. This statement is in the form of praise, as in His statement: ﴿رِجالٌ لا تُلْهِيهِمْ تِجارَةٌ ولا بَيْعٌ عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ﴾ ("men whom neither commerce nor trade distracts from the remembrance of Allah") (al-Nur: 37).

The scholars differed about who the people of al-A'raf are. It was said: they are the martyrs; this was mentioned by al-Qushayri and Shuraḥbil ibn Saʿd. It was said: they are the excellent believers who have finished with the concern for themselves and have freed themselves to observe the conditions of people; this was mentioned by Mujahid. It was said: they are a people of prophets; this was mentioned by al-Zajjaj. It was said: they are a people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal; this was said by Ibn Mas'ud, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Shaʿbi, al-Dahhak and Saʿid ibn Jubayr. It was said: they are al-ʿAbbas, Hamza, ʿAli and Jaʿfar al-Tayyar, who recognise their lovers by the whiteness of their faces and their haters by the blackness of them; this is related from Ibn ʿAbbas. It was said: they are the witnesses of the Resurrection who testify against people for their deeds, and they exist in every nation; al-Nahhas chose this view. It was said: they are the sons of fornication; this is related from Ibn ʿAbbas. It was said: they are angels appointed over these walls who distinguish the disbelievers from the believers before they are admitted to Paradise or the Fire; this was mentioned by Abu Mijlaz.

The clause "يَعْرِفُونَ كُلًّا بِسِيماهم" ("they recognise each by their marks") is a qualifier of "رِجالٌ" (men).

Al-Sima means the mark: that is, they recognise each of the people of Paradise and the Fire by their signs, such as the whiteness and blackness of faces, or the traces of ablution in believers, or a sign that Allah will set for each group in that place by which the men of al-A'raf recognise the happy from the wretched.

﴿ونادَوْا أصْحابَ الجَنَّةِ﴾ ("And they call out to the companions of Paradise"): that is, the men of al-A'raf call out to the companions of Paradise when they see them, saying: ﴿أنْ سَلامٌ عَلَيْكم﴾ ("Peace be upon you"). That is, they call to them with the words "Peace be upon you" as a greeting, honour and good tidings, or they inform them of their safety from the punishment.

Allah's statement: ﴿لَمْ يَدْخُلُوها وهم يَطْمَعُونَ﴾ ("They have not entered it, though they aspire"): that is, the men of al-A'raf had not entered Paradise, while they were hoping to enter it. It was said: the meaning of "yaṭmaʿūn" is that they know they will enter it; this is known among the lexicographers, as "ṭamiʿa" can mean "ʿalima" (to know). This was mentioned by al-Nahhas.

This view, namely that they are the people of al-A'raf, is related from a group including Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Mas'ud.

Abu Mijlaz said: they are the people of Paradise. That is, the people of al-A'raf said to them: "Peace be upon you," while the people of Paradise had not entered it, and they were hoping to enter it.

Allah's statement: ﴿وإذا صُرِفَتْ أبْصارُهم تِلْقاءَ أصْحابِ النّارِ﴾ ("And when their sights are turned toward the companions of the Fire"): that is, when the sights of the people of al-A'raf are turned toward the companions of the Fire, that is, toward their direction. The original meaning of "تِلْقاءَ" is the direction of meeting, which is the direction of facing. No noun of the pattern "tifāl" with a kasra on its first letter comes except two verbal nouns: this one, and "tibyān"; all others have a fatḥa. ﴿قالُوا﴾ ("they say"): that is, the people of al-A'raf say: ﴿رَبَّنا لا تَجْعَلْنا مَعَ القَوْمِ الظّالِمِينَ﴾ ("Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people"). They ask Allah not to make them among them.

﴿ونادى أصْحابُ الأعْرافِ رِجالًا﴾ ("And the companions of al-A'raf call out to men") from the disbelievers, whom they recognise by their marks, i.e. by their signs. "قالُوا" ("they say") is a substitute for "نادى" (called out). ﴿ما أغْنى عَنْكم جَمْعُكُمْ﴾ ("What did your gathering avail you") that you used to gather for barring from the way of Allah? The interrogative is for reproach and censure. Allah's statement: ﴿وما كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ ("and what you used to be arrogant"): "مَا" here is a verbal noun, i.e. "and what your arrogance availed you."

﴿أهَؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ أقْسَمْتُمْ لا يَنالُهُمُ اللَّهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ﴾ ("Are these the ones you swore Allah would not reach with mercy?"). This is from the speech of the people of al-A'raf: that is, they said to the disbelievers, pointing to the Muslims who had gone to Paradise, this statement.

The disbelievers used to swear this oath in the world when they saw the weak Muslims, and this is a rebuke to the disbelievers and a cause of their regret.

Allah's statement: ﴿ادْخُلُوا الجَنَّةَ لا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكم ولا أنْتُمْ تَحْزَنُونَ﴾ ("Enter Paradise; no fear will be upon you, nor will you grieve"). This is the completion of the speech of the people of al-A'raf: that is, they said to the Muslims, "Enter Paradise," for fear and grief have been removed from you after entering.

Talha ibn Musarrif read "أدْخِلُوا" ("admit") with a kasra on the khāʾ.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding Allah's statement: ﴿أنْ قَدْ وجَدْنا ما وعَدَنا رَبُّنا حَقًّا﴾ ("that we have found what our Lord promised to be true"), that he said: "of bliss and honour." ﴿فَهَلْ وجَدْتُمْ ما وعَدَ رَبُّكم حَقًّا﴾ ("Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?"), he said: "of disgrace, humiliation and punishment."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn ʿUmar that the Prophet (ﷺ), when he stood at the well of Badr, recited this verse.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related from al-Suddi, regarding Allah's statement: ﴿وبَيْنَهُما حِجابٌ﴾ ("and between them is a barrier"), that he said: it is the wall, and it is al-A'raf. It was named al-A'raf because its people recognise the people.

Saʿid ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Hudhayfah that he said: al-A'raf is a wall between Paradise and the Fire.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Baʿth wa al-Nushur related from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: al-A'raf is an elevated thing.

al-Firyabi, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh related from him that he said: al-A'raf is a wall with a crest like the crest of the rooster.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related from Saʿid ibn Jubayr that he said: al-A'raf are mountains between Paradise and the Fire, so they are upon its heights, meaning upon its peaks.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn ʿAbbas that it is a hill between Paradise and the Fire, on which some people of sins are held.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Jurayj that he said: they claim it is the Sirat (the bridge).

Ibn Jarir related from Hudhayfah that he said: the companions of al-A'raf are a people who had deeds by which Allah saved them from the Fire, and they are the last to enter Paradise; they knew the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn Mas'ud that they are those whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal; they stand on the Sirat.

Ibn Jarir related from Hudhayfah something similar.

Likewise, ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Saʿid ibn Mansur, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related something similar from him.

Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn ʿAsakir related from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah something similar.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Abu Zurʿah ibn ʿAmr ibn Jarir, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the companions of al-A'raf. He said: 'They are the last of the servants to be separated between. When the Lord of the worlds has finished separating between the servants, He says: You are a people whose good deeds have brought you out of the Fire, but you have not entered Paradise; so you are my freed ones. Graze in Paradise wherever you wish.'"

Ibn Kathir said: this is a good mursal (a hadith whose chain omits the Companion).

Al-Bayhaqi in al-Baʿth related from Hudhayfah, I think he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection. The people of Paradise are commanded to go to Paradise, and the people of the Fire are commanded to go to the Fire. Then it is said to the companions of al-A'raf: What are you waiting for? They say: We are waiting for your command. So it is said to them: Your good deeds have carried you past the Fire so that you do not enter it, and your sins have stood between you and Paradise. So enter by My forgiveness and My mercy."

Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn Manīʿ, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Baʿth related from ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Muzani, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the companions of al-A'raf. He said: They are a people who were killed in the way of Allah while in disobedience to their fathers; their killing in the way of Allah prevented them from the Fire, and their disobedience to their fathers prevented them from Paradise."

Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh related with a weak chain from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, marfuʿ (traced to the Prophet), something similar.

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Baʿth related from Abu Hurayrah, marfuʿ, something similar as well.

al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah in his Musnad, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh related from ʿAbd Allah ibn Malik al-Hilali, from his father, marfuʿ, something similar.

Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn ʿAbbas, marfuʿ, something similar.

Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh related from a man of Muzaynah, marfuʿ, something similar.

Abu al-Shaykh related from Abu ʿUbaydah ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAmmar that he was asked about Allah's statement: ﴿لَمْ يَدْخُلُوها وهم يَطْمَعُونَ﴾ ("They have not entered it, though they aspire"). He said: The angels greeted them while they had not entered it and were hoping to enter it when they greeted them.

Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh related from al-Suddi, who said: The companions of al-A'raf recognise people by their marks: the people of the Fire by the blackness of their faces, and the people of Paradise by the whiteness of their faces. When they pass by a group that is being taken to Paradise, they say: "Peace be upon you." When they pass by a group that is being taken to the Fire, they say: ﴿رَبَّنا لا تَجْعَلْنا مَعَ القَوْمِ الظّالِمِينَ﴾ ("Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people").

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding ﴿ونادى أصْحابُ الأعْرافِ رِجالًا﴾ ("And the companions of al-A'raf call out to men"), that he said: "in the Fire." ﴿يَعْرِفُونَهم بِسِيماهم قالُوا ما أغْنى عَنْكم جَمْعُكم وما كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ ("They recognise them by their marks, and say: What did your gathering avail you, and your arrogance?"). Allah said to the people of arrogance: ﴿أهَؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ أقْسَمْتُمْ لا يَنالُهُمُ اللَّهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ﴾ ("Are these the ones you swore Allah would not reach with mercy?"), meaning the companions of al-A'raf. ﴿ادْخُلُوا الجَنَّةَ لا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكم ولا أنْتُمْ تَحْزَنُونَ﴾ ("Enter Paradise; no fear will be upon you, nor will you grieve").

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 7, verse 50–54 (part 1 of 2):

His saying: ﴿Pour upon us some of the water﴾. Al-ifada (pouring out) means to lavish, as one says: he poured (afada) his blessings upon him. They asked them to share with them some of the water, or something of what Allah has provided them besides it, of drinks or foods. They answered with their words: ﴿Indeed, Allah has forbidden them﴾, that is, the water and what Allah has provided besides it, to the disbelievers. So we will not share with you anything of what Allah has forbidden you. It was also said that this call from the people of the Fire took place after the people of the A'raf had entered Paradise.

The clause ﴿those who took their religion as amusement and play﴾ is in the position of a descriptive qualifier (sifa) of "the disbelievers" and is in the genitive position.

The explanation of lahw (amusement), la'ib (play) and gharar (deception) has already been given.

His saying: ﴿So today We will forget them﴾, that is, We will leave them in the Fire, ﴿as they forgot the meeting of this their Day﴾. The kaf (ka) is an adjective of an omitted verbal noun (masdar), and ma is a verbal-noun particle (masdariyya): that is, a forgetting like their forgetting the meeting of this their Day.

His saying: ﴿and as they used to deny Our signs﴾ is coordinated with "as they forgot": that is, as they forgot, and as they used to deny them, that is, reject them.

The lam in ﴿And We have certainly brought them﴾ is the answer to an oath.

The word "the Book" is used generically if the pronoun refers to the disbelievers in general; but if it refers to the contemporaries of the Prophet (ﷺ), then "the Book" means the Qur'an. Tafsil (detailing) means clarification. The phrase ﴿with knowledge﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal): that is, knowing, while it is guidance and mercy for the believers.

Al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' said: it is also permissible to read "guidance and mercy" in the genitive case as a qualifier of "Book."

His saying: ﴿Do they await anything but its final outcome?﴾ is read with hamza from alla (to come to), while the people of Madina drop the hamza.

Al-nazar here means waiting (intizar): that is, do they await anything but what they were promised in the Book of punishment, toward which the matter returns? It was said: its ta'wil is its recompense; it was also said: its consequence. The meanings are close.

Yawma (the day) is an adverbial complement of "will say": that is, on the day its ta'wil comes, which is the Day of Resurrection, those who forgot it before will say, that is, those who abandoned it before its ta'wil came: ﴿The messengers of our Lord have certainly come with the truth﴾, which Allah sent them with to us. ﴿Then are there any intercessors for us?﴾ This is an interrogative from them, and its meaning is wishing (tamanni). ﴿So that they may intercede for us﴾ is in the accusative because it is an answer to the interrogative.

His saying: ﴿Or are we returned?﴾ Al-Farra' said: the meaning is "or can we be returned, so that we may act other than what we used to do."

Al-Zajjaj said: "nuradd" is coordinated upon the meaning: that is, can anyone intercede for us, or can we be returned?

Ibn Abi Ishaq read "aw nuradda fana'mala" with both verbs in the accusative, like the saying of Imru' al-Qays:
"I said to her: do not let your eye weep, for we only seek a kingdom or die and be excused."

Al-Hasan read both in the nominative. The meaning of the verse: Are there intercessors for us who will rescue us from what we are in of punishment, or can we be returned to the world so that we may do righteous deeds other than the sins we used to do? ﴿They have lost their souls﴾, that is, they did not benefit from them, so their souls became a trial and affliction for them, and so it is as if they lost them, as a merchant loses his capital. It was also said: they lost the bliss and their share of the souls. ﴿And what they used to fabricate has departed from them﴾, that is, their fabrication or that which they used to fabricate.

The meaning is that their lie which they used to say in the world has become void, or what they used to make partners with Allah has disappeared from them, so it did not benefit them, nor was it present with them.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾. This is a kind of the wondrous work of Allah, the majesty of His power, and His singularity in bringing into existence, which obliges the servants to affirm His oneness and worship Him.

The root of "six" (sitta) is sidsa; the taa replaced one of the two siins, and the daal was assimilated into it. The evidence for this is that in diminutive one says sudaysa, in plural asdas, and one says "he came as the sixth" (sadisan) to someone.

A day is from the rising of the sun to its setting. It was said: these days are of the days of this world; it was said: of the days of the Hereafter. These six days, the first of which is Sunday and the last Friday. He, glory be to Him, is able to create them in a single instant, saying to them "Be," and they are. But He willed to teach His servants gentleness and deliberation in affairs; or He created them in six days because everything has a term with Him. In another verse: ﴿And We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us﴾ (Qaf: 38).

His saying: ﴿Then He istawa over the Throne﴾. The scholars have differed about the meaning of this in fourteen opinions, and the most correct and most appropriate to the truth is the position of the righteous predecessors (salaf), that He istawa over it without modality (bila kayf), but in the manner befitting Him, while being exalted above what is not permissible for Him. Istiwa' in the Arabic language means to be high and to settle.

Al-Jawhari said: istawa 'ala zahr dabbatihi means he settled upon the back of his mount; istawa ila al-sama' means he ascended; istawa means he gained control and prevailed, and from this is the saying of the poet:
"Bishr has taken control of Iraq, without sword and without spilled blood."

Istawa al-rajulu means his youth ended; istawa means he became straight and balanced.

It is related from Abu 'Ubayda that the meaning of istawa here is "he rose high," and similar is the saying of the poet:
"So he brought them to water at Thaqif in a desert waste, when the Yemeni star had circled and risen high."
That is, it rose high and ascended.

Al-'arsh (the Throne): al-Jawhari said it is the king's couch.

The word 'arsh is used for other meanings, among them: the arsh of a house is its roof; the arsh of a well is its lining with wood; the arsh of al-simak is four small stars; and it is used for kingdom, authority and might. From this is the saying of Zuhayr:
"You two overtook Abs when their throne had been broken, and Dhubyan when their feet slipped."
And the saying of another:
"If they kill you, I have broken their thrones, through 'Utayba ibn al-Harith ibn Shihab."
And the saying of another:
"They saw my throne with its two sides broken, and when it broke, they left me alone."

The attribute of the Throne of the Most Merciful and its encompassing the heavens and the earth and what is between them and what is upon them has been established in authentic traditions, and this is what is meant here.

His saying: ﴿He covers the night over the day﴾, that is, He makes the night like a covering for the day, so that its darkness conceals its light.

ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza and al-Kisa'i read "yughashshi" with tashdid (doubled), and the rest read it without tashdid; both are dialects: one says aghsha yughshi and ghashshā yughashshi. Al-taghshiya originally means covering one thing with another. In this verse he did not mention "covers the night with the day," being satisfied with one of the two matters over the other, as in His saying: ﴿garments that protect you from the heat﴾ (al-Nahl: 81).

Humayd ibn Qays read "yughshi al-laylu al-nahar" with the verb attributed to the night. The clause is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause: the estimated sense is "He istawa over the Throne, covering the night over the day." Likewise His saying: ﴿seeking it urgently﴾ is a circumstantial clause of the night: that is, the night seeking the day with an urgent seeking that never slackens in any way. "Hathithan" is an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, that is, he seeks it with urgent seeking; or it is a circumstantial clause of the subject of "yatlubu."

Al-hathth means haste and speed; one says: he fled hathithan, that is, hastening.

His saying: ﴿And the sun and the moon and the stars, subjected by His command﴾. Al-Akhfash said: it is coordinated upon "the heavens." Ibn 'Amir read all of them in the nominative, as a beginning and predicate.

The meaning on the first reading: and He created the sun, the moon and the stars in the state of being subjected; on the second: information about these being subjected.

His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, to Him belong creation and command﴾. It is information from Him, glory be to Him, to His servants that both belong to Him. "Khalq" means the created thing, and "amr" means His speech, which is "Be" in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, "Be," and it is﴾ (al-Nahl: 40). Or "amr" is meant as what He commands in detail, or the disposal of His creatures. When He, glory be to Him, mentioned in this verse the creation of the heavens and the earth in that brief span, then His istiwa' over His Throne, and the subjection of the sun, moon and stars, and that to Him belong creation and command, He said: (p-479) ﴿Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, that is, His blessing has increased and become vast. From this comes "buriqa al-shay'" and "buriqa fihi." So said Ibn 'Arafa.

Al-Azhari said that the meaning of "tabaraka" is exalted and magnified.

The explanation of "Lord of the worlds" has already been given fully in al-Fatiha.

Ibn Abi Shayba, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise﴾, that he said: a man calls his brother, saying: "O my brother, help me, for I have been burned, so pour some water upon me." It is said to him: answer him. He says: "Indeed, Allah has forbidden them to the disbelievers."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿Pour upon us some of the water or of what Allah has provided you﴾, that he said: of the food.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn Zayd regarding the verse that he said: they ask them for drink and ask them for food; and regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has forbidden them to the disbelievers﴾, he said: the food and drink of Paradise.

They answered with their words: ﴿Indeed, Allah has forbidden them﴾, that is, the water and what Allah has provided besides it, to the disbelievers. The clause ﴿those who took their religion as amusement and play﴾ is in the position of a descriptive qualifier (sifa) of "the disbelievers" and is in the genitive position.

The explanation of lahw (amusement), la'ib (play) and gharar (deception) has already been given.

His saying: ﴿So today We will forget them﴾, that is, We will leave them in the Fire, ﴿as they forgot the meeting of this their Day﴾. The kaf (ka) is an adjective of an omitted verbal noun (masdar), and ma is a verbal-noun particle (masdariyya): that is, a forgetting like their forgetting the meeting of this their Day.

His saying: ﴿and as they used to deny Our signs﴾ is coordinated with "as they forgot": that is, as they forgot, and as they used to deny them, that is, reject them.

The lam in ﴿And We have certainly brought them﴾ is the answer to an oath.

The word "the Book" is used generically if the pronoun refers to the disbelievers in general; but if it refers to the contemporaries of the Prophet (ﷺ), then "the Book" means the Qur'an. Tafsil (detailing) means clarification. The phrase ﴿with knowledge﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal): that is, knowing, while it is guidance and mercy for the believers.

Al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' said: it is also permissible to read "guidance and mercy" in the genitive case as a qualifier of "Book."

His saying: ﴿Do they await anything but its final outcome?﴾ is read with hamza from alla (to come to), while the people of Madina drop the hamza.

Al-nazar here means waiting (intizar): that is, do they await anything but what they were promised in the Book of punishment, toward which the matter returns? It was said: its ta'wil is its recompense; it was also said: its consequence. The meanings are close.

Yawma (the day) is an adverbial complement of "will say": that is, on the day its ta'wil comes, which is the Day of Resurrection, those who forgot it before will say, that is, those who abandoned it before its ta'wil came: ﴿The messengers of our Lord have certainly come with the truth﴾, which Allah sent them with to us. ﴿Then are there any intercessors for us?﴾ This is an interrogative from them, and its meaning is wishing (tamanni). ﴿So that they may intercede for us﴾ is in the accusative because it is an answer to the interrogative.

His saying: ﴿Or are we returned?﴾ Al-Farra' said: the meaning is "or can we be returned, so that we may act other than what we used to do."

Al-Zajjaj said: "nuradd" is coordinated upon the meaning: that is, can anyone intercede for us, or can we be returned?

Ibn Abi Ishaq read "aw nuradda fana'mala" with both verbs in the accusative, like the saying of Imru' al-Qays:
"I said to her: do not let your eye weep, for we only seek a kingdom or die and be excused."

Al-Hasan read both in the nominative. The meaning of the verse: Are there intercessors for us who will rescue us from what we are in of punishment, or can we be returned to the world so that we may do righteous deeds other than the sins we used to do? ﴿They have lost their souls﴾, that is, they did not benefit from them, so their souls became a trial and affliction for them, and so it is as if they lost them, as a merchant loses his capital. It was also said: they lost the bliss and their share of the souls. ﴿And what they used to fabricate has departed from them﴾, that is, their fabrication or that which they used to fabricate.

The meaning is that their lie which they used to say in the world has become void, or what they used to make partners with Allah has disappeared from them, so it did not benefit them, nor was it present with them.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾. This is a kind of the wondrous work of Allah, the majesty of His power, and His singularity in bringing into existence, which obliges the servants to affirm His oneness and worship Him.

A day is from the rising of the sun to its setting. It was said: these days are of the days of this world; it was said: of the days of the Hereafter. But He willed to teach His servants gentleness and deliberation in affairs; or He created them in six days because everything has a term with Him. In another verse: ﴿And We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us﴾ (Qaf: 38).

His saying: ﴿Then He istawa over the Throne﴾. The scholars have differed about the meaning of this in fourteen opinions, and the most correct and most appropriate to the truth is the position of the righteous predecessors (salaf), that He istawa over it without modality (bila kayf), but in the manner befitting Him, while being exalted above what is not permissible for Him. Istiwa' in the Arabic language means to be high and to settle.

Al-Jawhari said: istawa 'ala zahr dabbatihi means he settled upon the back of his mount; istawa ila al-sama' means he ascended; istawa means he gained control and prevailed, and from this is the saying of the poet:

Istawa al-rajulu means his youth ended; istawa means he became straight and balanced.

It is related from Abu 'Ubayda that the meaning of istawa here is "he rose high," and similar is the saying of the poet:
"So he brought them to water at Thaqif in a desert waste, when the Yemeni star had circled and risen high."
That is, it rose high and ascended.

The word 'arsh is used for other meanings, among them: the arsh of a house is its roof; the arsh of a well is its lining with wood; the arsh of al-simak is four small stars; and it is used for kingdom, authority and might. From this is the saying of Zuhayr:

"If they kill you, I have broken their thrones, through 'Utayba ibn al-Harith ibn Shihab."
And the saying of another:
"They saw my throne with its two sides broken, and when it broke, they left me alone."

Al-hathth means haste and speed; one says: he fled hathithan, that is, hastening.

His saying: ﴿And the sun and the moon and the stars, subjected by His command﴾. Al-Akhfash said: it is coordinated upon "the heavens." Ibn 'Amir read all of them in the nominative, as a beginning and predicate.

The meaning on the first reading: and He created the sun, the moon and the stars in the state of being subjected; on the second: information about these being subjected.

His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, to Him belong creation and command﴾. It is information from Him, glory be to Him, to His servants that both belong to Him. "Khalq" means the created thing, and "amr" means His speech, which is "Be" in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, "Be," and it is﴾ (al-Nahl: 40). Or "amr" is meant as what He commands in detail, or the disposal of His creatures. When He, glory be to Him, mentioned in this verse the creation of the heavens and the earth in that brief span, then His istiwa' over His Throne, and the subjection of the sun, moon and stars, and that to Him belong creation and command, He said: (p-479) ﴿Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, that is, His blessing has increased and become vast. From this comes "buriqa al-shay'" and "buriqa fihi." So said Ibn 'Arafa.

Al-Azhari said that the meaning of "tabaraka" is exalted and magnified.

The explanation of "Lord of the worlds" has already been given fully in al-Fatiha.

The clause ﴿those who took their religion as amusement and play﴾ is in the position of a descriptive qualifier (sifa) of "the disbelievers" and is in the genitive position.

The explanation of lahw (amusement), la'ib (play) and gharar (deception) has already been given.

His saying: ﴿and as they used to deny Our signs﴾ is coordinated with "as they forgot": that is, as they forgot, and as they used to deny them, that is, reject them.

The lam in ﴿And We have certainly brought them﴾ is the answer to an oath.

Tafsil (detailing) means clarification. The phrase ﴿with knowledge﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal): that is, knowing, while it is guidance and mercy for the believers.

Al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' said: it is also permissible to read "guidance and mercy" in the genitive case as a qualifier of "Book."

His saying: ﴿Or are we returned?﴾ Al-Farra' said: the meaning is "or can we be returned, so that we may act other than what we used to do."

Al-Zajjaj said: "nuradd" is coordinated upon the meaning: that is, can anyone intercede for us, or can we be returned?

"I said to her: do not let your eye weep, for we only seek a kingdom or die and be excused."

Al-Hasan read both in the nominative. The meaning of the verse: Are there intercessors for us who will rescue us from what we are in of punishment, or can we be returned to the world so that we may do righteous deeds other than the sins we used to do? ﴿They have lost their souls﴾, that is, they did not benefit from them, so their souls became a trial and affliction for them, and so it is as if they lost them, as a merchant loses his capital. It was also said: they lost the bliss and their share of the souls. ﴿And what they used to fabricate has departed from them﴾, that is, their fabrication or that which they used to fabricate.

The meaning is that their lie which they used to say in the world has become void, or what they used to make partners with Allah has disappeared from them, so it did not benefit them, nor was it present with them.

And the saying of another:

And the saying of another:

Al-'arsh (the Throne): al-Jawhari said it is the king's couch.

The word 'arsh is used for other meanings, among them: the arsh of a house is its roof; the arsh of a well is its lining with wood; the arsh of al-simak is four small stars; and it is used for kingdom, authority and might. From this is the saying of Zuhayr:
"You two overtook Abs when their throne had been broken, and Dhubyan when their feet slipped."
And the saying of another:
"If they kill you, I have broken their thrones, through 'Utayba ibn al-Harith ibn Shihab."
And the saying of another:
"They saw my throne with its two sides broken, and when it broke, they left me alone."

The attribute of the Throne of the Most Merciful and its encompassing the heavens and the earth and what is between them and what is upon them has been established in authentic traditions, and this is what is meant here.

His saying: ﴿He covers the night over the day﴾, that is, He makes the night like a covering for the day, so that its darkness conceals its light.

ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza and al-Kisa'i read "yughashshi" with tashdid (doubled), and the rest read it without tashdid; both are dialects: one says aghsha yughshi and ghashshā yughashshi. Al-taghshiya originally means covering one thing with another. In this verse he did not mention "covers the night with the day," being satisfied with one of the two matters over the other, as in His saying: ﴿garments that protect you from the heat﴾ (al-Nahl: 81).

Humayd ibn Qays read "yughshi al-laylu al-nahar" with the verb attributed to the night. The clause is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause: the estimated sense is "He istawa over the Throne, covering the night over the day." Likewise His saying: ﴿seeking it urgently﴾ is a circumstantial clause of the night: that is, the night seeking the day with an urgent seeking that never slackens in any way. "Hathithan" is an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, that is, he seeks it with urgent seeking; or it is a circumstantial clause of the subject of "yatlubu."

Al-hathth means haste and speed; one says: he fled hathithan, that is, hastening.

His saying: ﴿And the sun and the moon and the stars, subjected by His command﴾. Al-Akhfash said: it is coordinated upon "the heavens." Ibn 'Amir read all of them in the nominative, as a beginning and predicate.

The meaning on the first reading: and He created the sun, the moon and the stars in the state of being subjected; on the second: information about these being subjected.

His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, to Him belong creation and command﴾. It is information from Him, glory be to Him, to His servants that both belong to Him. "Khalq" means the created thing, and "amr" means His speech, which is "Be" in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, "Be," and it is﴾ (al-Nahl: 40). Or "amr" is meant as what He commands in detail, or the disposal of His creatures. When He, glory be to Him, mentioned in this verse the creation of the heavens and the earth in that brief span, then His istiwa' over His Throne, and the subjection of the sun, moon and stars, and that to Him belong creation and command, He said: (p-479) ﴿Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, that is, His blessing has increased and become vast. From this comes "buriqa al-shay'" and "buriqa fihi." So said Ibn 'Arafa.

Al-Azhari said that the meaning of "tabaraka" is exalted and magnified.

The explanation of "Lord of the worlds" has already been given fully in al-Fatiha.

Ibn Abi Shayba, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise﴾, that he said: a man calls his brother, saying: "O my brother, help me, for I have been burned, so pour some water upon me." It is said to him: answer him. He says: "Indeed, Allah has forbidden them to the disbelievers."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿Pour upon us some of the water or of what Allah has provided you﴾, that he said: of the food.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn Zayd regarding the verse that he said: they ask them for drink and ask them for food; and regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has forbidden them to the disbelievers﴾, he said: the food and drink of Paradise.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿So today We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of this their Day﴾, he said: We will leave them in the Fire as they left the meeting of this their Day.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿So today We will forget them﴾, he said: We will delay them.

'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Qatada regarding His saying: ﴿Do they await anything but its ta'wil﴾, he said: its consequence.

Ibn Abi Shayba, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Mujahid, who said: ﴿The day its ta'wil comes﴾ is its recompense.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿the day its ta'wil comes﴾, he said: the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿what they used to fabricate﴾, he said: what they used to lie about in the world.

Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾, he said: each day is equal to a thousand years.

Ibn Mardawayh reported from Umm Salama, who said regarding His saying: ﴿istawa over the Throne﴾: the modality is unintelligible, the istiwa' is not unknown, affirming it is faith, and denying it is disbelief.

al-Lalika'i reported from Malik that a man asked him: how did He istawa over the Throne? He said: the modality is unintelligible, and the istiwa' from Him is not unknown; belief in it is obligatory, and asking about it is an innovation.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya in the Book of Supplication and al-Khatib in his History reported from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali who said: I guarantee for whoever recites these twenty verses every night that Allah will protect him from every oppressive ruler, from every rebellious devil, from every predatory beast, and from every transgressing thief: the Ayat al-Kursi, three verses from al-A'raf, ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ (al-A'raf: 54–56), ten from the beginning of al-Saffat, three verses from al-Rahman beginning with ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind﴾ (al-Rahman: 33–35), and the end of al-Hashr.

Abu al-Shaykh reported from 'Ubayd ibn Abi Marzuq who said: whoever recites ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth﴾, the verse, at his sleep, an angel will spread his wing over him until morning, and he will be safe from theft.

Abu al-Shaykh reported from Muhammad ibn Qays, companion of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, who said: a man from the people of Madina fell ill, and a group of his companions came to visit him. One of them recited ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth﴾, the entire verse, and the man had become silent; then he moved, then he sat up, then he prostrated the whole day and night until the next day at the same hour in which he had prostrated. His family said to him: praise be to Allah who has healed you. He said: an angel was sent to take my soul, but when your companion recited the verse he recited, the angel prostrated, and I prostrated with his prostration. This is when he raised his head, then he leaned and died.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿He covers the night with the day﴾, that he said: He covers the night with the day, so that it takes away its light and pursues it swiftly until it overtakes it.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatadah, who said: The night covers the day (yalbasu al-layl al-nahar, "the night clothes the day").

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿swiftly﴾ (hathithan), that he said: Quickly.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, regarding His words ﴿Surely, to Him belong the creation and the command﴾, that he said: The creation is what is below the Throne, and the command is what is above that.

Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated from him, who said: The creation is the creation itself, and the command is the speech (al-kalam).

[p. 479]

God Almighty commanded them to supplicate, and He restricted this by specifying that the one supplicating should be humble in his supplication and keep it hidden. The accusative of *tadarru'an* (humbly) and *khufyah* (secretly) is an adverbial of state: that is, "supplicate humbly and secretly," or they are an adjective of an omitted verbal noun: that is, "supplicate with a supplication of humility and a supplication of secrecy."

*Tadarru'* (humility) derives from *ad-durra'ah*, which means abasement, submissiveness and lowliness. *Khufyah* means keeping it private. This is because it cuts off the root of *riya'* (showing off) more decisively and closes the door to whatever contradicts *ikhlas* (sincerity). Then He gave the reason for this with His words: "Indeed He does not love the transgressors," that is, those who exceed what they were commanded in supplication and in everything else. Whoever exceeds what God has commanded him in any matter has transgressed, and God does not love transgressors. Exceeding the limits in supplication enters this general statement as a primary inclusion.

Among transgression in supplication is that the supplicant asks for what is not his due, such as eternal life in this world, or attaining what is impossible in itself, or seeking to reach the ranks of the prophets in the Hereafter, or raising his voice in supplication, shouting.

His words: ﴿And do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation﴾. God, Glorified is He, forbade them from corruption on the earth in any form, whether small or great, and among it is killing people, destroying their dwellings, cutting down their trees, and diverting their rivers.

Among corruption on the earth is disbelief in God and falling into [p. 480] His disobedience. The meaning of *ba'da islahiha* (after its reformation) is: after God had reformed it by sending the messengers, revealing the books, and establishing the laws.

His words: ﴿And supplicate Him in fear and hope﴾. The i'rab (grammatical analysis) of these two words admits the two possibilities mentioned earlier for *tadarru'an* and *khufyah*. In this is the indication that it is prescribed for the supplicant to be, during his supplication, fearful and anxious, yet hopeful that God will answer his supplication. For when he combines fear and hope during supplication, he attains his goal.

*Al-khawf* (fear) is being disturbed by harms whose occurrence cannot be assured against, and *at-tama'* (hope) is anticipating the occurrence of desirable things.

His words: ﴿Indeed, the mercy of God is near to the doers of good﴾. This is an information from God, Glorified is He, that His mercy is near to His righteous servants, in whatever form their goodness may be. In this is an encouragement for the servants toward good and an incitement for them, for the nearness of this mercy, through which one attains every sought-after goal, is for every servant of God.

The linguists and grammarians have differed concerning the reason for the masculine form of the predicate of "the mercy of God," where He said *qarib* (near, masculine) and did not say *qariba* (feminine). Az-Zajjaj said: *ar-rahmah* is interpreted as *ar-rahim* (the womb/kinship) because it carries the meaning of pardon and forgiveness, and an-Nahhas preferred this interpretation.

An-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: *ar-rahmah* is a verbal noun in the sense of *at-tarahhum* (showing mercy), and the original form of a verbal noun is masculine.

Al-Akhfash Sa'id said: by *ar-rahmah* here he meant rain, and the masculine for some feminine nouns is permissible. He recited:

*"No cloud has poured its pouring, nor land whose herbs have grown green."*

Abu 'Ubayda said: the masculine *qarib* is according to the masculine form of *al-makan* (the place): that is, "a near place."

Ali ibn Sulayman al-Akhfash said: this is an error. If it were as he said, *qarib* would be in the accusative, as you say: "Indeed Zayd is near to you" (*qariban*).

Al-Farra' said: when *qarib* means distance, it may be masculine or feminine; and if it means kinship, it is feminine without any disagreement among them.

It is related from al-Farra' that he said: it is said in kinship, "she is the near relative of so-and-so" (*qariba*), and in other than kinship it is permissible to use the masculine and feminine, so one says: "your house is near to us" (*qarib*) and "so-and-so is near to us" (*qarib*).

God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near﴾ (al-Ahzab: 63). And from it is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

*"Woe to you! Neither Umm Hashim is near, nor al-Basbasah, daughter of Yashkur."*

It is related from az-Zajjaj that he refuted al-Farra' in what he said and said: the way of the masculine and feminine is that they follow their own verbs. It was also said: since the feminine form of *ar-rahmah* is not real, it is permissible for its predicate to be masculine. Al-Jawhari mentioned this meaning.

His words: "And He is the One who sends the winds as glad tidings before His mercy." This is a conjunction with His words: ﴿He covers the night with the day﴾, and it includes the mention of one of the blessings with which He bestowed favour upon His servants, along with what this contains of indication of His oneness and the establishment of His divinity.

*Riyah* is the plural of *rih* (wind), and the original root of *rih* is *rawh*. The people of the two sanctuaries (Makkah and Madinah) and Abu 'Amr recited *nushuran* with a *damma* on the *nun* and the *shin*, as the plural of *nashir* (spreader), according to the sense of attribution: that is, possessing spreading.

Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ibn 'Amir recited *nushran* with a *damma* on the *nun* and a sukun on the *shin*, from *nashara*.

Al-A'mash, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited *nashran* with a *fatha* on the *nun* and a sukun on the *shin*, as a verbal noun; it is also permissible that it be a verbal noun in the position of a circumstantial accusative (*hal*). The meaning of these readings returns to *an-nashr* (spreading), which is the opposite of *at-tayy* (folding). It is as if the wind, while still, was folded, and then released from its folds so that it becomes as if opened.

Abu 'Ubayda said: its meaning is scattered in its directions, according to the sense of "we spread them here and there."

'Asim recited *bushran* with a *ba'* (single dot) and a sukun on the *shin*, as the plural of *bashir* (bearer of good news): that is, the winds bring good news of rain. A similar verse is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He sends the winds as bearers of glad tidings﴾ (ar-Rum: 46).

His words: ﴿before His mercy﴾. By *ar-rahmah* here he meant rain: that is, in front of His mercy. The meaning is that He, Glorified is He, sends the winds spreading or bringing glad tidings before the rain.

His words: ﴿until when they carry heavy clouds﴾. "Aqalla fulan ash-shay'" means he carried it and lifted it. *As-sahab* (the cloud) may be masculine or feminine. The meaning is: until the winds carry heavy clouds laden with the water that they are carrying, "We drive it," that is, the cloud, "to a dead land," that is, a barren land with no vegetation. It is said: "I drove it to the land of such-and-such," and "to the land of such-and-such." It was also said: the *lam* here is the *lam* of cause: that is, for the sake of a dead land. *Al-baladu* is the inhabited place on the earth. ﴿Then We sent down water thereby﴾: that is, with the land to which We drove it; or with the cloud: that is, We sent down with the cloud the water which it carries; or with the wind: that is, We sent down with the wind sent before the rain the water. It was also said: the *ba'* here means *min* (from): that is, "We sent down from it water, then We brought forth thereby," that is, with the water, "from all the fruits," that is, from all their kinds.

His words: ﴿Thus We bring forth the dead﴾: that is, like that bringing forth, which is the bringing forth of fruits, We will bring forth the dead from the graves on the day of their gathering ﴿that you may remember﴾: that is, that you may remember, so that you know the greatness of God's power, the wondrousness of His craftsmanship, and that He is capable of resurrecting you just as He was capable of bringing forth the fruits that you witness.

His words: ﴿And the good land, its vegetation comes forth by the permission of its Lord﴾.

That is, the good soil, its vegetation comes forth by the permission and facilitation of God, a good, complete and full emergence. ﴿And that which is corrupt comes forth only sparsely﴾: that is, and the corrupt soil does not bring forth its vegetation except sparsely: that is, there is no good in it.

Talhah ibn Musarrif recited *nakdan* with a sukun on the *kaf*.

Ibn al-Qa'qa' recited *nakadan* with a *fatha* on the *kaf*: that is, possessing scarcity.

The rest recited *nakidan* with a *fatha* on the *nun* and a *kasra* on the *kaf*.

It was recited *yukhriju* (with a *damma* on the *ya'*), that is, the land brings it forth. It was said: the meaning of the verse is a comparison: God, Exalted is He, likened the quick of understanding to the good land, and the dull to the corrupt land, as mentioned by an-Nahhas. It was also said: this is a parable for hearts, so He likened the heart receptive to admonition to the good land, and the one far from it to the corrupt land, as said by al-Hasan. It was also said: it is a parable for the heart of the believer and the hypocrite, as said by Qatadah. It was also said: it is a parable for the good and the bad among the children of Adam, as said by Mujahid.

﴿Thus We vary the signs﴾: that is, like that variation ﴿for a people who give thanks﴾ to God and acknowledge His blessing.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu ash-Shaykh have related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly﴾, that he said: "secretly" means privately. ﴿Indeed, He does not love the transgressors﴾ in supplication or in anything else.

Abu ash-Shaykh has related from Qatadah, who said: "humbly" is openly, and "secretly" is privately.

Ibn Abi Hatim has related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning His words ﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly﴾, that he meant "submissively," and "secretly": meaning in a low voice and calm in your needs of the matters of this world and the Hereafter. ﴿Indeed, He does not love the transgressors﴾: he said: do not invoke evil upon a believing man or woman, such as saying, "O God, disgrace him and curse him" and the like, for that is transgression.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim have related from Abu Mijlaz, concerning His words ﴿Indeed, He does not love the transgressors﴾, that he said: do not ask for the ranks of the prophets.

Ibn al-Mubarak, Ibn Jarir and Abu ash-Shaykh have related from al-Hasan, who said: The Muslims used to strive greatly in supplication, and no voice of theirs could be heard, except a murmur between them and their Lord. That is because God says: ﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly﴾, and because God mentioned a righteous servant and approved his words, so He said: ﴿When he called upon his Lord with a secret call﴾ (Maryam: 3).

Ibn Abi Hatim has related from Ibn Salih, concerning His words ﴿And do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation﴾, that he said: after the prophets and their companions had reformed it.

Abu ash-Shaykh has related from Abu Sinan concerning the verse, that he said: I have made lawful what is lawful for Me, forbidden what is forbidden for Me, and set the limits of My bounds, so do not corrupt them.

Abu ash-Shaykh has related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿And supplicate Him in fear and hope﴾, that he said: fear of Him and hope for what is with Him. ﴿Indeed, the mercy of God is near to the doers of good﴾: meaning the believers; and whoever does not believe in God is among the corrupters.

Ibn Jurayj, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu ash-Shaykh have related from as-Suddi, concerning His words ﴿And He is the One who sends the winds﴾, that he said: God sends the wind, and it brings the cloud from between the two horizons, the edge of the sky and the earth, from where they meet, and it brings it out from there; then it spreads it, spreading it through the sky as He wills; then He opens the gates of the sky, and the water flows upon the cloud; then the cloud rains after that.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu ash-Shaykh have related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿glad tidings before His mercy﴾, that he said: people rejoice in them.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim have related from as-Suddi, concerning His words ﴿before His mercy﴾, that he said: it is the rain. And concerning His words ﴿Thus We bring forth the dead﴾, he said: thus you will come forth, and thus is the resurrection, just as the crop comes forth by water.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu ash-Shaykh have related from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿Thus We bring forth the dead﴾, that he said: when God wills to bring forth the dead, He sends rain upon the sky until it splits the earth open for them; then He sends the spirits, and each spirit descends to its body. Thus God gives life to the dead through the rain, just as He gives life to the earth.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim have related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿And the good land﴾ up to the end of the verse, that he said: it is a parable God struck for the believer. He says: he is good and his deed is good, just as the good land its fruit is good. ﴿And that which is corrupt﴾ is struck as a parable for the disbeliever, like a salt-laden, barren land from which no blessing comes forth. So the disbeliever is the corrupt one and his deed is corrupt. Something similar has been related from a group of the Successors.
