The admonishing group said: our admonition is an excuse to Allah, ﴿and perhaps they will fear Allah﴾. If they had been only two groups, the admonishing non-disobedient group and the disobedient group, he would have said: "perhaps you will fear Allah."

His words: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾, meaning when the disobedient people of the town left what the righteous who forbid evil had reminded them of, leaving like one who forgets a thing and turns away from it completely. ﴿We saved those who forbade evil﴾, meaning those who performed the forbidding and did not abandon it. ﴿And We seized those who did wrong﴾, and they were the transgressors who exceeded the limits on the Sabbath, ﴿with a grievous punishment (bi'sin)﴾, meaning a severe one, from ba'usa (to be severe) when a thing is harsh. There are eleven recitations of this word by the Seven and others. ﴿Because they were defiantly disobedient﴾, meaning because of their defiance. The prepositional phrase is connected to "akhadhna" (We seized).

﴿So when they insolently persisted in what they had been forbidden﴾, meaning they exceeded the limit in disobedience to Allah, glory be to Him, out of rebelliousness and arrogance. ﴿We said to them: Be apes, despised﴾, meaning We commanded them with a creational command, not a verbal command: that is, We transformed them into apes. It was said: He, glory be to Him, first punished them for their disobedience, and when they did not give up, He transformed them into apes. It was also said: His words "So when they insolently persisted in what they had been forbidden" are a repetition of His words "So when they forgot what they had been reminded of," for emphasis and affirmation, and that the transformation is the grievous punishment. "Khasi'in" means abject, humiliated, or distanced and expelled. It is said: "khasa'tuhu fakhusi'a," meaning I pushed him away and he withdrew.

Know that the apparent meaning of the Qur'anic text is that none were saved from the punishment except the forbidding group which did not disobey, according to His words: ﴿We saved those who forbade evil﴾, and that none were punished by transformation except the disobedient group, according to His words: ﴿So when they insolently persisted in what they had been forbidden, We said to them: Be apes, despised﴾. If the groups among them were three as previously mentioned, then the group that did not forbid and did not disobey may possibly have been transformed along with the disobedient group, because they wronged themselves by staying silent about the prohibition and were insolent toward what Allah had forbidden them, namely abandoning the forbidding of evil. And it is possible that they were not transformed, because although they wronged themselves and were insolent toward their Lord's command and prohibition, they did not wrong themselves by this specific sin, which is hunting the fish on the Sabbath day, nor were they insolent toward His prohibition to them against hunting. As for when the third group was forbidding like the second group, and was only made a separate group because a discussion took place between it and the other group of forbidders who withdrew, then in reality they are one group, since they are united in forbidding, withdrawing, and salvation from transformation.

Among the reports from al-Firyabi and Ibn Abi Hatim, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Moses said, "My Lord, I find a community whose Gospels are in their hearts." He said, "That is a community that will come after you: the community of Ahmad (ﷺ)." He said, "My Lord, I find a community who pray the five (prayers), which are expiations for what lies between them." He said, "That is a community that will come after you: the community of Ahmad (ﷺ)." He said, "My Lord, I find a community who give the charity of their wealth, then it returns to them and they eat it." He said, "That is [a community] after you: the community of Ahmad (ﷺ)." He said, "My Lord, make me one of the community of Ahmad (ﷺ)." So Allah revealed, in a manner that pleased Moses, ﴿And among the people of Moses is a community who guide by the truth and by it do justice﴾.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying ﴿And among the people of Moses is a community﴾ and the rest of the verse, that he said: "It has reached me that the Children of Israel, when they killed their prophets and disbelieved, and they were twelve tribes (asbat), one tribe disassociated itself from what they had done, made an excuse, and asked Allah to separate them from them. So Allah opened for them a tunnel (nafaq) in the earth, and they travelled through it until they emerged from beyond China. There they are upright (hunafa') Muslims, facing our qibla."

Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "That is His saying: ﴿And We said after him to the Children of Israel, 'Dwell in the land, and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you together as a mixed multitude﴾ [al-Isra' 17:104]. And the promise of the Hereafter is 'Isa ibn Maryam."

Ibn 'Abbas said: "They travelled in the tunnel (sarb) for a year and a half."

I say: A report as strange and remarkable as this needs verification of its transmission.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: "After Moses, the Children of Israel split into seventy-one sects, all of them in the Fire except one sect. The Christians split after 'Isa into seventy-two sects, all of them in the Fire except one sect. This community will certainly split into seventy-three sects, all of them in the Fire except one sect. As for the Jews, Allah says: ﴿And among the people of Moses is a community who guide by the truth and by it do justice﴾, so this is the one that will be saved. As for the Christians, Allah says: ﴿Among them is a moderate community﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:66], so this is the one that will be saved. As for us, He says: ﴿And among those whom We created is a community who guide by the truth and by it do justice﴾ [al-A'raf 7:181], so this is the one that will be saved from this community."

We have already mentioned that the addition "all of them in the Fire" is not authentically established, neither as a marfu' (attributed to the Prophet) nor as a mawquf (attributed to a Companion).

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿fanbajasat﴾ [gushed forth], that he said: "﴿fanfajarat﴾ [burst forth]."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from 'Ikrimah, who said: "I entered upon Ibn 'Abbas while he was reciting this verse: ﴿And ask them about the town that was by the sea﴾. He said: 'O 'Ikrimah, do you know what town this is?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'It is Aylah.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from al-Zuhri, who said: "It is Tiberias."

Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿when they transgressed in the Sabbath﴾, that he said: "They wronged."

Ibn Jarir reported from him regarding His saying ﴿shurra'an﴾ [appearing in abundance], he said: "He means from every place."

Ibn Jarir also reported from him, who said: "Floating upon the water."

Ibn al-Mundhir reported from him, who said: "Coming in."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from him regarding the verse, who said: "It is a town on the shore of the sea between Egypt and Madinah, called Aylah. Allah forbade them the fish on their Sabbath day, and they would come to them on their Sabbath day, appearing in abundance on the shore of the sea. But when the Sabbath day had passed, they could not catch them. They remained like this for as long as Allah willed. Then a group of them took the fish on their Sabbath day. A group admonished them, but they only increased in misguidance. A group of those who forbade said, knowing that these were a people upon whom the punishment was due: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy?﴾ They were more angry than the other group, and all of them had been forbidding. When the wrath of Allah befell them, the two groups who said ﴿Why do you admonish?﴾ and those who said ﴿as an excuse before your Lord﴾ were saved, and Allah destroyed the people of His disobedience who had taken the fish, and He transformed them into apes."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from him that they were three groups: the group of the sinners, the group of those who forbade, and the group who said ﴿Why do you admonish?﴾. "Only those who forbade were saved, and the rest perished. Then one morning those who had forbidden found themselves in their gatherings searching for the people and not seeing them. They had spent the night and locked their houses behind them. So they began to say: 'Surely something has happened to the people. Look into their affairs.' They looked into their houses, and behold, the people had been transformed: they recognised the man by his eye, and he was an ape, and the woman by her eye, and she was an ape."

'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan reported from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, and he mentioned the story, and at its end he said: "I see that those who forbade were saved, and I do not see that the others were mentioned. And we see things that we disapprove of, but we do not say anything about them."

'Ikrimah said: "I said: 'May Allah make me your ransom, do you not see that they disliked what they were upon and opposed them, and said: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy?﴾'" He said: "He then ordered that I be clothed in two thick garments."

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn 'Abbas, also, who said: "Those who forbade evil were saved, and those who committed it perished, and I do not know what was done to those who remained silent."

'Abd ibn Humayd and Abu al-Shaykh reported from him, who said: "By Allah, if I knew that the people who said ﴿Why do you admonish a people?﴾ were saved along with those who forbade evil, it would be dearer to me than what I would exchange it for."

In another wording: "than red camels. But I fear that the punishment descended upon them all."

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir reported from 'Ikrimah, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "I do not know whether those who said ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy?﴾ were saved or not." He said: "I kept looking at him until he realised that they had been saved, and he clothed me in a robe."

'Abd ibn Humayd reported from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, who said: "Those who said ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy?﴾ were transformed into stones."

'Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿with a severe punishment (bi-'adhabin ba'is)﴾, that he said: "Painful and grievous."

(p. 506) His words: ﴿And among the people of Moses﴾. When Allah had related to us what had happened with the Samiri and his companions, and the instability in religion that occurred among the Children of Israel, He, glory be to Him, related to us that among the people of Moses there was a community that opposed those previously mentioned. They are described as ﴿guiding by the truth﴾, meaning they call people to guidance while being characterized by the truth, ﴿and by it they act justly﴾, meaning they judge fairly among people. It was said that they include those among them who believed in Muhammad (ﷺ).

His words: ﴿And We divided them into twelve tribes﴾. The pronoun refers to the people of Moses mentioned earlier, not to this community among them who guide by the truth and act justly by it. The meaning is: We made them separate groups and distinguished some of them from others. This is among the blessings that Allah related to us which He bestowed upon the Children of Israel. The meaning is that He distinguished some of them from others until they became tribes, each tribe known on its own, and each tribe had a leader (naqib, chief), as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We raised from among them twelve leaders﴾, which has already been discussed.

His words: ﴿twelve﴾ is the second object of qatta'na (divided), because it implies the meaning of "making" (tasyir). ﴿Tribes (asbatan)﴾ is either a specification (tamyiz) for it or a substitute (badal) for it, or ﴿nations (umaman)﴾ is an attribute of asbat or a substitute for it. Asbat is the plural of sibt, which means the son's son (grandson). They became twelve nations from twelve sons. By asbat he meant tribes, and for this reason the number is feminine, as in the words of the poet:

*And indeed Quraysh, all of it, is ten clans,*
*and you are innocent of its ten tribes.*

Here "clan" (batn) means tribe. The verification of the meaning of asbat has already been discussed in al-Baqarah. Al-Mufaddal narrated from ʿAsim that he recited "qatta'nahum" with a light pronunciation (without the doubled letter). He called them "nations" because each tribe was a large group of people, and they had differing opinions, one leading in a direction different from the other.

﴿And We revealed to Moses when his people asked him for water﴾, that is, at the time they asked him for water when thirst afflicted them in the wilderness, saying: ﴿Strike the rock with your staff﴾. This is an explanation (tafsir) of the act of revelation. ﴿So it burst forth﴾ is a conjunction with an implied element indicated by the context: that is, he struck, and it burst forth. Inbijas means gushing forth; that is, from it twelve springs gushed forth, according to the number of tribes, with each tribe having a spring from which they drank. ﴿Every people knew its drinking place﴾, meaning each tribe knew the specific spring from which it drank. What was said about this in al-Baqarah is sufficient and makes repetition unnecessary.

﴿And We shaded them with clouds﴾, meaning We made them shade over them in the wilderness; it moved with their movement and stopped with their stopping. ﴿And We sent down upon them manna and quails﴾, that is, the honey-like substance (tarnjabin) and the quail (as-samani), as its verification has already been discussed in al-Baqarah. ﴿Eat of the good things We have provided for you﴾, meaning We said to them: eat of the delicious things We have provided for you. ﴿And they did not wrong Us﴾ by what they did of disobedience, ingratitude for blessings, and failure to appreciate them as they should. ﴿But they were wronging themselves﴾, meaning their wrongdoing was confined to themselves and did not extend beyond them to others.

﴿And when it was said to them﴾, that is, remember the time when this statement was said to them: ﴿Dwell in this town﴾, meaning Bayt al-Maqdis or Jericho; it was said that it is other than that, which has already been explained. ﴿And eat from it﴾, meaning from the foods found in it. ﴿Wherever you wish﴾, meaning in any place of its places that you wish, with no prohibition on you to eat there. ﴿And say: Hittah (forgiveness)﴾, whose explanation has already been given in al-Baqarah. ﴿And enter the gate﴾, meaning the gate of the aforementioned town, while you are ﴿prostrating﴾. They were commanded to combine their saying "hittah" with entering while prostrating. So it is not said: how did He put the command to speak here before entering, and delay it in al-Baqarah? The meaning of the prostration they were commanded to perform has already been explained. ﴿We will forgive you your sins﴾ is the answer to the command.

It was also recited as "khatiyatakum" (singular). Then He promised them with His words: ﴿We will increase the good-doers﴾, meaning We will increase them beyond the forgiveness of sins with what is bestowed upon them of blessings. The sentence is a new independent clause, an answer to an implied question, as if it was said: what then is for them after forgiveness? ﴿But those who did wrong among them changed the word from what had been said to them﴾, the explanation of which has already been given in al-Baqarah. ﴿So We sent upon them a punishment (rijz) from the sky﴾, meaning a punishment coming from it ﴿because they were wronging﴾, meaning because of their wrongdoing.

His words: 163. ﴿And ask them about the town which was by the sea﴾. It is conjoined to the implied governing element of "idh": that is, remember when it was said to them, and ask them. This is a question of rebuke and reproach. By asking about the town is meant asking its people: that is, ask them about this event that happened to them there, which contradicted what Allah had commanded them.

Within this question is a great benefit: it informs the Jews that this is something known to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and that his knowledge of it could only come through information given to him by Allah, glory be to Him, and thus it is evidence of his truthfulness.

The people of tafsir differed about this town: which town was it? It was said: Aylah; it was said: Tiberias; it was said: Madyan; it was said: Iliya; and it was said: a town among the towns of the Syrian coast which was "by the sea", that is, which was near the sea. It is said: "I was in the presence (hadrah) of the house," meaning near it.

The meaning is: O Muhammad, ask these present Jews about the story of the people of the aforementioned town.

It was recited "wa-s'alhum" and also "sal-hum". ﴿When they transgressed (idh ya'dun)﴾, meaning at the time they transgressed. It is an adverbial of time governed by an implied element indicated by the speech, because the question concerns their condition and their story at the time they transgressed. It was also said that it is an adverbial of time for "kanat" (was) or for "hadirah" (presence).

It was recited "yu'iddun" with a damma on the yā' and a kasra on the ʿayn and a shadda on the dāl, from al-i'dad (preparation), meaning the instrument.

The majority recited "ya'dun" with a fatha on the yā', a sukun on the ʿayn and a damma on the dāl, without shadda: that is, they overstep Allah's limits by hunting on the Sabbath day, on which they were forbidden from fishing. It was also recited "ya'addun" with a fatha on the yā' and the ʿayn and a damma on the dāl with shadda, meaning ya'tadun (transgress), the tā' being assimilated into the dāl.

As-sabt is the well-known day, and its root meaning is rest; it is said: sabata when he rested. Sabata the Jews meant they abandoned work on their Sabbath. Its plural is asbut, sabut, and asbat. Ibn as-Sumayfa' recited "fi al-asbat" in the plural.

﴿When their fish came to them﴾ (part 2 of the verse's explanation) is an adverbial of time governed by "ya'dun".

Al-hitan is the plural of hut (fish), and it was attributed to them to emphasize their special connection to those of them that came in this manner, coming on the Sabbath day and not on other days. "On their Sabbath day" is an adverbial of time for "ta'tihim" (come to them).

It was recited "yawma asbatihim". "Shurra'an" is a circumstantial accusative (hal), and it is the plural of shari': that is, visible on the water. It was said: raising their heads; and it was said: they used to come forward at their doorways like white rams.

In al-Kashshaf it is said: "shara'a 'alayna fulan" means when so-and-so approached us and came up over us, and "shara'tu 'ala fulan fi baytihi fa-ra'aytuhu yaf'alu kadha" means I looked in on so-and-so in his house and saw him doing such-and-such, end of quote.

﴿And on the day they did not keep the Sabbath, they did not come to them﴾, meaning they did not observe the Sabbath; on the day after the Sabbath ended, the fish would not come to them, as they used to come on the Sabbath day. ﴿Thus did We test them﴾, meaning like that great trial We tested them because of their defiance. Ibtila' means trial and examination.

﴿And when a community said﴾ is conjoined to ﴿when they transgressed﴾, governed by its governing element and within its ruling. Ummah means a group: that is, a group of the righteous people of the town said to others among those who used to strive to admonish the transgressors on the Sabbath, when they had despaired of their accepting admonition and giving up disobedience: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy﴾, meaning who are destined for punishment ﴿or punish them with a severe punishment﴾ for the sacred things they violated and the disobedience they committed. It was said that the group saying "why do you admonish a people" were the disobedient who hunted on the Sabbath; they said this to those who admonished them when they admonished them.

The meaning: if you know that Allah is going to destroy us, as you claim, then why do you admonish us? They said: ﴿An excuse to your Lord﴾, meaning the admonishers said to the group who said to them "why do you admonish": they are a group of the righteous people of the town according to the first interpretation, or the doers (of the sin) according to the second. ﴿An excuse to your Lord﴾: ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar and Talhah ibn Musarrif recited "ma'dhiratan" in the accusative, which is the recitation of Hafs from ʿAsim; the rest recited it in the nominative.

Al-Kisa'i said: its accusative has two possibilities: one of them is as a verbal noun (masdar), and the second is by the implied meaning "we did that as an excuse," that is, for the sake of the excuse.

The nominative is by an implied subject: that is, our admonition is an excuse to Allah, so that He will not hold us accountable for abandoning the commanding of good and forbidding of evil which He made obligatory upon us, and in hope that they might take heed, fear Allah, and give up what they are engaged in of disobedience.

The majority of the commentators said: the Children of Israel split into three groups. One group disobeyed and hunted, and they were about seventy thousand. One group withdrew and did not admonish and did not disobey. And one group withdrew and admonished and did not disobey. The group that did not admonish and did not disobey said to the admonishing group: ﴿Why do you admonish a people﴾, meaning the disobedient group, ﴿whom Allah is going to destroy or punish?﴾ They said this based on the strong presumption according to Allah's custom of destroying or punishing the disobedient without total annihilation. The admonishing group said: our admonition is an excuse to Allah, ﴿and perhaps they will fear Allah﴾. If they had been only two groups, the admonishing non-disobedient group and the disobedient group, he would have said: "perhaps you will fear Allah."

His words: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾, meaning when the disobedient people of the town left what the righteous who forbid evil had reminded them of, leaving like one who forgets a thing and turns away from it completely. ﴿We saved those who forbade evil﴾, meaning those who performed the forbidding and did not abandon it. ﴿And We seized those who did wrong﴾, and they were the transgressors who exceeded the limits on the Sabbath, ﴿with a grievous punishment (bi'sin)﴾, meaning a severe one, from ba'usa (to be severe) when a thing is harsh. There are eleven recitations of this word by the Seven and others. ﴿Because they were defiantly disobedient﴾, meaning because of their defiance. The prepositional phrase is connected to "akhadhna" (We seized).

﴿So when they insolently persisted in what they had been forbidden﴾, meaning they exceeded the limit in disobedience to Allah, glory be to Him, out of rebelliousness and arrogance. ﴿We said to them: Be apes, despised﴾, meaning We commanded them with a creational command, not a verbal command: that is, We transformed them into apes. It was said: He, glory be to Him, first punished them for their disobedience, and when they did not give up, He transformed them into apes. It was also said: His words "So when they insolently persisted in what they had been forbidden" are a repetition of His words "So when they forgot what they had been reminded of," for emphasis and affirmation, and that the transformation is the grievous punishment. "Khasi'in" means abject, humiliated, or distanced and expelled. It is said: "khasa'tuhu fakhusi'a," meaning I pushed him away and he withdrew.

Know that the apparent meaning of the Qur'anic text is that none were saved from the punishment except the forbidding group which did not disobey, according to His words: ﴿We saved those who forbade evil﴾, and that none were punished by transformation except the disobedient group, according to His words: ﴿So when they insolently persisted in what they had been forbidden, We said to them: Be apes, despised﴾. If the groups among them were three as previously mentioned, then the group that did not forbid and did not disobey may possibly have been transformed along with the disobedient group, because they wronged themselves by staying silent about the prohibition and were insolent toward what Allah had forbidden them, namely abandoning the forbidding of evil. And it is possible that they were not transformed, because although they wronged themselves and were insolent toward their Lord's command and prohibition, they did not wrong themselves by this specific sin, which is hunting the fish on the Sabbath day, nor were they insolent toward His prohibition to them against hunting. As for when the third group was forbidding like the second group, and was only made a separate group because a discussion took place between it and the other group of forbidders who withdrew, then in reality they are one group, since they are united in forbidding, withdrawing, and salvation from transformation.

Among the reports from al-Firyabi and Ibn Abi Hatim, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Moses said, "My Lord, I find a community whose Gospels are in their hearts." He said, "That is a community that will come after you: the community of Ahmad (ﷺ)." He said, "My Lord, I find a community who pray the five (prayers), which are expiations for what lies between them." He said, "That is a community that will come after you: the community of Ahmad (ﷺ)." He said, "My Lord, I find a community who give the charity of their wealth, then it returns to them and they eat it." He said, "That is [a community] after you: the community of Ahmad (ﷺ)." He said, "My Lord, make me one of the community of Ahmad (ﷺ)." So Allah revealed, in a manner that pleased Moses, ﴿And among the people of Moses is a community who guide by the truth and by it do justice﴾.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying ﴿And among the people of Moses is a community﴾ and the rest of the verse, that he said: "It has reached me that the Children of Israel, when they killed their prophets and disbelieved, and they were twelve tribes (asbat), one tribe disassociated itself from what they had done, made an excuse, and asked Allah to separate them from them. So Allah opened for them a tunnel (nafaq) in the earth, and they travelled through it until they emerged from beyond China. There they are upright (hunafa') Muslims, facing our qibla."

Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "That is His saying: ﴿And We said after him to the Children of Israel, 'Dwell in the land, and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you together as a mixed multitude﴾ [al-Isra' 17:104]. And the promise of the Hereafter is 'Isa ibn Maryam."

Ibn 'Abbas said: "They travelled in the tunnel (sarb) for a year and a half."

I say: A report as strange and remarkable as this needs verification of its transmission.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: "After Moses, the Children of Israel split into seventy-one sects, all of them in the Fire except one sect. The Christians split after 'Isa into seventy-two sects, all of them in the Fire except one sect. This community will certainly split into seventy-three sects, all of them in the Fire except one sect. As for the Jews, Allah says: ﴿And among the people of Moses is a community who guide by the truth and by it do justice﴾, so this is the one that will be saved. As for the Christians, Allah says: ﴿Among them is a moderate community﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:66], so this is the one that will be saved. As for us, He says: ﴿And among those whom We created is a community who guide by the truth and by it do justice﴾ [al-A'raf 7:181], so this is the one that will be saved from this community."

We have already mentioned that the addition "all of them in the Fire" is not authentically established, neither as a marfu' (attributed to the Prophet) nor as a mawquf (attributed to a Companion).

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿fanbajasat﴾ [gushed forth], that he said: "﴿fanfajarat﴾ [burst forth]."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from 'Ikrimah, who said: "I entered upon Ibn 'Abbas while he was reciting this verse: ﴿And ask them about the town that was by the sea﴾. He said: 'O 'Ikrimah, do you know what town this is?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'It is Aylah.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from al-Zuhri, who said: "It is Tiberias."

Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿when they transgressed in the Sabbath﴾, that he said: "They wronged."

Ibn Jarir reported from him regarding His saying ﴿shurra'an﴾ [appearing in abundance], he said: "He means from every place."

Ibn Jarir also reported from him, who said: "Floating upon the water."

Ibn al-Mundhir reported from him, who said: "Coming in."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from him regarding the verse, who said: "It is a town on the shore of the sea between Egypt and Madinah, called Aylah. Allah forbade them the fish on their Sabbath day, and they would come to them on their Sabbath day, appearing in abundance on the shore of the sea. But when the Sabbath day had passed, they could not catch them. They remained like this for as long as Allah willed. Then a group of them took the fish on their Sabbath day. A group admonished them, but they only increased in misguidance. A group of those who forbade said, knowing that these were a people upon whom the punishment was due: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy?﴾ They were more angry than the other group, and all of them had been forbidding. When the wrath of Allah befell them, the two groups who said ﴿Why do you admonish?﴾ and those who said ﴿as an excuse before your Lord﴾ were saved, and Allah destroyed the people of His disobedience who had taken the fish, and He transformed them into apes."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from him that they were three groups: the group of the sinners, the group of those who forbade, and the group who said ﴿Why do you admonish?﴾. "Only those who forbade were saved, and the rest perished. Then one morning those who had forbidden found themselves in their gatherings searching for the people and not seeing them. They had spent the night and locked their houses behind them. So they began to say: 'Surely something has happened to the people. Look into their affairs.' They looked into their houses, and behold, the people had been transformed: they recognised the man by his eye, and he was an ape, and the woman by her eye, and she was an ape."

'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan reported from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, and he mentioned the story, and at its end he said: "I see that those who forbade were saved, and I do not see that the others were mentioned. And we see things that we disapprove of, but we do not say anything about them."

'Ikrimah said: "I said: 'May Allah make me your ransom, do you not see that they disliked what they were upon and opposed them, and said: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy?﴾'" He said: "He then ordered that I be clothed in two thick garments."

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn 'Abbas, also, who said: "Those who forbade evil were saved, and those who committed it perished, and I do not know what was done to those who remained silent."

'Abd ibn Humayd and Abu al-Shaykh reported from him, who said: "By Allah, if I knew that the people who said ﴿Why do you admonish a people?﴾ were saved along with those who forbade evil, it would be dearer to me than what I would exchange it for."

In another wording: "than red camels. But I fear that the punishment descended upon them all."

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir reported from 'Ikrimah, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "I do not know whether those who said ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy?﴾ were saved or not." He said: "I kept looking at him until he realised that they had been saved, and he clothed me in a robe."

'Abd ibn Humayd reported from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, who said: "Those who said ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy?﴾ were transformed into stones."

'Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿with a severe punishment (bi-'adhabin ba'is)﴾, that he said: "Painful and grievous."

(p. 506) His words: ﴿And among the people of Moses﴾. When Allah had related to us what had happened with the Samiri and his companions, and the instability in religion that occurred among the Children of Israel, He, glory be to Him, related to us that among the people of Moses there was a community that opposed those previously mentioned. They are described as ﴿guiding by the truth﴾, meaning they call people to guidance while being characterized by the truth, ﴿and by it they act justly﴾, meaning they judge fairly among people. It was said that they include those among them who believed in Muhammad (ﷺ).

His words: ﴿And We divided them into twelve tribes﴾. The pronoun refers to the people of Moses mentioned earlier, not to this community among them who guide by the truth and act justly by it. The meaning is: We made them separate groups and distinguished some of them from others. This is among the blessings that Allah related to us which He bestowed upon the Children of Israel. The meaning is that He distinguished some of them from others until they became tribes, each tribe known on its own, and each tribe had a leader (naqib, chief), as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We raised from among them twelve leaders﴾, which has already been discussed.

His words: ﴿twelve﴾ is the second object of qatta'na (divided), because it implies the meaning of "making" (tasyir). ﴿Tribes (asbatan)﴾ is either a specification (tamyiz) for it or a substitute (badal) for it, or ﴿nations (umaman)﴾ is an attribute of asbat or a substitute for it. Asbat is the plural of sibt, which means the son's son (grandson). They became twelve nations from twelve sons. By asbat he meant tribes, and for this reason the number is feminine, as in the words of the poet:

*And indeed Quraysh, all of it, is ten clans,*
*and you are innocent of its ten tribes.*

Here "clan" (batn) means tribe. The verification of the meaning of asbat has already been discussed in al-Baqarah. Al-Mufaddal narrated from ʿAsim that he recited "qatta'nahum" with a light pronunciation (without the doubled letter). He called them "nations" because each tribe was a large group of people, and they had differing opinions, one leading in a direction different from the other.

﴿And We revealed to Moses when his people asked him for water﴾, that is, at the time they asked him for water when thirst afflicted them in the wilderness, saying: ﴿Strike the rock with your staff﴾. This is an explanation (tafsir) of the act of revelation. ﴿So it burst forth﴾ is a conjunction with an implied element indicated by the context: that is, he struck, and it burst forth. Inbijas means gushing forth; that is, from it twelve springs gushed forth, according to the number of tribes, with each tribe having a spring from which they drank. ﴿Every people knew its drinking place﴾, meaning each tribe knew the specific spring from which it drank. What was said about this in al-Baqarah is sufficient and makes repetition unnecessary.

﴿And We shaded them with clouds﴾, meaning We made them shade over them in the wilderness; it moved with their movement and stopped with their stopping. ﴿And We sent down upon them manna and quails﴾, that is, the honey-like substance (tarnjabin) and the quail (as-samani), as its verification has already been discussed in al-Baqarah. ﴿Eat of the good things We have provided for you﴾, meaning We said to them: eat of the delicious things We have provided for you. ﴿And they did not wrong Us﴾ by what they did of disobedience, ingratitude for blessings, and failure to appreciate them as they should. ﴿But they were wronging themselves﴾, meaning their wrongdoing was confined to themselves and did not extend beyond them to others.

﴿And when it was said to them﴾, that is, remember the time when this statement was said to them: ﴿Dwell in this town﴾, meaning Bayt al-Maqdis or Jericho; it was said that it is other than that, which has already been explained. ﴿And eat from it﴾, meaning from the foods found in it. ﴿Wherever you wish﴾, meaning in any place of its places that you wish, with no prohibition on you to eat there. ﴿And say: Hittah (forgiveness)﴾, whose explanation has already been given in al-Baqarah. ﴿And enter the gate﴾, meaning the gate of the aforementioned town, while you are ﴿prostrating﴾. They were commanded to combine their saying "hittah" with entering while prostrating. So it is not said: how did He put the command to speak here before entering, and delay it in al-Baqarah? The meaning of the prostration they were commanded to perform has already been explained. ﴿We will forgive you your sins﴾ is the answer to the command.

It was also recited as "khatiyatakum" (singular). Then He promised them with His words: ﴿We will increase the good-doers﴾, meaning We will increase them beyond the forgiveness of sins with what is bestowed upon them of blessings. The sentence is a new independent clause, an answer to an implied question, as if it was said: what then is for them after forgiveness? ﴿But those who did wrong among them changed the word from what had been said to them﴾, the explanation of which has already been given in al-Baqarah. ﴿So We sent upon them a punishment (rijz) from the sky﴾, meaning a punishment coming from it ﴿because they were wronging﴾, meaning because of their wrongdoing.

His words: 163. ﴿And ask them about the town which was by the sea﴾. It is conjoined to the implied governing element of "idh": that is, remember when it was said to them, and ask them. This is a question of rebuke and reproach. By asking about the town is meant asking its people: that is, ask them about this event that happened to them there, which contradicted what Allah had commanded them.

Within this question is a great benefit: it informs the Jews that this is something known to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and that his knowledge of it could only come through information given to him by Allah, glory be to Him, and thus it is evidence of his truthfulness.

The people of tafsir differed about this town: which town was it? It was said: Aylah; it was said: Tiberias; it was said: Madyan; it was said: Iliya; and it was said: a town among the towns of the Syrian coast which was "by the sea", that is, which was near the sea. It is said: "I was in the presence (hadrah) of the house," meaning near it.

The meaning is: O Muhammad, ask these present Jews about the story of the people of the aforementioned town.

It was recited "wa-s'alhum" and also "sal-hum". ﴿When they transgressed (idh ya'dun)﴾, meaning at the time they transgressed. It is an adverbial of time governed by an implied element indicated by the speech, because the question concerns their condition and their story at the time they transgressed. It was also said that it is an adverbial of time for "kanat" (was) or for "hadirah" (presence).

It was recited "yu'iddun" with a damma on the yā' and a kasra on the ʿayn and a shadda on the dāl, from al-i'dad (preparation), meaning the instrument.

The majority recited "ya'dun" with a fatha on the yā', a sukun on the ʿayn and a damma on the dāl, without shadda: that is, they overstep Allah's limits by hunting on the Sabbath day, on which they were forbidden from fishing. It was also recited "ya'addun" with a fatha on the yā' and the ʿayn and a damma on the dāl with shadda, meaning ya'tadun (transgress), the tā' being assimilated into the dāl.

As-sabt is the well-known day, and its root meaning is rest; it is said: sabata when he rested. Sabata the Jews meant they abandoned work on their Sabbath. Its plural is asbut, sabut, and asbat. Ibn as-Sumayfa' recited "fi al-asbat" in the plural.

﴿When their fish came to them﴾ (part 2 of the verse's explanation) is an adverbial of time governed by "ya'dun".

Al-hitan is the plural of hut (fish), and it was attributed to them to emphasize their special connection to those of them that came in this manner, coming on the Sabbath day and not on other days. "On their Sabbath day" is an adverbial of time for "ta'tihim" (come to them).

It was recited "yawma asbatihim". "Shurra'an" is a circumstantial accusative (hal), and it is the plural of shari': that is, visible on the water. It was said: raising their heads; and it was said: they used to come forward at their doorways like white rams.

In al-Kashshaf it is said: "shara'a 'alayna fulan" means when so-and-so approached us and came up over us, and "shara'tu 'ala fulan fi baytihi fa-ra'aytuhu yaf'alu kadha" means I looked in on so-and-so in his house and saw him doing such-and-such, end of quote.

﴿And on the day they did not keep the Sabbath, they did not come to them﴾, meaning they did not observe the Sabbath; on the day after the Sabbath ended, the fish would not come to them, as they used to come on the Sabbath day. ﴿Thus did We test them﴾, meaning like that great trial We tested them because of their defiance. Ibtila' means trial and examination.

﴿And when a community said﴾ is conjoined to ﴿when they transgressed﴾, governed by its governing element and within its ruling. Ummah means a group: that is, a group of the righteous people of the town said to others among those who used to strive to admonish the transgressors on the Sabbath, when they had despaired of their accepting admonition and giving up disobedience: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy﴾, meaning who are destined for punishment ﴿or punish them with a severe punishment﴾ for the sacred things they violated and the disobedience they committed. It was said that the group saying "why do you admonish a people" were the disobedient who hunted on the Sabbath; they said this to those who admonished them when they admonished them.

The meaning: if you know that Allah is going to destroy us, as you claim, then why do you admonish us? They said: ﴿An excuse to your Lord﴾, meaning the admonishers said to the group who said to them "why do you admonish": they are a group of the righteous people of the town according to the first interpretation, or the doers (of the sin) according to the second. ﴿An excuse to your Lord﴾: ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar and Talhah ibn Musarrif recited "ma'dhiratan" in the accusative, which is the recitation of Hafs from ʿAsim; the rest recited it in the nominative.

Al-Kisa'i said: its accusative has two possibilities: one of them is as a verbal noun (masdar), and the second is by the implied meaning "we did that as an excuse," that is, for the sake of the excuse.

The nominative is by an implied subject: that is, our admonition is an excuse to Allah, so that He will not hold us accountable for abandoning the commanding of good and forbidding of evil which He made obligatory upon us, and in hope that they might take heed, fear Allah, and give up what they are engaged in of disobedience.

The majority of the commentators said: the Children of Israel split into three groups. One group disobeyed and hunted, and they were about seventy thousand. One group withdrew and did not admonish and did not disobey. And one group withdrew and admonished and did not disobey. The group that did not admonish and did not disobey said to the admonishing group: ﴿Why do you admonish a people﴾, meaning the disobedient group, ﴿whom Allah is going to destroy or punish?﴾ They said this based on the strong presumption according to Allah's custom of destroying or punishing the disobedient without total annihilation. The admonishing group said: our admonition is an excuse to Allah, ﴿and perhaps they will fear Allah﴾. If they had been only two groups, the admonishing non-disobedient group and the disobedient group, he would have said: "perhaps you will fear Allah."

His words: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾, meaning when the disobedient people of the town left what the righteous who forbid evil had reminded them of, leaving like one who forgets a thing and turns away from it completely. ﴿We saved those who forbade evil﴾, meaning those who performed the forbidding and did not abandon it. ﴿And We seized those who did wrong﴾, and they were the transgressors who exceeded the limits on the Sabbath, ﴿with a grievous punishment (bi'sin)﴾, meaning a severe one, from ba'usa (to be severe) when a thing is harsh. There are eleven recitations of this word by the Seven and others. ﴿Because they were defiantly disobedient﴾, meaning because of their defiance. The prepositional phrase is connected to "akhadhna" (We seized).

﴿So when they insolently persisted in what they had been forbidden﴾, meaning they exceeded the limit in disobedience to Allah, glory be to Him, out of rebelliousness and arrogance. ﴿We said to them: Be apes, despised﴾, meaning We commanded them with a creational command, not a verbal command: that is, We transformed them into apes. It was said: He, glory be to Him, first punished them for their disobedience, and when they did not give up, He transformed them into apes. It was also said: His words "So when they insolently persisted in what they had been forbidden" are a repetition of His words "So when they forgot what they had been reminded of," for emphasis and affirmation, and that the transformation is the grievous punishment. "Khasi'in" means abject, humiliated, or distanced and expelled. It is said: "khasa'tuhu fakhusi'a," meaning I pushed him away and he withdrew.

Know that the apparent meaning of the Qur'anic text is that none were saved from the punishment except the forbidding group which did not disobey, according to His words: ﴿We saved those who forbade evil﴾, and that none were punished by transformation except the disobedient group, according to His words: ﴿So when they insolently persisted in what they had been forbidden, We said to them: Be apes, despised﴾. If the groups among them were three as previously mentioned, then the group that did not forbid and did not disobey may possibly have been transformed along with the disobedient group, because they wronged themselves by staying silent about the prohibition and were insolent toward what Allah had forbidden them, namely abandoning the forbidding of evil. And it is possible that they were not transformed, because although they wronged themselves and were insolent toward their Lord's command and prohibition, they did not wrong themselves by this specific sin, which is hunting the fish on the Sabbath day, nor were they insolent toward His prohibition to them against hunting. As for when the third group was forbidding like the second group, and was only made a separate group because a discussion took place between it and the other group of forbidders who withdrew, then in reality they are one group, since they are united in forbidding, withdrawing, and salvation from transformation.

Among the reports from al-Firyabi and Ibn Abi Hatim, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Moses said, "My Lord, I find a community whose Gospels are in their hearts." He said, "That is a community that will come after you: the community of Ahmad (ﷺ)." He said, "My Lord, I find a community who pray the five (prayers), which are expiations for what lies between them." He said, "That is a community that will come after you: the community of Ahmad (ﷺ)." He said, "My Lord, I find a community who give the charity of their wealth, then it returns to them and they eat it." He said, "That is [a community] after you: the community of Ahmad (ﷺ)." He said, "My Lord, make me one of the community of Ahmad (ﷺ)." So Allah revealed, in a manner that pleased Moses, ﴿And among the people of Moses is a community who guide by the truth and by it do justice﴾.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying ﴿And among the people of Moses is a community﴾ and the rest of the verse, that he said: "It has reached me that the Children of Israel, when they killed their prophets and disbelieved, and they were twelve tribes (asbat), one tribe disassociated itself from what they had done, made an excuse, and asked Allah to separate them from them. So Allah opened for them a tunnel (nafaq) in the earth, and they travelled through it until they emerged from beyond China. There they are upright (hunafa') Muslims, facing our qibla."

Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "That is His saying: ﴿And We said after him to the Children of Israel, 'Dwell in the land, and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you together as a mixed multitude﴾ [al-Isra' 17:104]. And the promise of the Hereafter is 'Isa ibn Maryam."

Ibn 'Abbas said: "They travelled in the tunnel (sarb) for a year and a half."

I say: A report as strange and remarkable as this needs verification of its transmission.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: "After Moses, the Children of Israel split into seventy-one sects, all of them in the Fire except one sect. The Christians split after 'Isa into seventy-two sects, all of them in the Fire except one sect. This community will certainly split into seventy-three sects, all of them in the Fire except one sect. As for the Jews, Allah says: ﴿And among the people of Moses is a community who guide by the truth and by it do justice﴾, so this is the one that will be saved. As for the Christians, Allah says: ﴿Among them is a moderate community﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:66], so this is the one that will be saved. As for us, He says: ﴿And among those whom We created is a community who guide by the truth and by it do justice﴾ [al-A'raf 7:181], so this is the one that will be saved from this community."

We have already mentioned that the addition "all of them in the Fire" is not authentically established, neither as a marfu' (attributed to the Prophet) nor as a mawquf (attributed to a Companion).

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿fanbajasat﴾ [gushed forth], that he said: "﴿fanfajarat﴾ [burst forth]."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from 'Ikrimah, who said: "I entered upon Ibn 'Abbas while he was reciting this verse: ﴿And ask them about the town that was by the sea﴾. He said: 'O 'Ikrimah, do you know what town this is?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'It is Aylah.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from al-Zuhri, who said: "It is Tiberias."

Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿when they transgressed in the Sabbath﴾, that he said: "They wronged."

Ibn Jarir reported from him regarding His saying ﴿shurra'an﴾ [appearing in abundance], he said: "He means from every place."

Ibn Jarir also reported from him, who said: "Floating upon the water."

Ibn al-Mundhir reported from him, who said: "Coming in."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from him regarding the verse, who said: "It is a town on the shore of the sea between Egypt and Madinah, called Aylah. Allah forbade them the fish on their Sabbath day, and they would come to them on their Sabbath day, appearing in abundance on the shore of the sea. But when the Sabbath day had passed, they could not catch them. They remained like this for as long as Allah willed. Then a group of them took the fish on their Sabbath day. A group admonished them, but they only increased in misguidance. A group of those who forbade said, knowing that these were a people upon whom the punishment was due: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy?﴾ They were more angry than the other group, and all of them had been forbidding. When the wrath of Allah befell them, the two groups who said ﴿Why do you admonish?﴾ and those who said ﴿as an excuse before your Lord﴾ were saved, and Allah destroyed the people of His disobedience who had taken the fish, and He transformed them into apes."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from him that they were three groups: the group of the sinners, the group of those who forbade, and the group who said ﴿Why do you admonish?﴾. "Only those who forbade were saved, and the rest perished. Then one morning those who had forbidden found themselves in their gatherings searching for the people and not seeing them. They had spent the night and locked their houses behind them. So they began to say: 'Surely something has happened to the people. Look into their affairs.' They looked into their houses, and behold, the people had been transformed: they recognised the man by his eye, and he was an ape, and the woman by her eye, and she was an ape."

'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan reported from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, and he mentioned the story, and at its end he said: "I see that those who forbade were saved, and I do not see that the others were mentioned. And we see things that we disapprove of, but we do not say anything about them."

'Ikrimah said: "I said: 'May Allah make me your ransom, do you not see that they disliked what they were upon and opposed them, and said: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy?﴾'" He said: "He then ordered that I be clothed in two thick garments."

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn 'Abbas, also, who said: "Those who forbade evil were saved, and those who committed it perished, and I do not know what was done to those who remained silent."

'Abd ibn Humayd and Abu al-Shaykh reported from him, who said: "By Allah, if I knew that the people who said ﴿Why do you admonish a people?﴾ were saved along with those who forbade evil, it would be dearer to me than what I would exchange it for."

In another wording: "than red camels. But I fear that the punishment descended upon them all."

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir reported from 'Ikrimah, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "I do not know whether those who said ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy?﴾ were saved or not." He said: "I kept looking at him until he realised that they had been saved, and he clothed me in a robe."

'Abd ibn Humayd reported from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, who said: "Those who said ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy?﴾ were transformed into stones."

'Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿with a severe punishment (bi-'adhabin ba'is)﴾, that he said: "Painful and grievous."

Inbijas means gushing forth; that is, from it twelve springs gushed forth, according to the number of tribes, with each tribe having a spring from which they drank. ﴿Every people knew its drinking place﴾, meaning each tribe knew the specific spring from which it drank. What was said about this in al-Baqarah is sufficient and makes repetition unnecessary.

﴿And We shaded them with clouds﴾, meaning We made them shade over them in the wilderness; it moved with their movement and stopped with their stopping. ﴿And We sent down upon them manna and quails﴾, that is, the honey-like substance (tarnjabin) and the quail (as-samani), as its verification has already been discussed in al-Baqarah. ﴿Eat of the good things We have provided for you﴾, meaning We said to them: eat of the delicious things We have provided for you. ﴿And they did not wrong Us﴾ by what they did of disobedience, ingratitude for blessings, and failure to appreciate them as they should. ﴿But they were wronging themselves﴾, meaning their wrongdoing was confined to themselves and did not extend beyond them to others.

﴿And when it was said to them﴾, that is, remember the time when this statement was said to them: ﴿Dwell in this town﴾, meaning Bayt al-Maqdis or Jericho; it was said that it is other than that, which has already been explained. ﴿And eat from it﴾, meaning from the foods found in it. ﴿Wherever you wish﴾, meaning in any place of its places that you wish, with no prohibition on you to eat there. ﴿And say: Hittah (forgiveness)﴾, whose explanation has already been given in al-Baqarah. ﴿And enter the gate﴾, meaning the gate of the aforementioned town, while you are ﴿prostrating﴾. They were commanded to combine their saying "hittah" with entering while prostrating. So it is not said: how did He put the command to speak here before entering, and delay it in al-Baqarah? The meaning of the prostration they were commanded to perform has already been explained. ﴿We will forgive you your sins﴾ is the answer to the command.

It was also recited as "khatiyatakum" (singular). Then He promised them with His words: ﴿We will increase the good-doers﴾, meaning We will increase them beyond the forgiveness of sins with what is bestowed upon them of blessings. The sentence is a new independent clause, an answer to an implied question, as if it was said: what then is for them after forgiveness? ﴿But those who did wrong among them changed the word from what had been said to them﴾, the explanation of which has already been given in al-Baqarah. ﴿So We sent upon them a punishment (rijz) from the sky﴾, meaning a punishment coming from it ﴿because they were wronging﴾, meaning because of their wrongdoing.

His words: 163. ﴿And ask them about the town which was by the sea﴾. It is conjoined to the implied governing element of "idh": that is, remember when it was said to them, and ask them. This is a question of rebuke and reproach. By asking about the town is meant asking its people: that is, ask them about this event that happened to them there, which contradicted what Allah had commanded them.

Within this question is a great benefit: it informs the Jews that this is something known to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and that his knowledge of it could only come through information given to him by Allah, glory be to Him, and thus it is evidence of his truthfulness.

The people of tafsir differed about this town: which town was it? It was said: Aylah; it was said: Tiberias; it was said: Madyan; it was said: Iliya; and it was said: a town among the towns of the Syrian coast which was "by the sea", that is, which was near the sea. It is said: "I was in the presence (hadrah) of the house," meaning near it.

The meaning is: O Muhammad, ask these present Jews about the story of the people of the aforementioned town.

It was recited "wa-s'alhum" and also "sal-hum". ﴿When they transgressed (idh ya'dun)﴾, meaning at the time they transgressed. It is an adverbial of time governed by an implied element indicated by the speech, because the question concerns their condition and their story at the time they transgressed. It was also said that it is an adverbial of time for "kanat" (was) or for "hadirah" (presence).

It was recited "yu'iddun" with a damma on the yā' and a kasra on the ʿayn and a shadda on the dāl, from al-i'dad (preparation), meaning the instrument.

The majority recited "ya'dun" with a fatha on the yā', a sukun on the ʿayn and a damma on the dāl, without shadda: that is, they overstep Allah's limits by hunting on the Sabbath day, on which they were forbidden from fishing. It was also recited "ya'addun" with a fatha on the yā' and the ʿayn and a damma on the dāl with shadda, meaning ya'tadun (transgress), the tā' being assimilated into the dāl.

As-sabt is the well-known day, and its root meaning is rest; it is said: sabata when he rested. Sabata the Jews meant they abandoned work on their Sabbath. Its plural is asbut, sabut, and asbat. Ibn as-Sumayfa' recited "fi al-asbat" in the plural.

﴿When their fish came to them﴾ (part 2 of the verse's explanation) is an adverbial of time governed by "ya'dun".

Al-hitan is the plural of hut (fish), and it was attributed to them to emphasize their special connection to those of them that came in this manner, coming on the Sabbath day and not on other days. "On their Sabbath day" is an adverbial of time for "ta'tihim" (come to them).

It was recited "yawma asbatihim". "Shurra'an" is a circumstantial accusative (hal), and it is the plural of shari': that is, visible on the water. It was said: raising their heads; and it was said: they used to come forward at their doorways like white rams.

In al-Kashshaf it is said: "shara'a 'alayna fulan" means when so-and-so approached us and came up over us, and "shara'tu 'ala fulan fi baytihi fa-ra'aytuhu yaf'alu kadha" means I looked in on so-and-so in his house and saw him doing such-and-such, end of quote.

﴿And on the day they did not keep the Sabbath, they did not come to them﴾, meaning they did not observe the Sabbath; on the day after the Sabbath ended, the fish would not come to them, as they used to come on the Sabbath day. ﴿Thus did We test them﴾, meaning like that great trial We tested them because of their defiance. Ibtila' means trial and examination.

﴿And when a community said﴾ is conjoined to ﴿when they transgressed﴾, governed by its governing element and within its ruling. Ummah means a group: that is, a group of the righteous people of the town said to others among those who used to strive to admonish the transgressors on the Sabbath, when they had despaired of their accepting admonition and giving up disobedience: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy﴾, meaning who are destined for punishment ﴿or punish them with a severe punishment﴾ for the sacred things they violated and the disobedience they committed. It was said that the group saying "why do you admonish a people" were the disobedient who hunted on the Sabbath; they said this to those who admonished them when they admonished them.

The meaning: if you know that Allah is going to destroy us, as you claim, then why do you admonish us? They said: ﴿An excuse to your Lord﴾, meaning the admonishers said to the group who said to them "why do you admonish": they are a group of the righteous people of the town according to the first interpretation, or the doers (of the sin) according to the second. ﴿An excuse to your Lord﴾: ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar and Talhah ibn Musarrif recited "ma'dhiratan" in the accusative, which is the recitation of Hafs from ʿAsim; the rest recited it in the nominative.

Al-Kisa'i said: its accusative has two possibilities: one of them is as a verbal noun (masdar), and the second is by the implied meaning "we did that as an excuse," that is, for the sake of the excuse.

The nominative is by an implied subject: that is, our admonition is an excuse to Allah, so that He will not hold us accountable for abandoning the commanding of good and forbidding of evil which He made obligatory upon us, and in hope that they might take heed, fear Allah, and give up what they are engaged in of disobedience.

The majority of the commentators said: the Children of Israel split into three groups. One group disobeyed and hunted, and they were about seventy thousand. One group withdrew and did not admonish and did not disobey. And one group withdrew and admonished and did not disobey. The group that did not admonish and did not disobey said to the admonishing group: ﴿Why do you admonish a people﴾, meaning the disobedient group, ﴿whom Allah is going to destroy or punish?﴾ They said this based on the strong presumption according to Allah's custom of destroying or punishing the disobedient without total annihilation. The admonishing group said: our admonition is an excuse to Allah, ﴿and perhaps they will fear Allah﴾. If they had been only two groups, the admonishing non-disobedient group and the disobedient group, he would have said: "perhaps you will fear Allah."

His words: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾, meaning when the disobedient people of the town left what the righteous who forbid evil had reminded them of, leaving like one who forgets a thing and turns away from it completely. ﴿We saved those who forbade evil﴾, meaning those who performed the forbidding and did not abandon it. ﴿And We seized those who did wrong﴾, and they were the transgressors who exceeded the limits on the Sabbath, ﴿with a grievous punishment (bi'sin)﴾, meaning a severe one, from ba'usa (to be severe) when a thing is harsh. There are eleven recitations of this word by the Seven and others. ﴿Because they were defiantly disobedient﴾, meaning because of their defiance. The prepositional phrase is connected to "akhadhna" (We seized).

﴿So when they insolently persisted in what they had been forbidden﴾, meaning they exceeded the limit in disobedience to Allah, glory be to Him, out of rebelliousness and arrogance. ﴿We said to them: Be apes, despised﴾, meaning We commanded them with a creational command, not a verbal command: that is, We transformed them into apes. It was said: He, glory be to Him, first punished them for their disobedience, and when they did not give up, He transformed them into apes. It was also said: His words "So when they insolently persisted in what they had been forbidden" are a repetition of His words "So when they forgot what they had been reminded of," for emphasis and affirmation, and that the transformation is the grievous punishment. "Khasi'in" means abject, humiliated, or distanced and expelled. It is said: "khasa'tuhu fakhusi'a," meaning I pushed him away and he withdrew.

Know that the apparent meaning of the Qur'anic text is that none were saved from the punishment except the forbidding group which did not disobey, according to His words: ﴿We saved those who forbade evil﴾, and that none were punished by transformation except the disobedient group, according to His words: ﴿So when they insolently persisted in what they had been forbidden, We said to them: Be apes, despised﴾. If the groups among them were three as previously mentioned, then the group that did not forbid and did not disobey may possibly have been transformed along with the disobedient group, because they wronged themselves by staying silent about the prohibition and were insolent toward what Allah had forbidden them, namely abandoning the forbidding of evil. And it is possible that they were not transformed, because although they wronged themselves and were insolent toward their Lord's command and prohibition, they did not wrong themselves by this specific sin, which is hunting the fish on the Sabbath day, nor were they insolent toward His prohibition to them against hunting. As for when the third group was forbidding like the second group, and was only made a separate group because a discussion took place between it and the other group of forbidders who withdrew, then in reality they are one group, since they are united in forbidding, withdrawing, and salvation from transformation.

Among the reports from al-Firyabi and Ibn Abi Hatim, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Moses said, "My Lord, I find a community whose Gospels are in their hearts." He said, "That is a community that will come after you: the community of Ahmad (ﷺ)." He said, "My Lord, I find a community who pray the five (prayers), which are expiations for what lies between them." He said, "That is a community that will come after you: the community of Ahmad (ﷺ)." He said, "My Lord, I find a community who give the charity of their wealth, then it returns to them and they eat it." He said, "That is [a community] after you: the community of Ahmad (ﷺ)." He said, "My Lord, make me one of the community of Ahmad (ﷺ)." So Allah revealed, in a manner that pleased Moses, ﴿And among the people of Moses is a community who guide by the truth and by it do justice﴾.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying ﴿And among the people of Moses is a community﴾ and the rest of the verse, that he said: "It has reached me that the Children of Israel, when they killed their prophets and disbelieved, and they were twelve tribes (asbat), one tribe disassociated itself from what they had done, made an excuse, and asked Allah to separate them from them. So Allah opened for them a tunnel (nafaq) in the earth, and they travelled through it until they emerged from beyond China. There they are upright (hunafa') Muslims, facing our qibla."

Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "That is His saying: ﴿And We said after him to the Children of Israel, 'Dwell in the land, and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you together as a mixed multitude﴾ [al-Isra' 17:104]. And the promise of the Hereafter is 'Isa ibn Maryam."

Ibn 'Abbas said: "They travelled in the tunnel (sarb) for a year and a half."

I say: A report as strange and remarkable as this needs verification of its transmission.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: "After Moses, the Children of Israel split into seventy-one sects, all of them in the Fire except one sect. The Christians split after 'Isa into seventy-two sects, all of them in the Fire except one sect. This community will certainly split into seventy-three sects, all of them in the Fire except one sect. As for the Jews, Allah says: ﴿And among the people of Moses is a community who guide by the truth and by it do justice﴾, so this is the one that will be saved. As for the Christians, Allah says: ﴿Among them is a moderate community﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:66], so this is the one that will be saved. As for us, He says: ﴿And among those whom We created is a community who guide by the truth and by it do justice﴾ [al-A'raf 7:181], so this is the one that will be saved from this community."

We have already mentioned that the addition "all of them in the Fire" is not authentically established, neither as a marfu' (attributed to the Prophet) nor as a mawquf (attributed to a Companion).

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿fanbajasat﴾ [gushed forth], that he said: "﴿fanfajarat﴾ [burst forth]."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from 'Ikrimah, who said: "I entered upon Ibn 'Abbas while he was reciting this verse: ﴿And ask them about the town that was by the sea﴾. He said: 'O 'Ikrimah, do you know what town this is?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'It is Aylah.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from al-Zuhri, who said: "It is Tiberias."

Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿when they transgressed in the Sabbath﴾, that he said: "They wronged."

Ibn Jarir reported from him regarding His saying ﴿shurra'an﴾ [appearing in abundance], he said: "He means from every place."

Ibn Jarir also reported from him, who said: "Floating upon the water."

Ibn al-Mundhir reported from him, who said: "Coming in."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from him regarding the verse, who said: "It is a town on the shore of the sea between Egypt and Madinah, called Aylah. Allah forbade them the fish on their Sabbath day, and they would come to them on their Sabbath day, appearing in abundance on the shore of the sea. But when the Sabbath day had passed, they could not catch them. They remained like this for as long as Allah willed. Then a group of them took the fish on their Sabbath day. A group admonished them, but they only increased in misguidance. A group of those who forbade said, knowing that these were a people upon whom the punishment was due: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy?﴾ They were more angry than the other group, and all of them had been forbidding. When the wrath of Allah befell them, the two groups who said ﴿Why do you admonish?﴾ and those who said ﴿as an excuse before your Lord﴾ were saved, and Allah destroyed the people of His disobedience who had taken the fish, and He transformed them into apes."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from him that they were three groups: the group of the sinners, the group of those who forbade, and the group who said ﴿Why do you admonish?﴾. "Only those who forbade were saved, and the rest perished. Then one morning those who had forbidden found themselves in their gatherings searching for the people and not seeing them. They had spent the night and locked their houses behind them. So they began to say: 'Surely something has happened to the people. Look into their affairs.' They looked into their houses, and behold, the people had been transformed: they recognised the man by his eye, and he was an ape, and the woman by her eye, and she was an ape."

'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan reported from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, and he mentioned the story, and at its end he said: "I see that those who forbade were saved, and I do not see that the others were mentioned. And we see things that we disapprove of, but we do not say anything about them."

'Ikrimah said: "I said: 'May Allah make me your ransom, do you not see that they disliked what they were upon and opposed them, and said: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy?﴾'" He said: "He then ordered that I be clothed in two thick garments."

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn 'Abbas, also, who said: "Those who forbade evil were saved, and those who committed it perished, and I do not know what was done to those who remained silent."

'Abd ibn Humayd and Abu al-Shaykh reported from him, who said: "By Allah, if I knew that the people who said ﴿Why do you admonish a people?﴾ were saved along with those who forbade evil, it would be dearer to me than what I would exchange it for."

In another wording: "than red camels. But I fear that the punishment descended upon them all."

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir reported from 'Ikrimah, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "I do not know whether those who said ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy?﴾ were saved or not." He said: "I kept looking at him until he realised that they had been saved, and he clothed me in a robe."

'Abd ibn Humayd reported from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, who said: "Those who said ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy?﴾ were transformed into stones."

'Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿with a severe punishment (bi-'adhabin ba'is)﴾, that he said: "Painful and grievous."

(p. 506) His words: ﴿And among the people of Moses﴾. When Allah had related to us what had happened with the Samiri and his companions, and the instability in religion that occurred among the Children of Israel, He, glory be to Him, related to us that among the people of Moses there was a community that opposed those previously mentioned. They are described as ﴿guiding by the truth﴾, meaning they call people to guidance while being characterized by the truth, ﴿and by it they act justly﴾, meaning they judge fairly among people. It was said that they include those among them who believed in Muhammad (ﷺ).

His words: ﴿And We divided them into twelve tribes﴾. The pronoun refers to the people of Moses mentioned earlier, not to this community among them who guide by the truth and act justly by it. The meaning is: We made them separate groups and distinguished some of them from others. This is among the blessings that Allah related to us which He bestowed upon the Children of Israel. The meaning is that He distinguished some of them from others until they became tribes, each tribe known on its own, and each tribe had a leader (naqib, chief), as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We raised from among them twelve leaders﴾, which has already been discussed.

His words: ﴿twelve﴾ is the second object of qatta'na (divided), because it implies the meaning of "making" (tasyir). ﴿Tribes (asbatan)﴾ is either a specification (tamyiz) for it or a substitute (badal) for it, or ﴿nations (umaman)﴾ is an attribute of asbat or a substitute for it. Asbat is the plural of sibt, which means the son's son (grandson). They became twelve nations from twelve sons. By asbat he meant tribes, and for this reason the number is feminine, as in the words of the poet:

*And indeed Quraysh, all of it, is ten clans,*
*and you are innocent of its ten tribes.*

Here "clan" (batn) means tribe. The verification of the meaning of asbat has already been discussed in al-Baqarah. Al-Mufaddal narrated from ʿAsim that he recited "qatta'nahum" with a light pronunciation (without the doubled letter). He called them "nations" because each tribe was a large group of people, and they had differing opinions, one leading in a direction different from the other.

﴿And We revealed to Moses when his people asked him for water﴾, that is, at the time they asked him for water when thirst afflicted them in the wilderness, saying: ﴿Strike the rock with your staff﴾. This is an explanation (tafsir) of the act of revelation. ﴿So it burst forth﴾ is a conjunction with an implied element indicated by the context: that is, he struck, and it burst forth. Inbijas means gushing forth; that is, from it twelve springs gushed forth, according to the number of tribes, with each tribe having a spring from which they drank. ﴿Every people knew its drinking place﴾, meaning each tribe knew the specific spring from which it drank. What was said about this in al-Baqarah is sufficient and makes repetition unnecessary.
