His saying: *Fa-mathaluhu ka-mathali al-kalb* ("So his likeness is the likeness of a dog"): meaning, when he stripped away from the signs and did not act upon them, he sank to the lowest rank, resembling the most base of animals in lowliness, and matching it in its worst attributes. The dog pants in both states, whether a person approaches it or leaves it. It pants whether it is driven off or not, whether it is pursued or not. Nothing is lower or baser than this. The clause *in tahmil 'alayhi yalhath aw tatrukhu yalhath* ("whether you attack it, it pants, or you leave it, it pants") is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal): i.e., his likeness is the likeness of the dog, in a state of having this attribute. The meaning is that this one who has stripped away from the signs does not desist from disobedience in any of his circumstances, whether a preacher admonishes him, a reminder reminds him, or a restrainer restrains him, or none of that happens to him.

Al-Qutaybi said: Everything that pants does so from exhaustion or thirst, except the dog, which pants in a state of fatigue, in a state of rest, in a state of illness, in a state of health, in a state of satiety, and in a state of thirst. So God struck this as a parable for the one who denied His signs, saying: "If you admonish him, he goes astray, and if you leave him, he goes astray." He is like the dog: if you leave it, it pants, and if you drive it away, it pants, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you call them to guidance, they will not follow you; it is the same for you whether you call them or you remain silent﴾ (al-A'raf 7:193). *Al-lahth* is letting the tongue hang out due to fatigue, thirst, or other things.

Al-Jawhari said: *lahatha al-kalbu* (with a fatha) *yalhathu lahthan wa-luhaan* (with a damma) means the dog let its tongue hang out from exhaustion or thirst. Likewise a man does so when he is exhausted.

It was said: the meaning of the verse is that if you pursue the dog, it barks and runs away, and if you leave it, it attacks you and barks. It exhausts itself, approaching you and turning away from you. So it experiences at that moment what it experiences when thirsty, namely letting its tongue hang out. The reference in His saying *dhalika* ("that") is to the preceding parable with that base condition.

*Huwa* is the subject, and its predicate is *mathalu al-qawm alladhina kadhdhabu bi-ayatina* ("the likeness of the people who denied Our signs"). That is: that base parable is the likeness of the people who denied Our signs, from among the Jews, after they had come to know them and recognized them, yet they distorted, altered and concealed the description of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and denied them. *Fa-qsusi al-qasas* ("So relate the stories") means: relate to them this story, which describes the man who stripped away from the signs. His aforementioned likeness is like the likeness of these denying people from among the Jews, to whom you relate it, so that perhaps they will reflect upon it, apply their understanding to it, and thereby restrain themselves from error and turn toward what is right.

His saying: *sa'a mathalan al-qawmu alladhina kadhdhabu bi-ayatina* ("Evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs"): this sentence contains an explanation of the state of these people, extremely ugly. It is said: *sa'a al-shay'u* means it became ugly; this is intransitive. *Sa'ahu yasu'uhu mas'ah* is transitive, and it is one of the verbs of blame, like *bi'sa*. Its agent is a hidden pronoun within it, and *mathalan* is a specifying accusative (tamyiz) explaining it. The one to whom the blame applies is "the people who denied Our signs." It is necessary to assume an omitted genitive phrase for agreement, i.e., *sa'a mathalan* "the likeness of the people who denied" is evil.

Al-Akhfash said: The word *mathal* was made to refer to the people by way of metaphor. The people are in the nominative case as the subject, or by assuming an implied subject. The construction is: "The likeness is evil, a likeness that is the likeness of the people." So he said.

Abu 'Ali al-Farisi estimated it as: *sa'a mathalan mathalu al-qawm*, as we have already mentioned.

Al-Jahdari and al-A'mash read: *wa-sa'a mathalan al-qawmu* ("and evil is the example, the people").

His saying: *wa-anfusahum kanu yazlimun* ("and they were wronging themselves"): meaning, they wronged no one by denying except themselves; their wrongdoing did not extend beyond them to others and did not exceed them. The clause is coordinated with the one before it, in the sense that they combined denying the signs of God with wronging themselves.

*Man yahdi Allahu fa-huwa al-muhtadi* ("Whomever God guides, he is the one guided"), by what He prescribed and legislated for His servants. *Wa-man yudlil fa-ulaika hum al-khasirun* ("and whomever He leads astray, those are the losers"), those who are complete in loss. Whomever He guides, there is no misleader for him, and whomever He misleads, there is no guide for him: what He wills occurs, and what He does not will does not occur.

Al-Firyabi, 'Abd al-Razzaq, 'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding His saying: ﴿And recite to them the story of the one to whom We gave Our signs﴾, that he said: "He is a man from the Children of Israel called Bal'am ibn Ba'ura'."

Ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted through several chains from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "He is Bal'am ibn Ba'ura'." In another wording: "Bal'am ibn Ba'ir, the one who was given the Name, was among the Children of Israel."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And recite to them the story of the one to whom We gave Our signs﴾, that he said: "He is a man from the city of the tyrants called Bal'am. He had learned the Greatest Name of God. When Musa came down upon them, his kinsmen and people came to him and said: 'Musa is a fierce man, and with him are many troops, and if he prevails over us, he will destroy us. So invoke God to turn Musa and those with him away from us.' He said: 'If I invoke God to turn Musa and those with him away, my worldly life and my Hereafter will be lost.' They kept at him until he invoked God, and so He stripped from him what was in him."

Regarding His saying: ﴿If you attack him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants﴾, he said: "If he is burdened with wisdom, he does not carry it; and if he is left alone, he does not become guided to goodness, like the dog: if it is lying down, it pants, and if it is driven away, it pants."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh transmitted from him regarding the verse, that he said: "He is a man who was given three supplications, which would be answered for him. He had a wife, and he had a child by her. She said: 'Make one of them for me.' He said: 'Then you will have one. What is it that you want?' She said: 'Invoke God to make me the most beautiful woman among the Children of Israel.' He invoked God, and He made her the most beautiful woman among the Children of Israel. When she knew that there was none like her among them, she became averse to him and wanted something else. So he invoked God to make her a female dog, and she became a female dog. Two supplications were gone. Then her sons came and said: 'We cannot bear this. Our mother has become a female dog, and people taunt us with her. Invoke God to return her to the state she was in.' So he invoked God, and she returned as she had been. The three supplications were gone, and she was named al-Basus."

'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr regarding the verse, that he said: "He is Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt al-Thaqafi." In another wording: "It was revealed about your companion Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt."

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn 'Asakir transmitted from him something similar.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from al-Sha'bi, regarding this verse, that he said: "Ibn 'Abbas said: 'He is a man from the Children of Israel called Bal'am ibn Ba'ura'.' The Ansar used to say: 'He is the son of the monk for whom the Mosque of Discord (masjid al-shiqaq) was built.' The Thaqif used to say: 'He is Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "He is Sayfi ibn al-Rahib."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh transmitted from him regarding His saying: *fa-nsalakha minha*, that he said: "Knowledge was removed from him."

Regarding His saying: ﴿Had We willed, We would have raised him by them﴾, he said: "God raised him by His knowledge."

Muslim, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Asma' wa-l-Sifat* transmitted from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ), in his sermon, would praise God and extol Him with what is fitting for Him. Then he would say: 'Whomever God guides, there is none to mislead him, and whomever He leads astray, there is none to guide him. The truest speech is the Book of God, the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad (ﷺ), and the worst of affairs are their novelties. Every novelty is an innovation (bid'ah), every innovation is misguidance, and every misguidance is in the Fire.' Then he would say: 'I and the Hour have been sent like these two.'"

"And We have certainly created (dhara'na)" — i.e., We created.

The basic meaning of this word has already been explained fully, and this sentence confirms the content of what precedes it. "For Hell" — i.e., for punishment by it — "many" — i.e., a great many creatures — "of the jinn and mankind," i.e., from the two groups of jinn and mankind. He, glorified is He, made them for the Fire by His justice and by the deeds of its people, "who have deeds they do."

He knew what they would do before their existence, as is established in the authentic hadiths. Then He described these people, saying: "They have hearts with which they do not understand (la yafqahuna biha) as others understand with their minds." The clause "they do not understand with them" is in the place of raising, as a description of "hearts." The clause "they have hearts" is in the place of accusative, as a description of "many." He, glorified is He, made their hearts, since they did not understand what would benefit them and guide them, as though they did not understand at all; even if they understand other things, that is like non-existence. The same is the meaning of "and they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear." What is negated from the eyes is seeing what contains guidance through reflection and taking heed, even if they see other things. What is negated from the ears is hearing beneficial admonitions and the laws contained in the revealed books and what the messengers of God brought, even if they hear other things. The indication in His saying "those" (ulaika) refers to these people characterized by these attributes: they are like cattle in the absence of benefit from these faculties. Then He judged them to be more astray than cattle, because cattle perceive with these faculties what benefits and harms them, so they gain from what benefits and avoid what harms; these people do not distinguish between what benefits and what harms with respect to what God demanded of them and obligated them to. Then He judged them to be in complete heedlessness regarding their condition, which is the lack of discernment that is characteristic of one who has intellect, sight and hearing.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying "And We have certainly created (dhara'na)," that he said: "We created."

Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh related from al-Hasan regarding the verse, that he said: "We created for Hell."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn al-Najjar related from Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When God created for Hell those whom He created, the child of fornication was among those He created for Hell."

Ibn Jarir related from Mujahid regarding His saying: "And We have certainly created for Hell," that he said: "We have certainly created for Hell. They have hearts with which they do not understand," he said: "They do not understand anything of the affairs of life. And they have eyes with which they do not see (p-514) the guidance, and they have ears with which they do not hear the truth." Then He made them like cattle, then He made them worse than cattle, saying: "Nay, they are more astray." Then He informed that they are the heedless.

This verse contains a report from Allah, glorified is He, about His names in general, without detail. *Al-husna* is the feminine form of *al-ahsan*, meaning the names that are the most beautiful, because they signify the most beautiful named One and the most noble referent. Then He commanded them to call upon Him by them when in need, for when He is called by His most beautiful names, that is among the means of having one's supplication answered. It has been established in the *Sahih* (the authentic collection): "Indeed Allah has ninety-nine names; whoever counts them enters Paradise," and it will come, and the explanation of their number will also come at the end of this discussion, if Allah wills.

His saying: ﴿And leave those who deviate concerning His names﴾. *Al-ilhad* (deviation) means inclination and abandoning the right course. It is said: *lahada al-rajul fi al-din* and *alhada*, meaning the man inclined (from the truth) in the religion. From it comes *al-lahd* (the niche) in the grave, because it is at one side. It has been recited as *yalhadun*, and both are dialects. Deviation concerning His names, glorified is He, occurs in three ways: either by alteration, as the polytheists did, for they took the name *al-Lat* from *Allah*, *al-Uzza* from *al-Aziz*, and *Manat* from *al-Mannan*; or by addition to them, by inventing names of their own for which Allah has given no authority; or by reduction from them, by calling Him by some of them and not others. The meaning of ﴿And leave those who deviate﴾ is: leave them, do not argue with them, and do not confront them. On this meaning, the verse is abrogated (*mansukh*, i.e. superseded by a later ruling) by the verses on fighting. It has been said that its meaning is a threat, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Leave Me with whom I created alone﴾ (al-Muddaththir: 11), and His saying: ﴿Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves﴾ (al-Hijr: 3). This is preferable because of His saying: ﴿They will be recompensed for what they used to do﴾, for it is a threat to them of the descent of punishment, and a warning to the Muslims not to do as they did.

Muqatil and other exegetes (*mufassirun*) mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a man among the Muslims who used to say in his prayer: "O Most Merciful, O Most Compassionate." A man among the polytheists said: "Does not Muhammad and his companions claim that they worship one Lord? Then what is the matter with this man, who calls upon two lords?" Al-Qurtubi related this.

Ahmad, al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Khuzaymah, Abu 'Awanah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mandah, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym and al-Bayhaqi all transmitted from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has ninety-nine names, one hundred less one; whoever counts them enters Paradise. Indeed He is Odd (*witr*) and loves the odd."

In the wording of Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu'aym: "Whoever calls upon Him by them, Allah will answer his supplication."

At-Tirmidhi added in his *Sunan*, after his saying "loves the odd": "He is Allah, there is no god but He, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, the King, the Holy, the Source of Peace, the Granter of Security, the Guardian, the Mighty, the Compeller, the Majestic, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner, the Ever-Forgiving, the Subduer, the Bestower, the Provider, the Opener, the All-Knowing, the Restrainer, the Expander, the Abaser, the Exalter, the Bestower of Honour, the Humiliator, the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing, the Judge, the Just, the Subtle, the All-Aware, the Forbearing, the Magnificent, the Forgiving, the Appreciative, the Most High, the Great, the Preserver, the Nourisher, the Reckoner, the Majestic, the Generous, the Watchful, the Responsive, the All-Encompassing, the Wise, the Loving, the Glorious, the Resurrector, the Witness, the Truth, the Trustee, the Strong, the Firm, the Protector, the Praiseworthy, the Counter, the Originator, the Restorer, the Giver of Life, the Giver of Death, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, the Finder, the Glorious, the One, the Eternal, the Capable, the Omnipotent, the Expediter, the Delayer, the First, the Last, the Manifest, the Hidden, the Governor, the Exalted, the Benign, the Ever-Relenting, the Avenger, the Pardoner, the Compassionate, Master of the Kingdom, Possessor of Majesty and Honour, the Equitable, the Gatherer, the Self-Sufficient, the Enricher, the Preventer, the Distresser, the Benefactor, the Light, the Guide, the Originator, the Everlasting, the Inheritor, the Rightly Guiding, the Patient."

Thus al-Tirmidhi narrated this addition from al-Jūzjani, from Safwan ibn Salih, from al-Walid ibn Muslim, from Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, as a *marfu'* (attributed to the Prophet). He said: "This is a *gharib* (rare) hadith."

It has been related through more than one route from Abu Hurayrah, and in most narrations the enumeration of the names is not known except in this hadith.

Ibn Hibban in his *Sahih*, Ibn Khuzaymah and al-Hakim also related it by the route of Safwan with its previous chain.

Ibn Majah in his *Sunan* related it by another route, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, as *marfu'*, and listed the previously mentioned names with additions and omissions.

Ibn Kathir said in his *Tafsir*: "What the group of memorizers (*huffaz*) relied upon is that the listing of names in this hadith is *mudraj* (an interpolation inserted into the text)."

Rather, it is as narrated by al-Walid ibn Muslim and 'Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad al-San'ani, from Zuhayr ibn Muhammad, that it reached him from more than one of the people of knowledge that they said this, meaning that they compiled them from the Qur'an, as was related from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah and Abu Zayd al-Lughawi.

He said: Then let it be known that the Most Beautiful Names are not confined to the ninety-nine, by the evidence of what Imam Ahmad related in his *Musnad*, from Yazid ibn Harun, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from Abu Salamah al-Juhani, from al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "No worry or grief ever befalls anyone and he says: 'O Allah, I am Your servant, son of Your servant and daughter of Your servant; my forelock is in Your hand; Your judgment over me is executed; Your decree concerning me is just. I ask You by every name that You have, by which You named Yourself, or revealed in Your Book, or taught to any of Your creation, or kept to Yourself in the knowledge of the unseen with You, that You make the Great Qur'an the spring of my heart, the light of my breast, the removal of my sorrow and the departure of my worry and distress,' except that Allah removes his worry and grief and replaces them with relief." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, should we not learn them?" He said: "Yes, it is fitting for whoever hears them to learn them."

Abu Hatim Ibn Hibban also related it in his *Sahih* with the like of it. End of quotation.

Al-Bayhaqi also related it in *al-Asma' wa al-Sifat*.

Ibn Hazm said: "Concerning their enumeration, which is to say the Most Beautiful Names, there are hadiths that are *mudtarib* (confused in transmission), none of which is authentic at all."

Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym related with this number, from Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn 'Umar, who both said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, and they mentioned it, but I do not know its chain.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya and al-Tabarani, both in *al-Du'a'*, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym and al-Bayhaqi related from Abu Hurayrah: "Indeed Allah has ninety-nine names; whoever counts them enters Paradise: (p-515) I ask Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, the God, the Lord, the King, the Holy, the Source of Peace, the Granter of Security, the Guardian, the Mighty, the Compeller, the Majestic, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner, the Forbearing, the All-Knowing, the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, the Expansive, the Subtle, the All-Aware, the Most Gracious, the Bestower, the Originator, the Forgiving, the Loving, the Appreciative, the Glorious, the Initiator, the Restorer, the Light, the Creator (*al-bari'*)." And in another wording: "the Standing, the First, the Last, the Manifest, the Hidden, the Pardoner, the Ever-Forgiving, the Bestower, the Single, the One," and in another wording: "the Capable, the One, the Eternal Refuge, the Trustee, the Sufficient, the Everlasting, the Eternal, the Exalted, Possessor of Majesty and Honour, the Master, the Seeing, the Truth, the Firm, the Inheritor, the Illuminator, the Resurrector, the Capable," and in another wording: "the Answerer, the Giver of Life, the Giver of Death, the Praiseworthy," and in another wording: "the Beautiful, the Truthful, the Guardian, the Encompassing, the Great, the Near, the Watchful, the Opener, the Ever-Relenting, the Eternal, the Odd, the Originator of creation, the Provider, the All-Knowing, the Exalted, the Most High, the Great, the Self-Sufficient, the King, the Powerful, the Most Generous, the Kind, the Arranger, the Possessor, the Subduer, the Guide, the Grateful, the Generous, the Exalted in rank, the Witness, the One, Possessor of Bounty, Possessor of Ascension, Possessor of Grace, the Great Creator, the Guarantor, the Majestic."

Abu Nu'aym related from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, who said: I asked my father Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq about the ninety-nine names whoever counts enters Paradise. He said: They are in the Qur'an. In al-Fatihah there are five names: O Allah, O Lord, O Most Merciful, O Most Compassionate, O King. In al-Baqarah there are thirty-three names: O Encompassing, O Capable, O All-Knowing, O Wise, O Most High, O Great, O Ever-Relenting, O All-Seeing, O Protector, O Expansive, O Sufficient, O Kind, O Originator, O Grateful, O One, O All-Hearing, O Restrainer, O Living, O Self-Subsisting, O Self-Sufficient, O Praiseworthy, O Forgiving, O Forbearing, O God, O Near, O Responsive, O Mighty, O Helper, O Strong, O Severe, O Swift, O Aware. In Al 'Imran: O Bestower, O Standing, O Truthful, O Raiser, O Bountiful, O Most Gracious. In al-Nisa': O Watchful, O Reckoner, O Witness, O Nourisher, O Trustee, O Most High, O Great. In al-An'am: O Originator, O Subduer, O Subtle, O Proof. In al-A'raf: O Giver of Life, O Giver of Death. In al-Anfal: O Excellent Master, and O Excellent Helper. In Hud: O Preserver, O Glorious, O Loving, O Doer of what He wills. In al-Ra'd: O Great, O Exalted. In Ibrahim: O Bountiful, O Inheritor. In al-Hijr: O Creator. In Maryam: O Single. In Ta-Ha: O Ever-Forgiving. In "Qad aflaha" (Surat al-Mu'minun): O Generous. In al-Nur: O Truth, O Manifest. In al-Furqan: O Guide. In Saba': O Opener. In al-Zumar: O Knower. In Ghafir: O Acceptor of repentance, O Possessor of Bounty, O Exalted. In al-Dhariyat: O Provider, O Possessor of Strength, O Firm. In al-Tur: O Benign. In "Iqtarabat" (i.e. Surat al-Qamar): O Omnipotent, O King. In al-Rahman: O Possessor of Majesty and Honour, O Lord of the two Easts, O Lord of the two Wests, O Everlasting, O Helper. In al-Hadid: O First, O Last, O Manifest, O Hidden. In al-Hashr: O King, O Holy, O Source of Peace, O Granter of Security, O Guardian, O Mighty, O Compeller, O Majestic, O Creator, O Originator, O Fashioner. In al-Buruj: O Initiator, O Restorer. In al-Fajr: O Odd. In al-Ikhlas: O One, O Eternal. End of quotation.

Ibn Hajar mentioned in *al-Talkhis* that he traced them from the Noble Book until he compiled ninety-nine from it, then listed them. So examine that.

This is supported by what Abu Nu'aym related from Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn 'Umar, who both said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has ninety-nine names; whoever counts them enters Paradise, and they are in the Qur'an."

Al-Bayhaqi related from 'A'ishah that she said: "O Messenger of Allah, teach me the name of Allah by which, when He is called upon, He answers." He said to her: "Stand up, make wudu', enter the mosque, pray two rak'ahs, then supplicate until I hear." She did so, and when she sat for the supplication, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, grant her success." She said: "O Allah, I ask You by all Your Most Beautiful Names, all of them, what we know of them and what we do not know, and I ask You by Your Great Name, the Greatest, the Mightiest, the Most Great, the Most Mighty, by which whoever calls upon You, You answer, and whoever asks You by it, You give." The Prophet said: "You have hit it, you have hit it."

The people of knowledge have extended discourse on the Most Beautiful Names, to the point that Ibn al-'Arabi in his commentary on al-Tirmidhi related that some scholars gathered from the Book and the Sunnah a thousand names of Allah.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿And leave those who deviate concerning His names﴾, that he said: Deviation is calling upon al-Lat and al-Uzza with the names of Allah.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him that he said: Deviation is denial.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh related from Ibn Jurayj concerning the verse that he said: They derived al-Uzza from al-Aziz, and derived al-Lat from Allah.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from 'Ata' concerning the verse that he said: Deviation is resemblance (*al-mudahah*).

Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-A'mash that he recited *yalhadun* from *lahada*, and said: Its interpretation is that they introduce into them what is not part of them.

'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir related from Qatadah concerning the verse that he said: They associate partners (with Allah).

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 7, verses 181–187:

His saying: ﴿And among those We created﴾ is a fronted predicate (*khabar muqaddam*), and ﴿a community﴾ is a postponed subject (*mubtada' mu'akhkhar*). ﴿Who guide﴾ and what follows it is a description of it. It is permissible that ﴿among those We created﴾ itself be the subject, as was mentioned earlier in His saying: ﴿And among the people is one who says﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:8). The meaning is that among those whom Allah created is a community who guide people while adhering to the truth, or who guide them with what they know of the truth, and ﴿by the truth they dispense justice﴾ among them. It has been said: they are from this Ummah, and they are the group that will continue to be upon the truth and prevailing, as is related in the authentic hadith.

Then, when He had described the condition of this righteous community, He described the condition of those who oppose them, so He said: ﴿And those who denied Our signs, We will draw them gradually [from where they do not know]﴾. *Istidraj* (gradual leading toward destruction) is taking someone step by step from one station to another. *Al-darj* means the folding of a thing. It is said: *adraftuhu* and *darajtuhu*, and from it comes *idraj al-mayyit fi akfanih* (the wrapping of the dead in their shrouds). It has also been said: (p-516) it is from *al-darajah* (degree), so *istidraj* is to step from one degree to another toward the intended goal. So they immerse themselves in error and turn away from the paths of guidance, deceived by this and thinking that what they have gained has come only because of their rank and nearness with Allah.

His saying: ﴿And I give them respite﴾ is conjoined to ﴿We will draw them gradually﴾. That is, I prolong their term, grant them time, and defer punishment from them. The clause ﴿Indeed My plan is firm﴾ confirms what came before it, namely the drawing-on and the respite, and emphasises it. *Al-kayd* is scheming, and *al-matin* is strong and powerful. Its root is from *al-matn*, which is the thick flesh on the side of the spine.

Al-Zamakhshari said in *al-Kashshaf* (a commentary on the Qur'an): He called it a scheme because it resembles a scheme, in that outwardly it is a favour, while in reality it is abandonment.

The interrogative in ﴿Have they not reflected?﴾ is for denunciation of them, since they did not reflect upon the matter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and what he brought. The *ma* in ﴿there is no madness in their companion﴾ is interrogative of denial. It occupies a nominative position as a subject, and the predicate is ﴿in their companion﴾. *Al-jinnah* is a verbal noun. That is: they denied, and they did not reflect on what madness is present in their companion, as they claim! For if they had reflected, they would have found their claim false and their saying a lie and slander. It has also been said that *ma* is negative, its noun is ﴿madness﴾, and its predicate is ﴿in their companion﴾. That is: there is nothing of the madness they allege in their companion. This would be a rebuttal of their saying: ﴿O you to whom the Reminder has been revealed, you are indeed a madman!﴾ (al-Hijr 15:6). In this case the sentence is complete at ﴿Have they not reflected?﴾, and pausing there is one of the good pauses. The clause ﴿He is only a clear warner﴾ confirms the content of what precedes it and clarifies the true reality of the condition of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

The interrogative in ﴿Have they not looked into the dominion of the heavens and the earth?﴾ is for denial, reproach, and rebuke, and to express wonder at their turning away from considering the clear signs which indicate the perfection of His power and His singular divinity. *Al-malakut* is from the patterns of intensification, and its meaning is great sovereignty, which has already been explained. The meaning is: these people have not reflected so as to benefit from reflection, nor have they looked at Allah's creatures so that they might be guided thereby to faith in Him. Rather, they are wallowing in their misguidance and plunging into their error, not applying thought and not looking carefully.

His saying: ﴿Or at what Allah has created of any thing﴾ means: they did not look at the dominion of the heavens and the earth, nor at whatever thing Allah has created, whatever it may be. In all His creatures there is a lesson for those who take heed and an admonition for those who reflect, whether they are among the great things He has made, such as the dominion of the heavens and the earth, or among the fine details of them, from the rest of His creation.

His saying: ﴿And that perhaps their term has drawn near﴾ is conjoined to *malakut* (dominion). *Anna* here is the lightened form of the heavy (*anna al-mukhaffafah*), its noun is the pronoun of the matter (*damir al-sha'n*), and its predicate is *'asa* (perhaps), together with what follows it. That is: have they not looked into the matter, and into the fact that perhaps their term has drawn near, so that they will die soon?

The meaning is: if they admit the possibility that their terms are near, then why do they not look into that by which they could be guided, and benefit by reflecting upon it and taking heed from it? ﴿Then in what statement after this will they believe?﴾ The pronoun refers to what came before, namely the reflection and consideration of the matters mentioned. That is: in what statement after this one already explained will they believe? In this interrogative there is reproach and rebuke beyond measure. It has also been said that the pronoun refers to the Qur'an, or to Muhammad (ﷺ), or to the term mentioned before it.

The clause ﴿Whomever Allah leaves astray, there is none to guide him﴾ confirms what precedes it. That is: this heedlessness on their part regarding these clear and manifest matters is only because they are among those whom Allah has led astray. And whoever Allah leads astray, there is no guide for him, meaning there is no one who can guide him to the truth or turn him away from error at all. ﴿And He leaves them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾. It is read with *raf'* (*yadharuhum*) as a new sentence (*isti'naf*), and with *jazm* (*yadharhum*) as a conjunction to the place of the conditional (*mahall al-jaza'*). It is also read with *nun* (*nadharuhum*). The meaning of *ya'mahun* is they are bewildered. It has also been said: they hesitate. It is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (*hal*).

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Abu al-Shaykh related from Ibn Juraij, regarding His saying: ﴿And among those We created is a community who guide by the truth﴾, that he said: It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "This is my Ummah, who judge by the truth, and decide, and take, and give."

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Qatada concerning the verse, that he said: We have been told that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to say when he recited it: "This is for you, and a similar one has been given to the people before you: ﴿And among the people of Musa is a community who guide by the truth and by it dispense justice.﴾"

Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Rabi' concerning the verse, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed among my Ummah there is a people upon the truth until 'Isa, son of Maryam, descends, whenever he descends."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related from al-Suddi, concerning His saying: ﴿We will draw them gradually from where they do not know﴾, that he said: We will seize them from where they do not know. He said: it is the punishment of Badr.

Abu al-Shaykh related from Yahya ibn al-Muthanna concerning the verse, that he said: Whenever they committed a sin, We renewed for them a blessing which made them forget seeking forgiveness.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Abu al-Shaykh, and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Asma' wa al-Sifat* related from Sufyan concerning the verse, that he said: We lavish blessings upon them and prevent them from being thankful for them.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya and al-Bayhaqi related from Thabit al-Bunani that he was asked about *istidraj*, and he said: That is the scheming of Allah against the servants who waste (their opportunities).

Abu al-Shaykh related concerning His saying: ﴿And I give them respite﴾, that He says: I hold back from them. ﴿Indeed My plan is firm﴾: indeed My scheme is strong. Then Allah abrogated it (*naskh*) and sent down: ﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ (al-Tawbah 9:5).

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Abbas, who said: The scheme of Allah is punishment and vengeance.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh related from Qatada, who said: It has been mentioned to us that "the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) stood on al-Safa and called the Quraysh clan by clan: 'O Banu so-and-so, O Banu so-and-so,' warning them of the wrath of Allah and the calamities of Allah until morning. Then some speaker said: 'Indeed this companion of yours is surely a madman; he kept shouting until morning.' So Allah sent down: ﴿Have they not reflected? There is no madness in their companion; he is only a clear warner.﴾"

(p-517) His saying: ﴿They ask you about the Hour﴾. The askers were the Jews, and it was said they were the Quraysh. "The Hour" (al-sa'ah) is the Resurrection, and it is one of the names that became dominant for it. It is applied to the Resurrection either because it comes suddenly or because its reckoning is swift. "Ayyan" (when) is an adverb of time (zarf zaman) that is indeclinable (mabni) on the fatha. The reciter said:

*"When will my need be fulfilled? When? Do you not see that its ripeness is due?"*

Its meaning is the same as *mata* (when), and its derivation is from *ayy*. It was also said to be from *ayna* (where).

Al-Sulami read *"iyyan"* with a kasra on the hamza. It is then in the position of a predicate (khabar). ﴿Its settling﴾ (mursaha) is the subject (mubtada') according to Sibawayh. *Mursaha* with a damma on the *mim* means the time of its establishment, from *arsaha Allah*, meaning God fixed it. With a fatha on the *mim* it comes from *rasat*, meaning it became firm. From this is ﴿and cooking pots fixed firmly﴾ (Saba': 13), and from it is *rasa al-jabal*, meaning the mountain became fixed.

The meaning is: when will God settle it, that is, establish it and bring it about. The apparent sense of ﴿They ask you about the Hour﴾ is that the question concerns the Hour itself, and the apparent sense of ﴿When is its settling?﴾ is that the question concerns its time. From all of this it results that the question mentioned is about the Hour in terms of its occurrence at a specified time. Then God, glorified is He, commanded him to answer them with His saying: ﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾. That is, its knowledge, in terms of its occurrence, is with God alone, and no one else knows it or is guided to it. ﴿None will reveal it at its time except Him﴾. That is, none will make it manifest at its time or uncover it except God, glorified is He. *Tajliyah* means making a thing manifest. It is said: *jalla li fulan al-khabar*, meaning he made the news manifest and clear. In God's exclusive possession of the knowledge of the Hour there is great wisdom and profound design, like all the other things that God concealed and kept exclusively to His knowledge.

This sentence confirms the content of the one before it.

His saying: ﴿It has been heavy upon the heavens and the earth﴾. It was said that the meaning is: since its knowledge was hidden from the people of the heavens and the earth, it was heavy, because whatever knowledge is hidden is heavy on hearts. It was also said that the meaning is: the heavens and the earth cannot bear it because of its magnitude, since the sky will split, the stars will scatter, and the seas will dry up. It was also said: its description became great for them. It was also said: the question about it became heavy. This sentence also confirms the content of what precedes it. ﴿It will not come upon you except suddenly﴾, that is, except unexpectedly while you are heedless. *Al-baghtah* is a verbal noun in the position of a circumstantial clause (hal). This sentence is like the one before it in confirmation.

His saying: ﴿They ask you as though you were informed about it﴾. Ibn Faris said: *al-hafiy* is one who knows a thing, and *al-hafiy* is also one who presses in questioning. From this is the saying of al-A'sha:

*"If you ask about me, then how many a questioner, eager about al-A'sha, has asked where he ascended."*

It is said: *ahfa fi al-mas'alah* and *fi al-talab*, so he is *muhfin*. *Hafiy* is an intensive form like *mukhassib* and *khasib*.

The meaning is: they ask you about the Hour as though you knew it, or as though he were pressing in questioning about it and asking much about it. The simile clause is in a position of accusative (nasb) as a circumstantial clause, meaning they ask you while your state is made like the state of one who is informed about it. It was also said that the meaning is: they ask you about it as though you were eager for them, that is, eager for their goodness and pleased with their asking.

The first meaning is the meaning of the Qur'anic arrangement according to the requirement of the Arabic style.

His saying: ﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾. God, glorified is He, commanded him to repeat what he had already answered them, to establish and confirm the ruling. It was also said that it is not a repetition, but rather one of them means exclusive possession of its occurrence, and the other means exclusive possession of its very nature. ﴿But most people do not know﴾ this exclusive possession by God and the absence of knowledge of it among His creation. No near-angel and no sent prophet knows it.

His saying: ﴿Say: I possess for myself no benefit or harm except what God wills﴾. This sentence contains a confirmation of what preceded regarding his lack of knowledge of the Hour, when it will be and when it will occur. For if he does not have power to bring about benefit for himself or to repel harm from himself except what God, glorified is He, wills of benefit to him and repelling from him, then it is all the more so that he has no power to know what God has kept exclusively to His knowledge. In this there is a demonstration of servitude and an acknowledgment of inability regarding matters that are not the concern of servants, and an admission of weakness in claiming what is not his. In it is the greatest deterrent and the most eloquent admonition for whoever claims for himself what is not his concern and appropriates knowledge of the unseen through fortune-telling, sand divination, pebble casting, or augury. Then he confirmed and established this with His saying: ﴿And had I known the unseen, I would have acquired much good﴾. That is: if I knew the category of the unseen, I would have pursued what contains good and brought it to myself, and I would have guarded against what contains evil so that it would not touch me. But I am a servant who does not know what is with my Lord, nor what He has decreed for me and destined for me. So how could I know other than that and burden myself with knowing it? It was also said that the meaning is: had I known what God, mighty and majestic, wills of me before He informs me of it, I would have done it. It was also said: had I known when victory in war would be mine, I would have fought and not been defeated. It was also said: had I known the unseen, I would have answered every question asked of me. The better view is to take the verse in its generality, so these matters and others are included under it. It has also been said that ﴿and evil has not touched me﴾ is a new independent statement, meaning there is not in me what you claim of madness. The better view is that it is connected to what precedes it, and the meaning is: had I known the unseen, evil would not have touched me, and I would have guarded against it, as we have mentioned.

His saying: ﴿I am not but a warner and a bringer of good tidings to a people who believe﴾. That is: I am only a conveyor from God of His rulings, by which I warn one people and give good tidings to others, and I do not know the unseen of God, glorified is He. The lam in *li-qawmin* is connected to both attributes: a bringer of good tidings to a people, and a warner to a people. It was also said that it is connected to *bashir* (bringer of good tidings), and what is connected to *nadhir* (warner) is omitted, meaning: a warner to a people who disbelieve, and a bringer of good tidings to a people who believe.

His saying: ﴿He is the One who created you from one soul﴾. This is an independent statement containing a mention of God's blessings upon His servants and their failure to repay them with what is obligatory of gratitude and acknowledgment of servitude, and that He alone is singular in divinity.

The majority of exegetes said: by "one soul" is meant Adam. His saying ﴿and made from it its mate﴾ is conjoined to ﴿created you﴾, meaning: He is the One who created you from the soul of Adam and made from this soul its mate, who is Eve, whom He created from one of his ribs. It was also said that the meaning of ﴿made from it﴾ is from its kind, as in His saying: ﴿He made for you from yourselves mates﴾ (al-Nahl: 72). The first is better. ﴿So that he might find rest in her﴾ is the reason for the making: that is, He made her from him so that he would find rest and comfort in her and be at peace with her, for a kind is most at rest with its own kind and most at ease with it. This was in Paradise, as the reports have narrated. Then God, glorified is He, began with another state that existed between them in this world after their descent, and He said: ﴿So when he covered her﴾. *Al-taghashshi* is a metaphor for intercourse, that is, when he had intercourse with her. ﴿She carried a light burden﴾, meaning she conceived after intercourse. He described it as light because at the time of the drop of semen it is lighter than when it becomes a clot, and when it is a clot it is lighter than when it is a lump of flesh, and when it is a lump it is lighter than what comes after. It was also said that this pregnancy was light for her from its beginning to its end, and she did not find any heaviness in it as pregnant women do. This is because of His saying: ﴿and she continued with it﴾, that is, she went on with that pregnancy, standing, sitting, and going about her needs without finding heaviness in it. The first interpretation is better because of His saying: ﴿then when she became heavy﴾, for its meaning is: when she became one with heaviness due to the size of the child in her womb. It was read *famarrat bihi* with lightening, that is, she was disturbed by it. It was also read *famarat bihi* from *al-mawr*, which is coming and going. It was also said that the meaning is: she continued with it.

The reading with lightening has been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas and Yahya ibn Ya'mur. The reading *famarat* has been narrated from Abd Allah ibn Umar. It was also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he read *fastamarrat bihi* (she continued with it).

His saying: ﴿They both called upon God, their Lord﴾. This is the answer to *lamma* (when). That is: Adam and Eve called upon God, their Lord and the owner of their affairs: ﴿If You give us a righteous child﴾, that is, a righteous son. The lam is the answer to an omitted oath, and ﴿we will surely be among the grateful﴾ is the answer to the oath, serving in place of the answer to the condition, meaning: among those who are grateful to You for this blessing. In this supplication is evidence that they both knew that what had happened in Eve's womb from the effect of that intercourse was of their own kind, and they knew that offspring affected by that cause would be established.

﴿So when He gave them﴾ what they asked for, a righteous child, and answered their supplication, ﴿they made for Him partners in what He had given them﴾.

Many exegetes said: Iblis came to Eve and said to her: If you give birth to a child, name him after me. She said: And what is your name? He said: al-Harith. He would not have named himself to her, or she would have recognized him. So she named him Abd al-Harith. This was an act of associating in naming, not an association in worship. They only intended that al-Harith was the cause of the child's deliverance, just as a man names himself "servant of his guest," as Hatim al-Ta'i said:

*"I am indeed a servant of the guest as long as he stays, and there is nothing in me but that trait of the servant."*

Other exegetes said: the ones who make partners in what He gave them are the human race, as happened with the polytheists among them, and it was not from Adam and Eve. This is indicated by the plural pronoun in His saying: ﴿Exalted is God above what they associate﴾.

Some exegetes went to the view that the meaning of ﴿from one soul﴾ is from one form and one shape, ﴿and made from it its mate﴾ meaning of its kind, ﴿and when he covered her﴾ means the male kind covered the female kind. On this view, Adam and Eve are not mentioned in the verse, and the dual pronouns refer to the two kinds.

We have already pointed to something similar to this and mentioned that it is contrary to the better view for several reasons. Among them: ﴿and made from it its mate﴾ applies only to Eve. Among them: ﴿they called upon God, their Lord﴾, for every child born between the two kinds does not have this supplication from them at the approach of its delivery.

The people of Medina and Asim read *shirkan* (singular), and Abu 'Amr and the rest of the people of Kufa read it in the plural.

Al-Akhfash Sa'id denied the first reading. It has been answered that it is correct by omitting the genitive-modified noun: that is, they made for Him one who has a share (*dha shirk*), or those who have a share (*dhawi shirk*).

The interrogative in ﴿Do they associate what creates nothing?﴾ is for rebuke and reproach, meaning: how do they make for God a partner who creates nothing and is not able to bring benefit to them or repel harm from them?

His saying: ﴿while they themselves are created﴾ is conjoined to ﴿what creates nothing﴾, and the pronoun refers to the partners who create nothing. That is: these whom they made partners, from idols or devils, are themselves created. Their plural is the plural of rational beings because those who made them partners believed them to be such.

﴿And they cannot help them﴾, that is, those who made them partners, ﴿with victory﴾ if he seeks it from them, ﴿nor can they help themselves﴾ if something befalls them from others. Whoever is unable to help himself is all the more unable to help others.

Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Hamal ibn Abi Qays and Shamul ibn Zayd said to the Messenger of God ﷺ: Tell us when the Hour will be, if you are a prophet as you say, for we know what it is. So God revealed: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when is its settling? Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾ up to His saying: ﴿But most people do not know.﴾"

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، وابن جرير، عن قتادة: ﴿أيان مرساها﴾ أي متى قيامها؟ ﴿يسألونك عن الساعة أيان مرساها قل إنما علمها عند ربي لا يجليها لوقتها إلا هو﴾. قال: قالت قريش: يا محمد، أسرّ إلينا الساعة لما بيننا وبينك من القرابة؟ فقال: ﴿يسألونك كأنك حفي عنها قل إنما علمها عند الله﴾. وذُكر لنا أن نبي الله ﷺ كان يقول: «تهيج الساعة بالناس والرجل يسقي على ماشيته، والرجل يصلح حوضه، والرجل يخفض ميزانه ويرفعه، والرجل يقيم سلعته في السوق، قضاء الله لا تأتيكم إلا بغتة».

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿أيان مرساها﴾ قال: منتهاها.

وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة، وعبد بن حميد، وابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، عن مجاهد: ﴿لا يجليها لوقتها إلا هو﴾ يقول: لا يأتي بها إلا الله.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، عن قتادة، في الآية قال: هو يجليها لوقتها، لا يعلم ذلك إلا الله.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿ثقلت في السماوات والأرض﴾ قال: ليس شيء من الخلق إلا يصيبه من ضرر يوم القيامة.

وأخرج عبد الرزاق، وابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، عن قتادة، في قوله: ﴿ثقلت في السماوات والأرض﴾ قال: ثقل علمها على أهل السماوات والأرض، يقول: كبرت عليهم.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وأبو الشيخ، عن ابن جريج في قوله: ﴿ثقلت في السماوات والأرض﴾ (p-519) قال: إذا جاءت انشقت السماء، وانتثرت النجوم، وكوِّرت الشمس، وسُيِّرت الجبال، وما يصيب الأرض، وكان ما قال الله سبحانه، فذلك ثقلها فيهما.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، عن مجاهد في قوله: ﴿لا تأتيكم إلا بغتة﴾ قال: فجأة، وأنتم آمنون.

وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة، وعبد بن حميد، وابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، والبيهقي في البعث، عن مجاهد في قوله: ﴿كأنك حفي عنها﴾ قال: استحفيت عنها السؤال حتى علمتها.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿كأنك حفي عنها﴾ يقول: كأنك عالم بها، أي لست تعلمها.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، والبيهقي، عنه: ﴿كأنك حفي عنها﴾ قال: لطيف بها.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، وابن مردويه، والبيهقي، عنه أيضًا: ﴿كأنك حفي عنها﴾ يقول: كأن بينك وبينهم مودة، كأنك صديق لهم. قال: لما سأل الناس محمدًا ﷺ عن الساعة سألوه سؤال قوم كأنهم يُرَوْن أن محمدًا حفي بهم، فأوحى الله إليه ﴿إنما علمها عند الله﴾ استأثر بعلمها، فلم يُطلع ملكًا ولا رسولًا.

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، عن عمرو بن دينار قال: كان ابن عباس يقرأ: «كأنك حفي بها».

وأخرج ابن جرير، وأبو الشيخ، عن ابن جريج: ﴿قل لا أملك لنفسي نفعًا ولا ضرًا﴾ قال: الهدى والضلالة. ﴿ولو كنت أعلم الغيب﴾ متى أموت ﴿لاستكثرت من الخير﴾ قال: العمل الصالح.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿ولو كنت أعلم الغيب لاستكثرت من الخير﴾ قال: لعلمت إذا اشتريت شيئًا ما أربح فيه فلا أبيع شيئًا لا ربح فيه. ﴿وما مسني السوء﴾ قال: لاجتنبت ما يكون من الشر قبل أن يكون.

وأخرج أحمد، والترمذي، وحسّنه، وأبو يعلى، وابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، والرُّوياني، والطبراني، وأبو الشيخ، والحاكم وصححه، وابن مردويه، عن سمرة، عن النبي ﷺ قال: «لما ولدت حواء طاف بها إبليس، وكان لا يعيش لها ولد، فقال: سمّيه عبد الحارث فإنه يعيش، فسمّته عبد الحارث فعاش، فكان ذلك من وحي الشيطان وأمره».

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، وابن جرير، وابن مردويه، عن سمرة في قوله: ﴿فلما آتاهما صالحًا جعلا له شركاء﴾ قال: سمّياه عبد الحارث.

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، وأبو الشيخ، عن أُبيّ بن كعب نحو حديث سمرة المرفوع، موقوفًا عليه.

وأخرج سعيد بن منصور، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، عن ابن عباس، قال: حملت حواء فأتاها إبليس فقال: إني صاحبكما الذي أخرجتكما من الجنة، لتطيعنّني أو لأجعلنّ له قرني أيل، فيخرج من بطنك فيشقه، ولأفعلنّ ولأفعلنّ، يخوفهما. سمّياه عبد الحارث، فأبيا أن يطيعاه فخرج ميتًا، ثم حملت فأتاهما أيضًا فقال مثل ذلك، فأبيا أن يطيعاه فخرج ميتًا، ثم حملت فأتاهما فذكر لهما فأدركهما حب الولد فسمّياه عبد الحارث، فذلك قوله: ﴿جعلا له شركاء فيما آتاهما﴾.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وأبو الشيخ، عن الحسن في الآية قال: كان هذا في بعض أهل الملل، وليس بآدم.

وأخرج أبو الشيخ، وابن مردويه، عن سمرة في قوله: ﴿حملت حملًا خفيفًا﴾ لم يستبن ﴿فمرت به﴾ لما استبان حملها.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿فمرت به﴾ قال: فشكّت أحملت أم لا.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وأبو الشيخ، عن أيوب قال: سُئل الحسن عن قوله: ﴿فمرت به﴾ فقال: لو كنت عربيًا لعرفتها، إنما هي استمرت بالحمل.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، عن السدي، في قوله: ﴿حملت حملًا خفيفًا﴾ قال: هي النطفة. ﴿فمرت به﴾ يقول: استمرت به.

وأخرج سعيد بن منصور، وابن المنذر، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿فمرت به﴾ قال: فاستمرت به.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، عن ميمون بن مهران: ﴿فمرت به﴾ يقول: استخفّته.

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، وابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، عن أبي صالح في قوله: ﴿لئن آتيتنا صالحًا﴾ فقال: أشفقا أن يكون بهيمة، فقالا: لئن آتيتنا بشرًا سويًا.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، عن مجاهد نحوه.

وأخرج عبد الرزاق، وابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، عن الحسن في الآية قال: غلامًا سويًا.

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿جعلا له شركاء﴾ قال: كان شريكًا في الطاعة، ولم يكن شريكًا في العبادة.

وأخرج ابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، عنه قال: ما أشرك آدم، إن أولها شكر، وآخرها مثل ضربه لمن بعده.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، عن السدي، في قوله: ﴿فتعالى الله عما يشركون﴾ هذا فصل من آية آدم خاصة، في آلهة العرب.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، عن أبي مالك نحوه.

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، وأبو الشيخ، عن الحسن في الآية قال: هذا في الكفار يدعون الله، فإذا آتاهما صالحًا هوّدا أو نصّرا. ثم قال: ﴿أيشركون ما لا يخلق شيئًا وهم يُخلقون﴾ يقول: يطيعون ما لا يخلق شيئًا، وهي الشياطين، لا تخلق شيئًا وهي تُخلق. ﴿ولا يستطيعون لهم نصرًا﴾ يقول: لمن يدعوهم.

(p-517) His saying: ﴿They ask you about the Hour﴾. The askers were the Jews, and it was said they were the Quraysh. "The Hour" (al-sa'ah) is the Resurrection, and it is one of the names that became dominant for it. It is applied to the Resurrection either because it comes suddenly or because its reckoning is swift. "Ayyan" (when) is an adverb of time (zarf zaman) that is indeclinable (mabni) on the fatha. The reciter said:

*"When will my need be fulfilled? When? Do you not see that its ripeness is due?"*

Its meaning is the same as *mata* (when), and its derivation is from *ayy*. It was also said to be from *ayna* (where).

Al-Sulami read *"iyyan"* with a kasra on the hamza. It is then in the position of a predicate (khabar). ﴿Its settling﴾ (mursaha) is the subject (mubtada') according to Sibawayh. *Mursaha* with a damma on the *mim* means the time of its establishment, from *arsaha Allah*, meaning God fixed it. With a fatha on the *mim* it comes from *rasat*, meaning it became firm. From this is ﴿and cooking pots fixed firmly﴾ (Saba': 13), and from it is *rasa al-jabal*, meaning the mountain became fixed.

The meaning is: when will God settle it, that is, establish it and bring it about. The apparent sense of ﴿They ask you about the Hour﴾ is that the question concerns the Hour itself, and the apparent sense of ﴿When is its settling?﴾ is that the question concerns its time. From all of this it results that the question mentioned is about the Hour in terms of its occurrence at a specified time. Then God, glorified is He, commanded him to answer them with His saying: ﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾. That is, its knowledge, in terms of its occurrence, is with God alone, and no one else knows it or is guided to it. ﴿None will reveal it at its time except Him﴾. That is, none will make it manifest at its time or uncover it except God, glorified is He. *Tajliyah* means making a thing manifest. It is said: *jalla li fulan al-khabar*, meaning he made the news manifest and clear. In God's exclusive possession of the knowledge of the Hour there is great wisdom and profound design, like all the other things that God concealed and kept exclusively to His knowledge.

This sentence confirms the content of the one before it.

His saying: ﴿It has been heavy upon the heavens and the earth﴾. It was said that the meaning is: since its knowledge was hidden from the people of the heavens and the earth, it was heavy, because whatever knowledge is hidden is heavy on hearts. It was also said that the meaning is: the heavens and the earth cannot bear it because of its magnitude, since the sky will split, the stars will scatter, and the seas will dry up. It was also said: its description became great for them. It was also said: the question about it became heavy. This sentence also confirms the content of what precedes it. ﴿It will not come upon you except suddenly﴾, that is, except unexpectedly while you are heedless. *Al-baghtah* is a verbal noun in the position of a circumstantial clause (hal). This sentence is like the one before it in confirmation.

His saying: ﴿They ask you as though you were informed about it﴾. Ibn Faris said: *al-hafiy* is one who knows a thing, and *al-hafiy* is also one who presses in questioning. From this is the saying of al-A'sha:

*"If you ask about me, then how many a questioner, eager about al-A'sha, has asked where he ascended."*

It is said: *ahfa fi al-mas'alah* and *fi al-talab*, so he is *muhfin*. *Hafiy* is an intensive form like *mukhassib* and *khasib*.

The meaning is: they ask you about the Hour as though you knew it, or as though he were pressing in questioning about it and asking much about it. The simile clause is in a position of accusative (nasb) as a circumstantial clause, meaning they ask you while your state is made like the state of one who is informed about it. It was also said that the meaning is: they ask you about it as though you were eager for them, that is, eager for their goodness and pleased with their asking.

The first meaning is the meaning of the Qur'anic arrangement according to the requirement of the Arabic style.

His saying: ﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾. God, glorified is He, commanded him to repeat what he had already answered them, to establish and confirm the ruling. It was also said that it is not a repetition, but rather one of them means exclusive possession of its occurrence, and the other means exclusive possession of its very nature. ﴿But most people do not know﴾ this exclusive possession by God and the absence of knowledge of it among His creation. No near-angel and no sent prophet knows it.

His saying: ﴿Say: I possess for myself no benefit or harm except what God wills﴾. This sentence contains a confirmation of what preceded regarding his lack of knowledge of the Hour, when it will be and when it will occur. For if he does not have power to bring about benefit for himself or to repel harm from himself except what God, glorified is He, wills of benefit to him and repelling from him, then it is all the more so that he has no power to know what God has kept exclusively to His knowledge. In this there is a demonstration of servitude and an acknowledgment of inability regarding matters that are not the concern of servants, and an admission of weakness in claiming what is not his. In it is the greatest deterrent and the most eloquent admonition for whoever claims for himself what is not his concern and appropriates knowledge of the unseen through fortune-telling, sand divination, pebble casting, or augury. Then he confirmed and established this with His saying: ﴿And had I known the unseen, I would have acquired much good﴾. That is: if I knew the category of the unseen, I would have pursued what contains good and brought it to myself, and I would have guarded against what contains evil so that it would not touch me. But I am a servant who does not know what is with my Lord, nor what He has decreed for me and destined for me. So how could I know other than that and burden myself with knowing it? It was also said that the meaning is: had I known what God, mighty and majestic, wills of me before He informs me of it, I would have done it. It was also said: had I known when victory in war would be mine, I would have fought and not been defeated. It was also said: had I known the unseen, I would have answered every question asked of me. The better view is to take the verse in its generality, so these matters and others are included under it. It has also been said that ﴿and evil has not touched me﴾ is a new independent statement, meaning there is not in me what you claim of madness. The better view is that it is connected to what precedes it, and the meaning is: had I known the unseen, evil would not have touched me, and I would have guarded against it, as we have mentioned.

His saying: ﴿I am not but a warner and a bringer of good tidings to a people who believe﴾. That is: I am only a conveyor from God of His rulings, by which I warn one people and give good tidings to others, and I do not know the unseen of God, glorified is He. The lam in *li-qawmin* is connected to both attributes: a bringer of good tidings to a people, and a warner to a people. It was also said that it is connected to *bashir* (bringer of good tidings), and what is connected to *nadhir* (warner) is omitted, meaning: a warner to a people who disbelieve, and a bringer of good tidings to a people who believe.

His saying: ﴿He is the One who created you from one soul﴾. This is an independent statement containing a mention of God's blessings upon His servants and their failure to repay them with what is obligatory of gratitude and acknowledgment of servitude, and that He alone is singular in divinity.

The majority of exegetes said: by "one soul" is meant Adam. His saying ﴿and made from it its mate﴾ is conjoined to ﴿created you﴾, meaning: He is the One who created you from the soul of Adam and made from this soul its mate, who is Eve, whom He created from one of his ribs. It was also said that the meaning of ﴿made from it﴾ is from its kind, as in His saying: ﴿He made for you from yourselves mates﴾ (al-Nahl: 72). The first is better. ﴿So that he might find rest in her﴾ is the reason for the making: that is, He made her from him so that he would find rest and comfort in her and be at peace with her, for a kind is most at rest with its own kind and most at ease with it. This was in Paradise, as the reports have narrated. Then God, glorified is He, began with another state that existed between them in this world after their descent, and He said: ﴿So when he covered her﴾. *Al-taghashshi* is a metaphor for intercourse, that is, when he had intercourse with her. ﴿She carried a light burden﴾, meaning she conceived after intercourse. He described it as light because at the time of the drop of semen it is lighter than when it becomes a clot, and when it is a clot it is lighter than when it is a lump of flesh, and when it is a lump it is lighter than what comes after. It was also said that this pregnancy was light for her from its beginning to its end, and she did not find any heaviness in it as pregnant women do. This is because of His saying: ﴿and she continued with it﴾, that is, she went on with that pregnancy, standing, sitting, and going about her needs without finding heaviness in it. The first interpretation is better because of His saying: ﴿then when she became heavy﴾, for its meaning is: when she became one with heaviness due to the size of the child in her womb. It was read *famarrat bihi* with lightening, that is, she was disturbed by it. It was also read *famarat bihi* from *al-mawr*, which is coming and going. It was also said that the meaning is: she continued with it.

The reading with lightening has been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas and Yahya ibn Ya'mur. The reading *famarat* has been narrated from Abd Allah ibn Umar. It was also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he read *fastamarrat bihi* (she continued with it).

His saying: ﴿They both called upon God, their Lord﴾. This is the answer to *lamma* (when). That is: Adam and Eve called upon God, their Lord and the owner of their affairs: ﴿If You give us a righteous child﴾, that is, a righteous son. The lam is the answer to an omitted oath, and ﴿we will surely be among the grateful﴾ is the answer to the oath, serving in place of the answer to the condition, meaning: among those who are grateful to You for this blessing. In this supplication is evidence that they both knew that what had happened in Eve's womb from the effect of that intercourse was of their own kind, and they knew that offspring affected by that cause would be established.

﴿So when He gave them﴾ what they asked for, a righteous child, and answered their supplication, ﴿they made for Him partners in what He had given them﴾.

Many exegetes said: Iblis came to Eve and said to her: If you give birth to a child, name him after me. She said: And what is your name? He said: al-Harith. He would not have named himself to her, or she would have recognized him. So she named him Abd al-Harith. This was an act of associating in naming, not an association in worship. They only intended that al-Harith was the cause of the child's deliverance, just as a man names himself "servant of his guest," as Hatim al-Ta'i said:

*"I am indeed a servant of the guest as long as he stays, and there is nothing in me but that trait of the servant."*

Other exegetes said: the ones who make partners in what He gave them are the human race, as happened with the polytheists among them, and it was not from Adam and Eve. This is indicated by the plural pronoun in His saying: ﴿Exalted is God above what they associate﴾.

Some exegetes went to the view that the meaning of ﴿from one soul﴾ is from one form and one shape, ﴿and made from it its mate﴾ meaning of its kind, ﴿and when he covered her﴾ means the male kind covered the female kind. On this view, Adam and Eve are not mentioned in the verse, and the dual pronouns refer to the two kinds.

We have already pointed to something similar to this and mentioned that it is contrary to the better view for several reasons. Among them: ﴿and made from it its mate﴾ applies only to Eve. Among them: ﴿they called upon God, their Lord﴾, for every child born between the two kinds does not have this supplication from them at the approach of its delivery.

The people of Medina and Asim read *shirkan* (singular), and Abu 'Amr and the rest of the people of Kufa read it in the plural.

Al-Akhfash Sa'id denied the first reading. It has been answered that it is correct by omitting the genitive-modified noun: that is, they made for Him one who has a share (*dha shirk*), or those who have a share (*dhawi shirk*).

The interrogative in ﴿Do they associate what creates nothing?﴾ is for rebuke and reproach, meaning: how do they make for God a partner who creates nothing and is not able to bring benefit to them or repel harm from them?

His saying: ﴿while they themselves are created﴾ is conjoined to ﴿what creates nothing﴾, and the pronoun refers to the partners who create nothing. That is: these whom they made partners, from idols or devils, are themselves created. Their plural is the plural of rational beings because those who made them partners believed them to be such.

﴿And they cannot help them﴾, that is, those who made them partners, ﴿with victory﴾ if he seeks it from them, ﴿nor can they help themselves﴾ if something befalls them from others. Whoever is unable to help himself is all the more unable to help others.

Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Hamal ibn Abi Qays and Shamul ibn Zayd said to the Messenger of God ﷺ: Tell us when the Hour will be, if you are a prophet as you say, for we know what it is. So God revealed: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when is its settling? Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾ up to His saying: ﴿But most people do not know.﴾"

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، وابن جرير، عن قتادة: ﴿أيان مرساها﴾ أي متى قيامها؟ ﴿يسألونك عن الساعة أيان مرساها قل إنما علمها عند ربي لا يجليها لوقتها إلا هو﴾. قال: قالت قريش: يا محمد، أسرّ إلينا الساعة لما بيننا وبينك من القرابة؟ فقال: ﴿يسألونك كأنك حفي عنها قل إنما علمها عند الله﴾. وذُكر لنا أن نبي الله ﷺ كان يقول: «تهيج الساعة بالناس والرجل يسقي على ماشيته، والرجل يصلح حوضه، والرجل يخفض ميزانه ويرفعه، والرجل يقيم سلعته في السوق، قضاء الله لا تأتيكم إلا بغتة».

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿أيان مرساها﴾ قال: منتهاها.

وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة، وعبد بن حميد، وابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، عن مجاهد: ﴿لا يجليها لوقتها إلا هو﴾ يقول: لا يأتي بها إلا الله.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، عن قتادة، في الآية قال: هو يجليها لوقتها، لا يعلم ذلك إلا الله.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿ثقلت في السماوات والأرض﴾ قال: ليس شيء من الخلق إلا يصيبه من ضرر يوم القيامة.

وأخرج عبد الرزاق، وابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، عن قتادة، في قوله: ﴿ثقلت في السماوات والأرض﴾ قال: ثقل علمها على أهل السماوات والأرض، يقول: كبرت عليهم.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وأبو الشيخ، عن ابن جريج في قوله: ﴿ثقلت في السماوات والأرض﴾ (p-519) قال: إذا جاءت انشقت السماء، وانتثرت النجوم، وكوِّرت الشمس، وسُيِّرت الجبال، وما يصيب الأرض، وكان ما قال الله سبحانه، فذلك ثقلها فيهما.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، عن مجاهد في قوله: ﴿لا تأتيكم إلا بغتة﴾ قال: فجأة، وأنتم آمنون.

وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة، وعبد بن حميد، وابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، والبيهقي في البعث، عن مجاهد في قوله: ﴿كأنك حفي عنها﴾ قال: استحفيت عنها السؤال حتى علمتها.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿كأنك حفي عنها﴾ يقول: كأنك عالم بها، أي لست تعلمها.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، والبيهقي، عنه: ﴿كأنك حفي عنها﴾ قال: لطيف بها.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، وابن مردويه، والبيهقي، عنه أيضًا: ﴿كأنك حفي عنها﴾ يقول: كأن بينك وبينهم مودة، كأنك صديق لهم. قال: لما سأل الناس محمدًا ﷺ عن الساعة سألوه سؤال قوم كأنهم يُرَوْن أن محمدًا حفي بهم، فأوحى الله إليه ﴿إنما علمها عند الله﴾ استأثر بعلمها، فلم يُطلع ملكًا ولا رسولًا.

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، عن عمرو بن دينار قال: كان ابن عباس يقرأ: «كأنك حفي بها».

وأخرج ابن جرير، وأبو الشيخ، عن ابن جريج: ﴿قل لا أملك لنفسي نفعًا ولا ضرًا﴾ قال: الهدى والضلالة. ﴿ولو كنت أعلم الغيب﴾ متى أموت ﴿لاستكثرت من الخير﴾ قال: العمل الصالح.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿ولو كنت أعلم الغيب لاستكثرت من الخير﴾ قال: لعلمت إذا اشتريت شيئًا ما أربح فيه فلا أبيع شيئًا لا ربح فيه. ﴿وما مسني السوء﴾ قال: لاجتنبت ما يكون من الشر قبل أن يكون.

وأخرج أحمد، والترمذي، وحسّنه، وأبو يعلى، وابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، والرُّوياني، والطبراني، وأبو الشيخ، والحاكم وصححه، وابن مردويه، عن سمرة، عن النبي ﷺ قال: «لما ولدت حواء طاف بها إبليس، وكان لا يعيش لها ولد، فقال: سمّيه عبد الحارث فإنه يعيش، فسمّته عبد الحارث فعاش، فكان ذلك من وحي الشيطان وأمره».

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، وابن جرير، وابن مردويه، عن سمرة في قوله: ﴿فلما آتاهما صالحًا جعلا له شركاء﴾ قال: سمّياه عبد الحارث.

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، وأبو الشيخ، عن أُبيّ بن كعب نحو حديث سمرة المرفوع، موقوفًا عليه.

وأخرج سعيد بن منصور، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، عن ابن عباس، قال: حملت حواء فأتاها إبليس فقال: إني صاحبكما الذي أخرجتكما من الجنة، لتطيعنّني أو لأجعلنّ له قرني أيل، فيخرج من بطنك فيشقه، ولأفعلنّ ولأفعلنّ، يخوفهما. سمّياه عبد الحارث، فأبيا أن يطيعاه فخرج ميتًا، ثم حملت فأتاهما أيضًا فقال مثل ذلك، فأبيا أن يطيعاه فخرج ميتًا، ثم حملت فأتاهما فذكر لهما فأدركهما حب الولد فسمّياه عبد الحارث، فذلك قوله: ﴿جعلا له شركاء فيما آتاهما﴾.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وأبو الشيخ، عن الحسن في الآية قال: كان هذا في بعض أهل الملل، وليس بآدم.

وأخرج أبو الشيخ، وابن مردويه، عن سمرة في قوله: ﴿حملت حملًا خفيفًا﴾ لم يستبن ﴿فمرت به﴾ لما استبان حملها.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿فمرت به﴾ قال: فشكّت أحملت أم لا.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وأبو الشيخ، عن أيوب قال: سُئل الحسن عن قوله: ﴿فمرت به﴾ فقال: لو كنت عربيًا لعرفتها، إنما هي استمرت بالحمل.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، عن السدي، في قوله: ﴿حملت حملًا خفيفًا﴾ قال: هي النطفة. ﴿فمرت به﴾ يقول: استمرت به.

وأخرج سعيد بن منصور، وابن المنذر، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿فمرت به﴾ قال: فاستمرت به.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، عن ميمون بن مهران: ﴿فمرت به﴾ يقول: استخفّته.

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، وابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، عن أبي صالح في قوله: ﴿لئن آتيتنا صالحًا﴾ فقال: أشفقا أن يكون بهيمة، فقالا: لئن آتيتنا بشرًا سويًا.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، عن مجاهد نحوه.

وأخرج عبد الرزاق، وابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، عن الحسن في الآية قال: غلامًا سويًا.

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿جعلا له شركاء﴾ قال: كان شريكًا في الطاعة، ولم يكن شريكًا في العبادة.

وأخرج ابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، عنه قال: ما أشرك آدم، إن أولها شكر، وآخرها مثل ضربه لمن بعده.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، عن السدي، في قوله: ﴿فتعالى الله عما يشركون﴾ هذا فصل من آية آدم خاصة، في آلهة العرب.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، عن أبي مالك نحوه.

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، وأبو الشيخ، عن الحسن في الآية قال: هذا في الكفار يدعون الله، فإذا آتاهما صالحًا هوّدا أو نصّرا. ثم قال: ﴿أيشركون ما لا يخلق شيئًا وهم يُخلقون﴾ يقول: يطيعون ما لا يخلق شيئًا، وهي الشياطين، لا تخلق شيئًا وهي تُخلق. ﴿ولا يستطيعون لهم نصرًا﴾ يقول: لمن يدعوهم.

(p-517) His saying: ﴿They ask you about the Hour﴾. The askers were the Jews, and it was said they were the Quraysh. "The Hour" (al-sa'ah) is the Resurrection, and it is one of the names that became dominant for it. It is applied to the Resurrection either because it comes suddenly or because its reckoning is swift. "Ayyan" (when) is an adverb of time (zarf zaman) that is indeclinable (mabni) on the fatha. The reciter said:

*"When will my need be fulfilled? When? Do you not see that its ripeness is due?"*

Its meaning is the same as *mata* (when), and its derivation is from *ayy*. It was also said to be from *ayna* (where).

Al-Sulami read *"iyyan"* with a kasra on the hamza. It is then in the position of a predicate (khabar). ﴿Its settling﴾ (mursaha) is the subject (mubtada') according to Sibawayh. *Mursaha* with a damma on the *mim* means the time of its establishment, from *arsaha Allah*, meaning God fixed it. With a fatha on the *mim* it comes from *rasat*, meaning it became firm. From this is ﴿and cooking pots fixed firmly﴾ (Saba': 13), and from it is *rasa al-jabal*, meaning the mountain became fixed.

The meaning is: when will God settle it, that is, establish it and bring it about. The apparent sense of ﴿They ask you about the Hour﴾ is that the question concerns the Hour itself, and the apparent sense of ﴿When is its settling?﴾ is that the question concerns its time. From all of this it results that the question mentioned is about the Hour in terms of its occurrence at a specified time. Then God, glorified is He, commanded him to answer them with His saying: ﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾. That is, its knowledge, in terms of its occurrence, is with God alone, and no one else knows it or is guided to it. ﴿None will reveal it at its time except Him﴾. That is, none will make it manifest at its time or uncover it except God, glorified is He. *Tajliyah* means making a thing manifest. It is said: *jalla li fulan al-khabar*, meaning he made the news manifest and clear. In God's exclusive possession of the knowledge of the Hour there is great wisdom and profound design, like all the other things that God concealed and kept exclusively to His knowledge.

This sentence confirms the content of the one before it.

His saying: ﴿It has been heavy upon the heavens and the earth﴾. It was said that the meaning is: since its knowledge was hidden from the people of the heavens and the earth, it was heavy, because whatever knowledge is hidden is heavy on hearts. It was also said that the meaning is: the heavens and the earth cannot bear it because of its magnitude, since the sky will split, the stars will scatter, and the seas will dry up. It was also said: its description became great for them. It was also said: the question about it became heavy. This sentence also confirms the content of what precedes it. ﴿It will not come upon you except suddenly﴾, that is, except unexpectedly while you are heedless. *Al-baghtah* is a verbal noun in the position of a circumstantial clause (hal). This sentence is like the one before it in confirmation.

His saying: ﴿They ask you as though you were informed about it﴾. Ibn Faris said: *al-hafiy* is one who knows a thing, and *al-hafiy* is also one who presses in questioning. From this is the saying of al-A'sha:

*"If you ask about me, then how many a questioner, eager about al-A'sha, has asked where he ascended."*

It is said: *ahfa fi al-mas'alah* and *fi al-talab*, so he is *muhfin*. *Hafiy* is an intensive form like *mukhassib* and *khasib*.

The meaning is: they ask you about the Hour as though you knew it, or as though he were pressing in questioning about it and asking much about it. The simile clause is in a position of accusative (nasb) as a circumstantial clause, meaning they ask you while your state is made like the state of one who is informed about it. It was also said that the meaning is: they ask you about it as though you were eager for them, that is, eager for their goodness and pleased with their asking.

The first meaning is the meaning of the Qur'anic arrangement according to the requirement of the Arabic style.

His saying: ﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾. God, glorified is He, commanded him to repeat what he had already answered them, to establish and confirm the ruling. It was also said that it is not a repetition, but rather one of them means exclusive possession of its occurrence, and the other means exclusive possession of its very nature. ﴿But most people do not know﴾ this exclusive possession by God and the absence of knowledge of it among His creation. No near-angel and no sent prophet knows it.

His saying: ﴿Say: I possess for myself no benefit or harm except what God wills﴾. This sentence contains a confirmation of what preceded regarding his lack of knowledge of the Hour, when it will be and when it will occur. For if he does not have power to bring about benefit for himself or to repel harm from himself except what God, glorified is He, wills of benefit to him and repelling from him, then it is all the more so that he has no power to know what God has kept exclusively to His knowledge. In this there is a demonstration of servitude and an acknowledgment of inability regarding matters that are not the concern of servants, and an admission of weakness in claiming what is not his. In it is the greatest deterrent and the most eloquent admonition for whoever claims for himself what is not his concern and appropriates knowledge of the unseen through fortune-telling, sand divination, pebble casting, or augury. Then he confirmed and established this with His saying: ﴿And had I known the unseen, I would have acquired much good﴾. That is: if I knew the category of the unseen, I would have pursued what contains good and brought it to myself, and I would have guarded against what contains evil so that it would not touch me. But I am a servant who does not know what is with my Lord, nor what He has decreed for me and destined for me. So how could I know other than that and burden myself with knowing it?
