It was also said that the meaning is: had I known what God, mighty and majestic, wills of me before He informs me of it, I would have done it. It was also said: had I known when victory in war would be mine, I would have fought and not been defeated. It was also said: had I known the unseen, I would have answered every question asked of me. The better view is to take the verse in its generality, so these matters and others are included under it. It has also been said that ﴿and evil has not touched me﴾ is a new independent statement, meaning there is not in me what you claim of madness. The better view is that it is connected to what precedes it, and the meaning is: had I known the unseen, evil would not have touched me, and I would have guarded against it, as we have mentioned.

His saying: ﴿I am not but a warner and a bringer of good tidings to a people who believe﴾. That is: I am only a conveyor from God of His rulings, by which I warn one people and give good tidings to others, and I do not know the unseen of God, glorified is He. The lam in *li-qawmin* is connected to both attributes: a bringer of good tidings to a people, and a warner to a people. It was also said that it is connected to *bashir* (bringer of good tidings), and what is connected to *nadhir* (warner) is omitted, meaning: a warner to a people who disbelieve, and a bringer of good tidings to a people who believe.

His saying: ﴿He is the One who created you from one soul﴾. This is an independent statement containing a mention of God's blessings upon His servants and their failure to repay them with what is obligatory of gratitude and acknowledgment of servitude, and that He alone is singular in divinity.

The majority of exegetes said: by "one soul" is meant Adam. His saying ﴿and made from it its mate﴾ is conjoined to ﴿created you﴾, meaning: He is the One who created you from the soul of Adam and made from this soul its mate, who is Eve, whom He created from one of his ribs. It was also said that the meaning of ﴿made from it﴾ is from its kind, as in His saying: ﴿He made for you from yourselves mates﴾ (al-Nahl: 72). The first is better. ﴿So that he might find rest in her﴾ is the reason for the making: that is, He made her from him so that he would find rest and comfort in her and be at peace with her, for a kind is most at rest with its own kind and most at ease with it. This was in Paradise, as the reports have narrated. Then God, glorified is He, began with another state that existed between them in this world after their descent, and He said: ﴿So when he covered her﴾. *Al-taghashshi* is a metaphor for intercourse, that is, when he had intercourse with her. ﴿She carried a light burden﴾, meaning she conceived after intercourse. He described it as light because at the time of the drop of semen it is lighter than when it becomes a clot, and when it is a clot it is lighter than when it is a lump of flesh, and when it is a lump it is lighter than what comes after. It was also said that this pregnancy was light for her from its beginning to its end, and she did not find any heaviness in it as pregnant women do. This is because of His saying: ﴿and she continued with it﴾, that is, she went on with that pregnancy, standing, sitting, and going about her needs without finding heaviness in it. The first interpretation is better because of His saying: ﴿then when she became heavy﴾, for its meaning is: when she became one with heaviness due to the size of the child in her womb. It was read *famarrat bihi* with lightening, that is, she was disturbed by it. It was also read *famarat bihi* from *al-mawr*, which is coming and going. It was also said that the meaning is: she continued with it.

The reading with lightening has been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas and Yahya ibn Ya'mur. The reading *famarat* has been narrated from Abd Allah ibn Umar. It was also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he read *fastamarrat bihi* (she continued with it).

His saying: ﴿They both called upon God, their Lord﴾. This is the answer to *lamma* (when). That is: Adam and Eve called upon God, their Lord and the owner of their affairs: ﴿If You give us a righteous child﴾, that is, a righteous son. The lam is the answer to an omitted oath, and ﴿we will surely be among the grateful﴾ is the answer to the oath, serving in place of the answer to the condition, meaning: among those who are grateful to You for this blessing. In this supplication is evidence that they both knew that what had happened in Eve's womb from the effect of that intercourse was of their own kind, and they knew that offspring affected by that cause would be established.

﴿So when He gave them﴾ what they asked for, a righteous child, and answered their supplication, ﴿they made for Him partners in what He had given them﴾.

Many exegetes said: Iblis came to Eve and said to her: If you give birth to a child, name him after me. She said: And what is your name? He said: al-Harith. He would not have named himself to her, or she would have recognized him. So she named him Abd al-Harith. This was an act of associating in naming, not an association in worship. They only intended that al-Harith was the cause of the child's deliverance, just as a man names himself "servant of his guest," as Hatim al-Ta'i said:

*"I am indeed a servant of the guest as long as he stays, and there is nothing in me but that trait of the servant."*

Other exegetes said: the ones who make partners in what He gave them are the human race, as happened with the polytheists among them, and it was not from Adam and Eve. This is indicated by the plural pronoun in His saying: ﴿Exalted is God above what they associate﴾.

Some exegetes went to the view that the meaning of ﴿from one soul﴾ is from one form and one shape, ﴿and made from it its mate﴾ meaning of its kind, ﴿and when he covered her﴾ means the male kind covered the female kind. On this view, Adam and Eve are not mentioned in the verse, and the dual pronouns refer to the two kinds.

We have already pointed to something similar to this and mentioned that it is contrary to the better view for several reasons. Among them: ﴿and made from it its mate﴾ applies only to Eve. Among them: ﴿they called upon God, their Lord﴾, for every child born between the two kinds does not have this supplication from them at the approach of its delivery.

The people of Medina and Asim read *shirkan* (singular), and Abu 'Amr and the rest of the people of Kufa read it in the plural.

Al-Akhfash Sa'id denied the first reading. It has been answered that it is correct by omitting the genitive-modified noun: that is, they made for Him one who has a share (*dha shirk*), or those who have a share (*dhawi shirk*).

The interrogative in ﴿Do they associate what creates nothing?﴾ is for rebuke and reproach, meaning: how do they make for God a partner who creates nothing and is not able to bring benefit to them or repel harm from them?

His saying: ﴿while they themselves are created﴾ is conjoined to ﴿what creates nothing﴾, and the pronoun refers to the partners who create nothing. That is: these whom they made partners, from idols or devils, are themselves created. Their plural is the plural of rational beings because those who made them partners believed them to be such.

﴿And they cannot help them﴾, that is, those who made them partners, ﴿with victory﴾ if he seeks it from them, ﴿nor can they help themselves﴾ if something befalls them from others. Whoever is unable to help himself is all the more unable to help others.

Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Hamal ibn Abi Qays and Shamul ibn Zayd said to the Messenger of God ﷺ: Tell us when the Hour will be, if you are a prophet as you say, for we know what it is. So God revealed: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when is its settling? Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾ up to His saying: ﴿But most people do not know.﴾"

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، وابن جرير، عن قتادة: ﴿أيان مرساها﴾ أي متى قيامها؟ ﴿يسألونك عن الساعة أيان مرساها قل إنما علمها عند ربي لا يجليها لوقتها إلا هو﴾. قال: قالت قريش: يا محمد، أسرّ إلينا الساعة لما بيننا وبينك من القرابة؟ فقال: ﴿يسألونك كأنك حفي عنها قل إنما علمها عند الله﴾. وذُكر لنا أن نبي الله ﷺ كان يقول: «تهيج الساعة بالناس والرجل يسقي على ماشيته، والرجل يصلح حوضه، والرجل يخفض ميزانه ويرفعه، والرجل يقيم سلعته في السوق، قضاء الله لا تأتيكم إلا بغتة».

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿أيان مرساها﴾ قال: منتهاها.

وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة، وعبد بن حميد، وابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، عن مجاهد: ﴿لا يجليها لوقتها إلا هو﴾ يقول: لا يأتي بها إلا الله.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، عن قتادة، في الآية قال: هو يجليها لوقتها، لا يعلم ذلك إلا الله.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿ثقلت في السماوات والأرض﴾ قال: ليس شيء من الخلق إلا يصيبه من ضرر يوم القيامة.

وأخرج عبد الرزاق، وابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، عن قتادة، في قوله: ﴿ثقلت في السماوات والأرض﴾ قال: ثقل علمها على أهل السماوات والأرض، يقول: كبرت عليهم.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وأبو الشيخ، عن ابن جريج في قوله: ﴿ثقلت في السماوات والأرض﴾ (p-519) قال: إذا جاءت انشقت السماء، وانتثرت النجوم، وكوِّرت الشمس، وسُيِّرت الجبال، وما يصيب الأرض، وكان ما قال الله سبحانه، فذلك ثقلها فيهما.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، عن مجاهد في قوله: ﴿لا تأتيكم إلا بغتة﴾ قال: فجأة، وأنتم آمنون.

وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة، وعبد بن حميد، وابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، والبيهقي في البعث، عن مجاهد في قوله: ﴿كأنك حفي عنها﴾ قال: استحفيت عنها السؤال حتى علمتها.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿كأنك حفي عنها﴾ يقول: كأنك عالم بها، أي لست تعلمها.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، والبيهقي، عنه: ﴿كأنك حفي عنها﴾ قال: لطيف بها.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، وابن مردويه، والبيهقي، عنه أيضًا: ﴿كأنك حفي عنها﴾ يقول: كأن بينك وبينهم مودة، كأنك صديق لهم. قال: لما سأل الناس محمدًا ﷺ عن الساعة سألوه سؤال قوم كأنهم يُرَوْن أن محمدًا حفي بهم، فأوحى الله إليه ﴿إنما علمها عند الله﴾ استأثر بعلمها، فلم يُطلع ملكًا ولا رسولًا.

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، عن عمرو بن دينار قال: كان ابن عباس يقرأ: «كأنك حفي بها».

وأخرج ابن جرير، وأبو الشيخ، عن ابن جريج: ﴿قل لا أملك لنفسي نفعًا ولا ضرًا﴾ قال: الهدى والضلالة. ﴿ولو كنت أعلم الغيب﴾ متى أموت ﴿لاستكثرت من الخير﴾ قال: العمل الصالح.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿ولو كنت أعلم الغيب لاستكثرت من الخير﴾ قال: لعلمت إذا اشتريت شيئًا ما أربح فيه فلا أبيع شيئًا لا ربح فيه. ﴿وما مسني السوء﴾ قال: لاجتنبت ما يكون من الشر قبل أن يكون.

وأخرج أحمد، والترمذي، وحسّنه، وأبو يعلى، وابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، والرُّوياني، والطبراني، وأبو الشيخ، والحاكم وصححه، وابن مردويه، عن سمرة، عن النبي ﷺ قال: «لما ولدت حواء طاف بها إبليس، وكان لا يعيش لها ولد، فقال: سمّيه عبد الحارث فإنه يعيش، فسمّته عبد الحارث فعاش، فكان ذلك من وحي الشيطان وأمره».

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، وابن جرير، وابن مردويه، عن سمرة في قوله: ﴿فلما آتاهما صالحًا جعلا له شركاء﴾ قال: سمّياه عبد الحارث.

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، وأبو الشيخ، عن أُبيّ بن كعب نحو حديث سمرة المرفوع، موقوفًا عليه.

وأخرج سعيد بن منصور، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، عن ابن عباس، قال: حملت حواء فأتاها إبليس فقال: إني صاحبكما الذي أخرجتكما من الجنة، لتطيعنّني أو لأجعلنّ له قرني أيل، فيخرج من بطنك فيشقه، ولأفعلنّ ولأفعلنّ، يخوفهما. سمّياه عبد الحارث، فأبيا أن يطيعاه فخرج ميتًا، ثم حملت فأتاهما أيضًا فقال مثل ذلك، فأبيا أن يطيعاه فخرج ميتًا، ثم حملت فأتاهما فذكر لهما فأدركهما حب الولد فسمّياه عبد الحارث، فذلك قوله: ﴿جعلا له شركاء فيما آتاهما﴾.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وأبو الشيخ، عن الحسن في الآية قال: كان هذا في بعض أهل الملل، وليس بآدم.

وأخرج أبو الشيخ، وابن مردويه، عن سمرة في قوله: ﴿حملت حملًا خفيفًا﴾ لم يستبن ﴿فمرت به﴾ لما استبان حملها.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿فمرت به﴾ قال: فشكّت أحملت أم لا.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وأبو الشيخ، عن أيوب قال: سُئل الحسن عن قوله: ﴿فمرت به﴾ فقال: لو كنت عربيًا لعرفتها، إنما هي استمرت بالحمل.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، عن السدي، في قوله: ﴿حملت حملًا خفيفًا﴾ قال: هي النطفة. ﴿فمرت به﴾ يقول: استمرت به.

وأخرج سعيد بن منصور، وابن المنذر، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿فمرت به﴾ قال: فاستمرت به.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، عن ميمون بن مهران: ﴿فمرت به﴾ يقول: استخفّته.

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، وابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، عن أبي صالح في قوله: ﴿لئن آتيتنا صالحًا﴾ فقال: أشفقا أن يكون بهيمة، فقالا: لئن آتيتنا بشرًا سويًا.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، عن مجاهد نحوه.

وأخرج عبد الرزاق، وابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، عن الحسن في الآية قال: غلامًا سويًا.

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿جعلا له شركاء﴾ قال: كان شريكًا في الطاعة، ولم يكن شريكًا في العبادة.

وأخرج ابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، عنه قال: ما أشرك آدم، إن أولها شكر، وآخرها مثل ضربه لمن بعده.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، عن السدي، في قوله: ﴿فتعالى الله عما يشركون﴾ هذا فصل من آية آدم خاصة، في آلهة العرب.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، عن أبي مالك نحوه.

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، وأبو الشيخ، عن الحسن في الآية قال: هذا في الكفار يدعون الله، فإذا آتاهما صالحًا هوّدا أو نصّرا. ثم قال: ﴿أيشركون ما لا يخلق شيئًا وهم يُخلقون﴾ يقول: يطيعون ما لا يخلق شيئًا، وهي الشياطين، لا تخلق شيئًا وهي تُخلق. ﴿ولا يستطيعون لهم نصرًا﴾ يقول: لمن يدعوهم.

(p-517) His saying: ﴿They ask you about the Hour﴾. The askers were the Jews, and it was said they were the Quraysh. "The Hour" (al-sa'ah) is the Resurrection, and it is one of the names that became dominant for it. It is applied to the Resurrection either because it comes suddenly or because its reckoning is swift. "Ayyan" (when) is an adverb of time (zarf zaman) that is indeclinable (mabni) on the fatha. The reciter said:

*"When will my need be fulfilled? When? Do you not see that its ripeness is due?"*

Its meaning is the same as *mata* (when), and its derivation is from *ayy*. It was also said to be from *ayna* (where).

Al-Sulami read *"iyyan"* with a kasra on the hamza. It is then in the position of a predicate (khabar). ﴿Its settling﴾ (mursaha) is the subject (mubtada') according to Sibawayh. *Mursaha* with a damma on the *mim* means the time of its establishment, from *arsaha Allah*, meaning God fixed it. With a fatha on the *mim* it comes from *rasat*, meaning it became firm. From this is ﴿and cooking pots fixed firmly﴾ (Saba': 13), and from it is *rasa al-jabal*, meaning the mountain became fixed.

The meaning is: when will God settle it, that is, establish it and bring it about. The apparent sense of ﴿They ask you about the Hour﴾ is that the question concerns the Hour itself, and the apparent sense of ﴿When is its settling?﴾ is that the question concerns its time. From all of this it results that the question mentioned is about the Hour in terms of its occurrence at a specified time. Then God, glorified is He, commanded him to answer them with His saying: ﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾. That is, its knowledge, in terms of its occurrence, is with God alone, and no one else knows it or is guided to it. ﴿None will reveal it at its time except Him﴾. That is, none will make it manifest at its time or uncover it except God, glorified is He. *Tajliyah* means making a thing manifest. It is said: *jalla li fulan al-khabar*, meaning he made the news manifest and clear. In God's exclusive possession of the knowledge of the Hour there is great wisdom and profound design, like all the other things that God concealed and kept exclusively to His knowledge.

This sentence confirms the content of the one before it.

His saying: ﴿It has been heavy upon the heavens and the earth﴾. It was said that the meaning is: since its knowledge was hidden from the people of the heavens and the earth, it was heavy, because whatever knowledge is hidden is heavy on hearts. It was also said that the meaning is: the heavens and the earth cannot bear it because of its magnitude, since the sky will split, the stars will scatter, and the seas will dry up. It was also said: its description became great for them. It was also said: the question about it became heavy. This sentence also confirms the content of what precedes it. ﴿It will not come upon you except suddenly﴾, that is, except unexpectedly while you are heedless. *Al-baghtah* is a verbal noun in the position of a circumstantial clause (hal). This sentence is like the one before it in confirmation.

His saying: ﴿They ask you as though you were informed about it﴾. Ibn Faris said: *al-hafiy* is one who knows a thing, and *al-hafiy* is also one who presses in questioning. From this is the saying of al-A'sha:

*"If you ask about me, then how many a questioner, eager about al-A'sha, has asked where he ascended."*

It is said: *ahfa fi al-mas'alah* and *fi al-talab*, so he is *muhfin*. *Hafiy* is an intensive form like *mukhassib* and *khasib*.

The meaning is: they ask you about the Hour as though you knew it, or as though he were pressing in questioning about it and asking much about it. The simile clause is in a position of accusative (nasb) as a circumstantial clause, meaning they ask you while your state is made like the state of one who is informed about it. It was also said that the meaning is: they ask you about it as though you were eager for them, that is, eager for their goodness and pleased with their asking.

The first meaning is the meaning of the Qur'anic arrangement according to the requirement of the Arabic style.

His saying: ﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾. God, glorified is He, commanded him to repeat what he had already answered them, to establish and confirm the ruling. It was also said that it is not a repetition, but rather one of them means exclusive possession of its occurrence, and the other means exclusive possession of its very nature. ﴿But most people do not know﴾ this exclusive possession by God and the absence of knowledge of it among His creation. No near-angel and no sent prophet knows it.

His saying: ﴿Say: I possess for myself no benefit or harm except what God wills﴾. This sentence contains a confirmation of what preceded regarding his lack of knowledge of the Hour, when it will be and when it will occur. For if he does not have power to bring about benefit for himself or to repel harm from himself except what God, glorified is He, wills of benefit to him and repelling from him, then it is all the more so that he has no power to know what God has kept exclusively to His knowledge. In this there is a demonstration of servitude and an acknowledgment of inability regarding matters that are not the concern of servants, and an admission of weakness in claiming what is not his. In it is the greatest deterrent and the most eloquent admonition for whoever claims for himself what is not his concern and appropriates knowledge of the unseen through fortune-telling, sand divination, pebble casting, or augury. Then he confirmed and established this with His saying: ﴿And had I known the unseen, I would have acquired much good﴾. That is: if I knew the category of the unseen, I would have pursued what contains good and brought it to myself, and I would have guarded against what contains evil so that it would not touch me. But I am a servant who does not know what is with my Lord, nor what He has decreed for me and destined for me. So how could I know other than that and burden myself with knowing it? It was also said that the meaning is: had I known what God, mighty and majestic, wills of me before He informs me of it, I would have done it. It was also said: had I known when victory in war would be mine, I would have fought and not been defeated. It was also said: had I known the unseen, I would have answered every question asked of me. The better view is to take the verse in its generality, so these matters and others are included under it. It has also been said that ﴿and evil has not touched me﴾ is a new independent statement, meaning there is not in me what you claim of madness. The better view is that it is connected to what precedes it, and the meaning is: had I known the unseen, evil would not have touched me, and I would have guarded against it, as we have mentioned.

His saying: ﴿I am not but a warner and a bringer of good tidings to a people who believe﴾. That is: I am only a conveyor from God of His rulings, by which I warn one people and give good tidings to others, and I do not know the unseen of God, glorified is He. The lam in *li-qawmin* is connected to both attributes: a bringer of good tidings to a people, and a warner to a people. It was also said that it is connected to *bashir* (bringer of good tidings), and what is connected to *nadhir* (warner) is omitted, meaning: a warner to a people who disbelieve, and a bringer of good tidings to a people who believe.

His saying: ﴿He is the One who created you from one soul﴾. This is an independent statement containing a mention of God's blessings upon His servants and their failure to repay them with what is obligatory of gratitude and acknowledgment of servitude, and that He alone is singular in divinity.

The majority of exegetes said: by "one soul" is meant Adam. His saying ﴿and made from it its mate﴾ is conjoined to ﴿created you﴾, meaning: He is the One who created you from the soul of Adam and made from this soul its mate, who is Eve, whom He created from one of his ribs. It was also said that the meaning of ﴿made from it﴾ is from its kind, as in His saying: ﴿He made for you from yourselves mates﴾ (al-Nahl: 72). The first is better. ﴿So that he might find rest in her﴾ is the reason for the making: that is, He made her from him so that he would find rest and comfort in her and be at peace with her, for a kind is most at rest with its own kind and most at ease with it. This was in Paradise, as the reports have narrated. Then God, glorified is He, began with another state that existed between them in this world after their descent, and He said: ﴿So when he covered her﴾. *Al-taghashshi* is a metaphor for intercourse, that is, when he had intercourse with her. ﴿She carried a light burden﴾, meaning she conceived after intercourse. He described it as light because at the time of the drop of semen it is lighter than when it becomes a clot, and when it is a clot it is lighter than when it is a lump of flesh, and when it is a lump it is lighter than what comes after. It was also said that this pregnancy was light for her from its beginning to its end, and she did not find any heaviness in it as pregnant women do. This is because of His saying: ﴿and she continued with it﴾, that is, she went on with that pregnancy, standing, sitting, and going about her needs without finding heaviness in it. The first interpretation is better because of His saying: ﴿then when she became heavy﴾, for its meaning is: when she became one with heaviness due to the size of the child in her womb. It was read *famarrat bihi* with lightening, that is, she was disturbed by it. It was also read *famarat bihi* from *al-mawr*, which is coming and going. It was also said that the meaning is: she continued with it.

The reading with lightening has been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas and Yahya ibn Ya'mur. The reading *famarat* has been narrated from Abd Allah ibn Umar. It was also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he read *fastamarrat bihi* (she continued with it).

His saying: ﴿They both called upon God, their Lord﴾. This is the answer to *lamma* (when). That is: Adam and Eve called upon God, their Lord and the owner of their affairs: ﴿If You give us a righteous child﴾, that is, a righteous son. The lam is the answer to an omitted oath, and ﴿we will surely be among the grateful﴾ is the answer to the oath, serving in place of the answer to the condition, meaning: among those who are grateful to You for this blessing. In this supplication is evidence that they both knew that what had happened in Eve's womb from the effect of that intercourse was of their own kind, and they knew that offspring affected by that cause would be established.

﴿So when He gave them﴾ what they asked for, a righteous child, and answered their supplication, ﴿they made for Him partners in what He had given them﴾.

Many exegetes said: Iblis came to Eve and said to her: If you give birth to a child, name him after me. She said: And what is your name? He said: al-Harith. He would not have named himself to her, or she would have recognized him. So she named him Abd al-Harith. This was an act of associating in naming, not an association in worship. They only intended that al-Harith was the cause of the child's deliverance, just as a man names himself "servant of his guest," as Hatim al-Ta'i said:

*"I am indeed a servant of the guest as long as he stays, and there is nothing in me but that trait of the servant."*

Other exegetes said: the ones who make partners in what He gave them are the human race, as happened with the polytheists among them, and it was not from Adam and Eve. This is indicated by the plural pronoun in His saying: ﴿Exalted is God above what they associate﴾.

Some exegetes went to the view that the meaning of ﴿from one soul﴾ is from one form and one shape, ﴿and made from it its mate﴾ meaning of its kind, ﴿and when he covered her﴾ means the male kind covered the female kind. On this view, Adam and Eve are not mentioned in the verse, and the dual pronouns refer to the two kinds.

We have already pointed to something similar to this and mentioned that it is contrary to the better view for several reasons. Among them: ﴿and made from it its mate﴾ applies only to Eve. Among them: ﴿they called upon God, their Lord﴾, for every child born between the two kinds does not have this supplication from them at the approach of its delivery.

The people of Medina and Asim read *shirkan* (singular), and Abu 'Amr and the rest of the people of Kufa read it in the plural.

Al-Akhfash Sa'id denied the first reading. It has been answered that it is correct by omitting the genitive-modified noun: that is, they made for Him one who has a share (*dha shirk*), or those who have a share (*dhawi shirk*).

The interrogative in ﴿Do they associate what creates nothing?﴾ is for rebuke and reproach, meaning: how do they make for God a partner who creates nothing and is not able to bring benefit to them or repel harm from them?

His saying: ﴿while they themselves are created﴾ is conjoined to ﴿what creates nothing﴾, and the pronoun refers to the partners who create nothing. That is: these whom they made partners, from idols or devils, are themselves created. Their plural is the plural of rational beings because those who made them partners believed them to be such.

﴿And they cannot help them﴾, that is, those who made them partners, ﴿with victory﴾ if he seeks it from them, ﴿nor can they help themselves﴾ if something befalls them from others. Whoever is unable to help himself is all the more unable to help others.

Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Hamal ibn Abi Qays and Shamul ibn Zayd said to the Messenger of God ﷺ: Tell us when the Hour will be, if you are a prophet as you say, for we know what it is. So God revealed: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when is its settling? Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾ up to His saying: ﴿But most people do not know.﴾"

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، وابن جرير، عن قتادة: ﴿أيان مرساها﴾ أي متى قيامها؟ ﴿يسألونك عن الساعة أيان مرساها قل إنما علمها عند ربي لا يجليها لوقتها إلا هو﴾. قال: قالت قريش: يا محمد، أسرّ إلينا الساعة لما بيننا وبينك من القرابة؟ فقال: ﴿يسألونك كأنك حفي عنها قل إنما علمها عند الله﴾. وذُكر لنا أن نبي الله ﷺ كان يقول: «تهيج الساعة بالناس والرجل يسقي على ماشيته، والرجل يصلح حوضه، والرجل يخفض ميزانه ويرفعه، والرجل يقيم سلعته في السوق، قضاء الله لا تأتيكم إلا بغتة».

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿أيان مرساها﴾ قال: منتهاها.

وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة، وعبد بن حميد، وابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، عن مجاهد: ﴿لا يجليها لوقتها إلا هو﴾ يقول: لا يأتي بها إلا الله.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، عن قتادة، في الآية قال: هو يجليها لوقتها، لا يعلم ذلك إلا الله.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿ثقلت في السماوات والأرض﴾ قال: ليس شيء من الخلق إلا يصيبه من ضرر يوم القيامة.

وأخرج عبد الرزاق، وابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، عن قتادة، في قوله: ﴿ثقلت في السماوات والأرض﴾ قال: ثقل علمها على أهل السماوات والأرض، يقول: كبرت عليهم.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وأبو الشيخ، عن ابن جريج في قوله: ﴿ثقلت في السماوات والأرض﴾ (p-519) قال: إذا جاءت انشقت السماء، وانتثرت النجوم، وكوِّرت الشمس، وسُيِّرت الجبال، وما يصيب الأرض، وكان ما قال الله سبحانه، فذلك ثقلها فيهما.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، عن مجاهد في قوله: ﴿لا تأتيكم إلا بغتة﴾ قال: فجأة، وأنتم آمنون.

وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة، وعبد بن حميد، وابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، والبيهقي في البعث، عن مجاهد في قوله: ﴿كأنك حفي عنها﴾ قال: استحفيت عنها السؤال حتى علمتها.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿كأنك حفي عنها﴾ يقول: كأنك عالم بها، أي لست تعلمها.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، والبيهقي، عنه: ﴿كأنك حفي عنها﴾ قال: لطيف بها.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، وابن مردويه، والبيهقي، عنه أيضًا: ﴿كأنك حفي عنها﴾ يقول: كأن بينك وبينهم مودة، كأنك صديق لهم. قال: لما سأل الناس محمدًا ﷺ عن الساعة سألوه سؤال قوم كأنهم يُرَوْن أن محمدًا حفي بهم، فأوحى الله إليه ﴿إنما علمها عند الله﴾ استأثر بعلمها، فلم يُطلع ملكًا ولا رسولًا.

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، عن عمرو بن دينار قال: كان ابن عباس يقرأ: «كأنك حفي بها».

وأخرج ابن جرير، وأبو الشيخ، عن ابن جريج: ﴿قل لا أملك لنفسي نفعًا ولا ضرًا﴾ قال: الهدى والضلالة. ﴿ولو كنت أعلم الغيب﴾ متى أموت ﴿لاستكثرت من الخير﴾ قال: العمل الصالح.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿ولو كنت أعلم الغيب لاستكثرت من الخير﴾ قال: لعلمت إذا اشتريت شيئًا ما أربح فيه فلا أبيع شيئًا لا ربح فيه. ﴿وما مسني السوء﴾ قال: لاجتنبت ما يكون من الشر قبل أن يكون.

وأخرج أحمد، والترمذي، وحسّنه، وأبو يعلى، وابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، والرُّوياني، والطبراني، وأبو الشيخ، والحاكم وصححه، وابن مردويه، عن سمرة، عن النبي ﷺ قال: «لما ولدت حواء طاف بها إبليس، وكان لا يعيش لها ولد، فقال: سمّيه عبد الحارث فإنه يعيش، فسمّته عبد الحارث فعاش، فكان ذلك من وحي الشيطان وأمره».

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، وابن جرير، وابن مردويه، عن سمرة في قوله: ﴿فلما آتاهما صالحًا جعلا له شركاء﴾ قال: سمّياه عبد الحارث.

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، وأبو الشيخ، عن أُبيّ بن كعب نحو حديث سمرة المرفوع، موقوفًا عليه.

وأخرج سعيد بن منصور، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، عن ابن عباس، قال: حملت حواء فأتاها إبليس فقال: إني صاحبكما الذي أخرجتكما من الجنة، لتطيعنّني أو لأجعلنّ له قرني أيل، فيخرج من بطنك فيشقه، ولأفعلنّ ولأفعلنّ، يخوفهما. سمّياه عبد الحارث، فأبيا أن يطيعاه فخرج ميتًا، ثم حملت فأتاهما أيضًا فقال مثل ذلك، فأبيا أن يطيعاه فخرج ميتًا، ثم حملت فأتاهما فذكر لهما فأدركهما حب الولد فسمّياه عبد الحارث، فذلك قوله: ﴿جعلا له شركاء فيما آتاهما﴾.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وأبو الشيخ، عن الحسن في الآية قال: كان هذا في بعض أهل الملل، وليس بآدم.

وأخرج أبو الشيخ، وابن مردويه، عن سمرة في قوله: ﴿حملت حملًا خفيفًا﴾ لم يستبن ﴿فمرت به﴾ لما استبان حملها.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿فمرت به﴾ قال: فشكّت أحملت أم لا.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وأبو الشيخ، عن أيوب قال: سُئل الحسن عن قوله: ﴿فمرت به﴾ فقال: لو كنت عربيًا لعرفتها، إنما هي استمرت بالحمل.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، عن السدي، في قوله: ﴿حملت حملًا خفيفًا﴾ قال: هي النطفة. ﴿فمرت به﴾ يقول: استمرت به.

وأخرج سعيد بن منصور، وابن المنذر، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿فمرت به﴾ قال: فاستمرت به.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، عن ميمون بن مهران: ﴿فمرت به﴾ يقول: استخفّته.

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، وابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، عن أبي صالح في قوله: ﴿لئن آتيتنا صالحًا﴾ فقال: أشفقا أن يكون بهيمة، فقالا: لئن آتيتنا بشرًا سويًا.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، عن مجاهد نحوه.

وأخرج عبد الرزاق، وابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، عن الحسن في الآية قال: غلامًا سويًا.

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿جعلا له شركاء﴾ قال: كان شريكًا في الطاعة، ولم يكن شريكًا في العبادة.

وأخرج ابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، عنه قال: ما أشرك آدم، إن أولها شكر، وآخرها مثل ضربه لمن بعده.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، عن السدي، في قوله: ﴿فتعالى الله عما يشركون﴾ هذا فصل من آية آدم خاصة، في آلهة العرب.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، عن أبي مالك نحوه.

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، وأبو الشيخ، عن الحسن في الآية قال: هذا في الكفار يدعون الله، فإذا آتاهما صالحًا هوّدا أو نصّرا. ثم قال: ﴿أيشركون ما لا يخلق شيئًا وهم يُخلقون﴾ يقول: يطيعون ما لا يخلق شيئًا، وهي الشياطين، لا تخلق شيئًا وهي تُخلق. ﴿ولا يستطيعون لهم نصرًا﴾ يقول: لمن يدعوهم.

(p-517) His saying: ﴿They ask you about the Hour﴾. The askers were the Jews, and it was said they were the Quraysh. "The Hour" (al-sa'ah) is the Resurrection, and it is one of the names that became dominant for it. It is applied to the Resurrection either because it comes suddenly or because its reckoning is swift. "Ayyan" (when) is an adverb of time (zarf zaman) that is indeclinable (mabni) on the fatha. The reciter said:

*"When will my need be fulfilled? When? Do you not see that its ripeness is due?"*

Its meaning is the same as *mata* (when), and its derivation is from *ayy*. It was also said to be from *ayna* (where).

Al-Sulami read *"iyyan"* with a kasra on the hamza. It is then in the position of a predicate (khabar). ﴿Its settling﴾ (mursaha) is the subject (mubtada') according to Sibawayh. *Mursaha* with a damma on the *mim* means the time of its establishment, from *arsaha Allah*, meaning God fixed it. With a fatha on the *mim* it comes from *rasat*, meaning it became firm. From this is ﴿and cooking pots fixed firmly﴾ (Saba': 13), and from it is *rasa al-jabal*, meaning the mountain became fixed.

The meaning is: when will God settle it, that is, establish it and bring it about. The apparent sense of ﴿They ask you about the Hour﴾ is that the question concerns the Hour itself, and the apparent sense of ﴿When is its settling?﴾ is that the question concerns its time. From all of this it results that the question mentioned is about the Hour in terms of its occurrence at a specified time. Then God, glorified is He, commanded him to answer them with His saying: ﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾. That is, its knowledge, in terms of its occurrence, is with God alone, and no one else knows it or is guided to it. ﴿None will reveal it at its time except Him﴾. That is, none will make it manifest at its time or uncover it except God, glorified is He. *Tajliyah* means making a thing manifest. It is said: *jalla li fulan al-khabar*, meaning he made the news manifest and clear. In God's exclusive possession of the knowledge of the Hour there is great wisdom and profound design, like all the other things that God concealed and kept exclusively to His knowledge.

This sentence confirms the content of the one before it.

His saying: ﴿It has been heavy upon the heavens and the earth﴾. It was said that the meaning is: since its knowledge was hidden from the people of the heavens and the earth, it was heavy, because whatever knowledge is hidden is heavy on hearts. It was also said that the meaning is: the heavens and the earth cannot bear it because of its magnitude, since the sky will split, the stars will scatter, and the seas will dry up. It was also said: its description became great for them. It was also said: the question about it became heavy. This sentence also confirms the content of what precedes it. ﴿It will not come upon you except suddenly﴾, that is, except unexpectedly while you are heedless. *Al-baghtah* is a verbal noun in the position of a circumstantial clause (hal). This sentence is like the one before it in confirmation.

His saying: ﴿They ask you as though you were informed about it﴾. Ibn Faris said: *al-hafiy* is one who knows a thing, and *al-hafiy* is also one who presses in questioning. From this is the saying of al-A'sha:

*"If you ask about me, then how many a questioner, eager about al-A'sha, has asked where he ascended."*

It is said: *ahfa fi al-mas'alah* and *fi al-talab*, so he is *muhfin*. *Hafiy* is an intensive form like *mukhassib* and *khasib*.

The meaning is: they ask you about the Hour as though you knew it, or as though he were pressing in questioning about it and asking much about it. The simile clause is in a position of accusative (nasb) as a circumstantial clause, meaning they ask you while your state is made like the state of one who is informed about it. It was also said that the meaning is: they ask you about it as though you were eager for them, that is, eager for their goodness and pleased with their asking.

The first meaning is the meaning of the Qur'anic arrangement according to the requirement of the Arabic style.

His saying: ﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾. God, glorified is He, commanded him to repeat what he had already answered them, to establish and confirm the ruling. It was also said that it is not a repetition, but rather one of them means exclusive possession of its occurrence, and the other means exclusive possession of its very nature. ﴿But most people do not know﴾ this exclusive possession by God and the absence of knowledge of it among His creation. No near-angel and no sent prophet knows it.

His saying: ﴿Say: I possess for myself no benefit or harm except what God wills﴾. This sentence contains a confirmation of what preceded regarding his lack of knowledge of the Hour, when it will be and when it will occur. For if he does not have power to bring about benefit for himself or to repel harm from himself except what God, glorified is He, wills of benefit to him and repelling from him, then it is all the more so that he has no power to know what God has kept exclusively to His knowledge. In this there is a demonstration of servitude and an acknowledgment of inability regarding matters that are not the concern of servants, and an admission of weakness in claiming what is not his. In it is the greatest deterrent and the most eloquent admonition for whoever claims for himself what is not his concern and appropriates knowledge of the unseen through fortune-telling, sand divination, pebble casting, or augury. Then he confirmed and established this with His saying: ﴿And had I known the unseen, I would have acquired much good﴾. That is: if I knew the category of the unseen, I would have pursued what contains good and brought it to myself, and I would have guarded against what contains evil so that it would not touch me. But I am a servant who does not know what is with my Lord, nor what He has decreed for me and destined for me. So how could I know other than that and burden myself with knowing it? It was also said that the meaning is: had I known what God, mighty and majestic, wills of me before He informs me of it, I would have done it. It was also said: had I known when victory in war would be mine, I would have fought and not been defeated. It was also said: had I known the unseen, I would have answered every question asked of me. The better view is to take the verse in its generality, so these matters and others are included under it. It has also been said that ﴿and evil has not touched me﴾ is a new independent statement, meaning there is not in me what you claim of madness. The better view is that it is connected to what precedes it, and the meaning is: had I known the unseen, evil would not have touched me, and I would have guarded against it, as we have mentioned.

His saying: ﴿I am not but a warner and a bringer of good tidings to a people who believe﴾. That is: I am only a conveyor from God of His rulings, by which I warn one people and give good tidings to others, and I do not know the unseen of God, glorified is He. The lam in *li-qawmin* is connected to both attributes: a bringer of good tidings to a people, and a warner to a people. It was also said that it is connected to *bashir* (bringer of good tidings), and what is connected to *nadhir* (warner) is omitted, meaning: a warner to a people who disbelieve, and a bringer of good tidings to a people who believe.

His saying: ﴿He is the One who created you from one soul﴾. This is an independent statement containing a mention of God's blessings upon His servants and their failure to repay them with what is obligatory of gratitude and acknowledgment of servitude, and that He alone is singular in divinity.

The majority of exegetes said: by "one soul" is meant Adam. His saying ﴿and made from it its mate﴾ is conjoined to ﴿created you﴾, meaning: He is the One who created you from the soul of Adam and made from this soul its mate, who is Eve, whom He created from one of his ribs. It was also said that the meaning of ﴿made from it﴾ is from its kind, as in His saying: ﴿He made for you from yourselves mates﴾ (al-Nahl: 72). The first is better. ﴿So that he might find rest in her﴾ is the reason for the making: that is, He made her from him so that he would find rest and comfort in her and be at peace with her, for a kind is most at rest with its own kind and most at ease with it. This was in Paradise, as the reports have narrated. Then God, glorified is He, began with another state that existed between them in this world after their descent, and He said: ﴿So when he covered her﴾. *Al-taghashshi* is a metaphor for intercourse, that is, when he had intercourse with her. ﴿She carried a light burden﴾, meaning she conceived after intercourse. He described it as light because at the time of the drop of semen it is lighter than when it becomes a clot, and when it is a clot it is lighter than when it is a lump of flesh, and when it is a lump it is lighter than what comes after. It was also said that this pregnancy was light for her from its beginning to its end, and she did not find any heaviness in it as pregnant women do. This is because of His saying: ﴿and she continued with it﴾, that is, she went on with that pregnancy, standing, sitting, and going about her needs without finding heaviness in it. The first interpretation is better because of His saying: ﴿then when she became heavy﴾, for its meaning is: when she became one with heaviness due to the size of the child in her womb. It was read *famarrat bihi* with lightening, that is, she was disturbed by it. It was also read *famarat bihi* from *al-mawr*, which is coming and going. It was also said that the meaning is: she continued with it.

The reading with lightening has been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas and Yahya ibn Ya'mur. The reading *famarat* has been narrated from Abd Allah ibn Umar. It was also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he read *fastamarrat bihi* (she continued with it).

His saying: ﴿They both called upon God, their Lord﴾. This is the answer to *lamma* (when). That is: Adam and Eve called upon God, their Lord and the owner of their affairs: ﴿If You give us a righteous child﴾, that is, a righteous son. The lam is the answer to an omitted oath, and ﴿we will surely be among the grateful﴾ is the answer to the oath, serving in place of the answer to the condition, meaning: among those who are grateful to You for this blessing. In this supplication is evidence that they both knew that what had happened in Eve's womb from the effect of that intercourse was of their own kind, and they knew that offspring affected by that cause would be established.

﴿So when He gave them﴾ what they asked for, a righteous child, and answered their supplication, ﴿they made for Him partners in what He had given them﴾.

Many exegetes said: Iblis came to Eve and said to her: If you give birth to a child, name him after me. She said: And what is your name? He said: al-Harith. He would not have named himself to her, or she would have recognized him. So she named him Abd al-Harith. This was an act of associating in naming, not an association in worship. They only intended that al-Harith was the cause of the child's deliverance, just as a man names himself "servant of his guest," as Hatim al-Ta'i said:

*"I am indeed a servant of the guest as long as he stays, and there is nothing in me but that trait of the servant."*

Other exegetes said: the ones who make partners in what He gave them are the human race, as happened with the polytheists among them, and it was not from Adam and Eve. This is indicated by the plural pronoun in His saying: ﴿Exalted is God above what they associate﴾.

Some exegetes went to the view that the meaning of ﴿from one soul﴾ is from one form and one shape, ﴿and made from it its mate﴾ meaning of its kind, ﴿and when he covered her﴾ means the male kind covered the female kind. On this view, Adam and Eve are not mentioned in the verse, and the dual pronouns refer to the two kinds.

We have already pointed to something similar to this and mentioned that it is contrary to the better view for several reasons. Among them: ﴿and made from it its mate﴾ applies only to Eve. Among them: ﴿they called upon God, their Lord﴾, for every child born between the two kinds does not have this supplication from them at the approach of its delivery.

The people of Medina and Asim read *shirkan* (singular), and Abu 'Amr and the rest of the people of Kufa read it in the plural.

Al-Akhfash Sa'id denied the first reading. It has been answered that it is correct by omitting the genitive-modified noun: that is, they made for Him one who has a share (*dha shirk*), or those who have a share (*dhawi shirk*).

The interrogative in ﴿Do they associate what creates nothing?﴾ is for rebuke and reproach, meaning: how do they make for God a partner who creates nothing and is not able to bring benefit to them or repel harm from them?

His saying: ﴿while they themselves are created﴾ is conjoined to ﴿what creates nothing﴾, and the pronoun refers to the partners who create nothing. That is: these whom they made partners, from idols or devils, are themselves created. Their plural is the plural of rational beings because those who made them partners believed them to be such.

﴿And they cannot help them﴾, that is, those who made them partners, ﴿with victory﴾ if he seeks it from them, ﴿nor can they help themselves﴾ if something befalls them from others. Whoever is unable to help himself is all the more unable to help others.

Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Hamal ibn Abi Qays and Shamul ibn Zayd said to the Messenger of God ﷺ: Tell us when the Hour will be, if you are a prophet as you say, for we know what it is. So God revealed: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when is its settling? Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾ up to His saying: ﴿But most people do not know.﴾"

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، وابن جرير، عن قتادة: ﴿أيان مرساها﴾ أي متى قيامها؟ ﴿يسألونك عن الساعة أيان مرساها قل إنما علمها عند ربي لا يجليها لوقتها إلا هو﴾. قال: قالت قريش: يا محمد، أسرّ إلينا الساعة لما بيننا وبينك من القرابة؟ فقال: ﴿يسألونك كأنك حفي عنها قل إنما علمها عند الله﴾. وذُكر لنا أن نبي الله ﷺ كان يقول: «تهيج الساعة بالناس والرجل يسقي على ماشيته، والرجل يصلح حوضه، والرجل يخفض ميزانه ويرفعه، والرجل يقيم سلعته في السوق، قضاء الله لا تأتيكم إلا بغتة».

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿أيان مرساها﴾ قال: منتهاها.

وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة، وعبد بن حميد، وابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، عن مجاهد: ﴿لا يجليها لوقتها إلا هو﴾ يقول: لا يأتي بها إلا الله.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، عن قتادة، في الآية قال: هو يجليها لوقتها، لا يعلم ذلك إلا الله.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿ثقلت في السماوات والأرض﴾ قال: ليس شيء من الخلق إلا يصيبه من ضرر يوم القيامة.

وأخرج عبد الرزاق، وابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، عن قتادة، في قوله: ﴿ثقلت في السماوات والأرض﴾ قال: ثقل علمها على أهل السماوات والأرض، يقول: كبرت عليهم.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وأبو الشيخ، عن ابن جريج في قوله: ﴿ثقلت في السماوات والأرض﴾ (p-519) قال: إذا جاءت انشقت السماء، وانتثرت النجوم، وكوِّرت الشمس، وسُيِّرت الجبال، وما يصيب الأرض، وكان ما قال الله سبحانه، فذلك ثقلها فيهما.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، عن مجاهد في قوله: ﴿لا تأتيكم إلا بغتة﴾ قال: فجأة، وأنتم آمنون.

وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة، وعبد بن حميد، وابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، والبيهقي في البعث، عن مجاهد في قوله: ﴿كأنك حفي عنها﴾ قال: استحفيت عنها السؤال حتى علمتها.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿كأنك حفي عنها﴾ يقول: كأنك عالم بها، أي لست تعلمها.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، والبيهقي، عنه: ﴿كأنك حفي عنها﴾ قال: لطيف بها.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، وابن مردويه، والبيهقي، عنه أيضًا: ﴿كأنك حفي عنها﴾ يقول: كأن بينك وبينهم مودة، كأنك صديق لهم. قال: لما سأل الناس محمدًا ﷺ عن الساعة سألوه سؤال قوم كأنهم يُرَوْن أن محمدًا حفي بهم، فأوحى الله إليه ﴿إنما علمها عند الله﴾ استأثر بعلمها، فلم يُطلع ملكًا ولا رسولًا.

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، عن عمرو بن دينار قال: كان ابن عباس يقرأ: «كأنك حفي بها».

وأخرج ابن جرير، وأبو الشيخ، عن ابن جريج: ﴿قل لا أملك لنفسي نفعًا ولا ضرًا﴾ قال: الهدى والضلالة. ﴿ولو كنت أعلم الغيب﴾ متى أموت ﴿لاستكثرت من الخير﴾ قال: العمل الصالح.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿ولو كنت أعلم الغيب لاستكثرت من الخير﴾ قال: لعلمت إذا اشتريت شيئًا ما أربح فيه فلا أبيع شيئًا لا ربح فيه. ﴿وما مسني السوء﴾ قال: لاجتنبت ما يكون من الشر قبل أن يكون.

وأخرج أحمد، والترمذي، وحسّنه، وأبو يعلى، وابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، والرُّوياني، والطبراني، وأبو الشيخ، والحاكم وصححه، وابن مردويه، عن سمرة، عن النبي ﷺ قال: «لما ولدت حواء طاف بها إبليس، وكان لا يعيش لها ولد، فقال: سمّيه عبد الحارث فإنه يعيش، فسمّته عبد الحارث فعاش، فكان ذلك من وحي الشيطان وأمره».

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، وابن جرير، وابن مردويه، عن سمرة في قوله: ﴿فلما آتاهما صالحًا جعلا له شركاء﴾ قال: سمّياه عبد الحارث.

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، وأبو الشيخ، عن أُبيّ بن كعب نحو حديث سمرة المرفوع، موقوفًا عليه.

وأخرج سعيد بن منصور، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، عن ابن عباس، قال: حملت حواء فأتاها إبليس فقال: إني صاحبكما الذي أخرجتكما من الجنة، لتطيعنّني أو لأجعلنّ له قرني أيل، فيخرج من بطنك فيشقه، ولأفعلنّ ولأفعلنّ، يخوفهما. سمّياه عبد الحارث، فأبيا أن يطيعاه فخرج ميتًا، ثم حملت فأتاهما أيضًا فقال مثل ذلك، فأبيا أن يطيعاه فخرج ميتًا، ثم حملت فأتاهما فذكر لهما فأدركهما حب الولد فسمّياه عبد الحارث، فذلك قوله: ﴿جعلا له شركاء فيما آتاهما﴾.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وأبو الشيخ، عن الحسن في الآية قال: كان هذا في بعض أهل الملل، وليس بآدم.

وأخرج أبو الشيخ، وابن مردويه، عن سمرة في قوله: ﴿حملت حملًا خفيفًا﴾ لم يستبن ﴿فمرت به﴾ لما استبان حملها.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿فمرت به﴾ قال: فشكّت أحملت أم لا.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وأبو الشيخ، عن أيوب قال: سُئل الحسن عن قوله: ﴿فمرت به﴾ فقال: لو كنت عربيًا لعرفتها، إنما هي استمرت بالحمل.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، عن السدي، في قوله: ﴿حملت حملًا خفيفًا﴾ قال: هي النطفة. ﴿فمرت به﴾ يقول: استمرت به.

وأخرج سعيد بن منصور، وابن المنذر، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿فمرت به﴾ قال: فاستمرت به.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، عن ميمون بن مهران: ﴿فمرت به﴾ يقول: استخفّته.

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، وابن أبي حاتم، وأبو الشيخ، عن أبي صالح في قوله: ﴿لئن آتيتنا صالحًا﴾ فقال: أشفقا أن يكون بهيمة، فقالا: لئن آتيتنا بشرًا سويًا.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، عن مجاهد نحوه.

وأخرج عبد الرزاق، وابن جرير، وابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، عن الحسن في الآية قال: غلامًا سويًا.

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: ﴿جعلا له شركاء﴾ قال: كان شريكًا في الطاعة، ولم يكن شريكًا في العبادة.

وأخرج ابن المنذر، وابن أبي حاتم، عنه قال: ما أشرك آدم، إن أولها شكر، وآخرها مثل ضربه لمن بعده.

وأخرج ابن جرير، وابن أبي حاتم، عن السدي، في قوله: ﴿فتعالى الله عما يشركون﴾ هذا فصل من آية آدم خاصة، في آلهة العرب.

وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم، عن أبي مالك نحوه.

وأخرج عبد بن حميد، وأبو الشيخ، عن الحسن في الآية قال: هذا في الكفار يدعون الله، فإذا آتاهما صالحًا هوّدا أو نصّرا. ثم قال: ﴿أيشركون ما لا يخلق شيئًا وهم يُخلقون﴾ يقول: يطيعون ما لا يخلق شيئًا، وهي الشياطين، لا تخلق شيئًا وهي تُخلق. ﴿ولا يستطيعون لهم نصرًا﴾ يقول: لمن يدعوهم.

He said: ﴿And if you call them to guidance, they will not follow you.﴾ This is addressed to the polytheists. That is: if you call these associates to guidance and right direction, by asking them to guide and direct you, they will not follow you or answer you in that. This is less than what you ask of them, namely bringing benefit, averting harm, and granting victory over enemies.

Al-Akhfash said: its meaning is "And if you call them," that is, the idols, "to guidance, they will not follow you." It was also said that what is meant are those whom God knows in advance will not believe.

It is recited as "lā yattabiʿūkum" with the doubled and the single ʿayn, and both are dialectal variants (lughatān).

Some of the linguists said: ittabaʿahu, without doubling, means he went after him but did not catch up with him; ittabaʿahu, with doubling, means he went after him and caught up with him.

The clause ﴿It is all the same to you whether you call them or you remain silent.﴾ confirms the content of what precedes it. That is: your calling upon them in times of hardship and your not calling upon them are the same; there is no difference between the two, because they neither benefit nor harm, neither hear nor answer. He said ﴿or you remain silent﴾ (amun antum ṣāmitūn) instead of aṣamamtum because of the emphasis contained in the nominal sentence (jumlah ismiyyah, a sentence beginning with a noun).

Muhammad ibn Yahya said: he used the nominal sentence only because it is the end of a verse (raʾs āyah), meaning to match ﴿nor can they help themselves﴾ and what precedes it.

He said: ﴿Indeed, those you call upon besides God are servants like you.﴾ He, Glorified is He, informed them that these whom you have made gods are servants of God, just as you are servants of Him, and you are more perfect than they are, because you are living, you speak, walk, hear and see, whereas these idols are not like that. Yet they are like you in being owned by God and subjugated to His command. In this there is a severe rebuke and great reproach to them.

The clause ﴿So call upon them, and let them respond to you, if you are truthful.﴾ confirms the content of what precedes it, that if they call them to guidance, they will not follow them, and that they have no power over anything. That is: call upon these associates. If they are as you claim, ﴿let them respond to you, if you are truthful﴾ in what you assert for them of power to benefit and harm.

The interrogation in His words ﴿Do they have feet with which to walk?﴾ and what follows is for rebuke and reproach. That is: these whom you have made associates have none of the faculties that you possess, let alone being able to do what you ask of them. As you see, these idols you devote yourselves to worshipping have ﴿feet with which to walk﴾ for their own benefit, let alone walking for your benefit. They have no ﴿hands with which to grasp﴾ as other living beings grasp, no ﴿eyes with which to see﴾ as you see, and no ﴿ears with which to hear﴾ as you hear. So how can you call upon those who are in this state, deprived of the instruments and in this position of helplessness?

Am (amm) in these places is the disjunctive (munqaṭiʿah) particle meaning "rather"; the hamzah is as the grammarians (aʾimmat al-nahw) have mentioned.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr recited ﴿Indeed, those whom you call upon besides God are servants like you﴾ with the particle inna lightened and ʿibādan in the accusative. That is: "those whom you call upon besides God are not servants like you," with inna functioning as a negative in the manner of the Hijazi "mā" (ʿamal mā al-ḥijāziyyah, the usage of "mā" in the Hijazi dialect, where it governs the predicate in the accusative). This reading has been deemed weak, because it contradicts what Sibawayh and others preferred, namely the nominative for its predicate, and because al-Kisāʾī said that it hardly occurs in Arabic speech with the meaning of "mā" unless it is followed by an affirmative statement, as in His words ﴿The disbelievers are only in delusion﴾ (Surah al-Mulk 67:20).

Al-baṭsh is seizing with force.

Abu Jaʿfar recited yabṭushūn with a ḍammah on the ṭāʾ, and this is a dialect (lughah).

Then, when He had shown them the condition of these idols and covered all aspects of their deficiency and incapacity from every angle, God commanded him to say to them: call upon your associates whom you claim have power to benefit and harm. ﴿Then plot against me﴾, you and them all together, with whatever kinds of plotting you wish, ﴿and give me no respite﴾, that is, do not delay me, and do not postpone bringing harm upon me by their means. Kayd means scheming. After this challenge and this proof of their incapacity, there is nothing more to say about their idols.

Then he said to them: ﴿Indeed, my protector is God, who has sent down the Book.﴾ That is: how could I fear these idols, which have such attributes, when I have a protector to whom I take refuge and from whom I seek victory, namely God, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿who has sent down the Book.﴾ This clause gives the reason for not being concerned about them. The protector (waliyy) of a thing is the one who guards it, takes responsibility for supporting it, and prevents harm from reaching it. ﴿And He takes care of the righteous﴾, that is, He guards and supports them, and stands between them and their enemies.

Al-Akhfash said: it is also recited "inna waliyya Allāh alladhī nazzala al-kitāb," meaning Gabriel.

Al-Nahhas said: this is the reading of ʿĀṣim al-Jahdarī, but the first reading is clearer because of His words ﴿And He takes care of the righteous.﴾

His words: ﴿Those you call upon besides Him cannot help you, nor can they help themselves.﴾ Glorified is He repeated this for further emphasis and affirmation, and because repeating the rebuke and reproach carries humiliation of the polytheists and disparagement of them, and reveals the frivolity of their minds and the feebleness of their reasoning.

﴿And you see them looking at you﴾ is a new (mubtadaʾah) clause explaining their incapacity, or a circumstantial clause (ḥāliyyah), meaning: while you see them looking at you, they are in a state of not seeing. What is meant are the idols: they resemble those who look, yet they have no eyes with which to see. It was said: they used to make eyes for the idols from crafted jewels, so they were in the form of those who look while not seeing. It was also said that what is meant are the polytheists: God informed that they do not see when they did not benefit from their sight, even though they saw with it things other than what would benefit them.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 7, verses 200–206 (part 1 of 2):

His saying: ﴿Take what is easy﴾. When Allah had enumerated the states of the polytheists, their foolish opinions and the misguidance of their efforts, He commanded His Messenger ﷺ to take what is easy (al-'afw) from their dispositions. It is said: "I took my right al-'afwa," meaning easily: (p-٥٢١) without difficulty. This is a type of the facilitation which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command, as is established in the Sahih that he would say: "Make things easy and do not make them difficult; give good news and do not repel." The meaning of al-'afw here is the opposite of hardship. It is also said that the meaning is: take what is easy from their charities, and do not be harsh with them regarding them, nor take what is burdensome for them. This was before the obligation of zakat was revealed. ﴿And enjoin what is customary﴾, that is, what is good (bi-l-ma'ruf).

'Isa ibn 'Umar read "bi-l-'urufi" with two dammas, and both are dialectal variants. Al-'urf, al-ma'ruf and al-'arifah all mean every good quality which the intellects approve and to which the souls are at rest. From this is the saying of the poet:

Whoever does good will not lack its rewarder;
Good customs do not perish between Allah and the people.

﴿And turn away from the ignorant﴾, that is: if you have established the proof concerning their matter by what is customary and they do not act upon it, then turn away from them, do not dispute with them, and do not match their foolishness, in return for what proceeds from them of contention and foolishness. It has been said: this verse is among what was abrogated by the verse of the sword; this was stated by 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd and 'Ata'. It has also been said: it is muhkam (not abrogated); this was stated by Mujahid and Qatadah.

His saying: ﴿And if an incitement from Satan incites you﴾. Al-nazgh is whispering, and likewise al-naghz and al-nakhs (prodding).

Al-Zajjaj said: al-nazgh is the least movement, and "from Satan" is the least whispering. The root of al-nazgh is corruption; it is said: "nazgha baynana," meaning he sowed corruption between us. It is also said that al-nazgh is misguidance (al-igwa'), and the meanings are close. Allah, glorified is He, commanded His Prophet ﷺ that when he perceives anything of Satan's whispering, he should seek refuge in Allah. It is also said that when His saying ﴿Take what is easy﴾ was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ said: "How, O Lord, [will it be] with anger?" and then this was revealed. The clause ﴿Indeed He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾ is the reason for His command to seek refuge, that is: seek refuge in Him and take refuge with Him, for He hears that from you and knows it.

The clause ﴿Indeed, those who fear Allah, when an apparition from Satan touches them, remember﴾ confirms the content of what precedes it: that is, the affair and state of those who fear Allah is that they remember what Allah commanded of seeking refuge in Him and taking refuge with Him when an apparition from Satan touches them, even if it is slight.

The people of Basra read "tayf", and likewise the people of Makkah. The people of Madinah and Kufa read "ta'if". Sa'id ibn Jubayr read "tayyif" with shaddah.

Al-Nahhas said: the Arabic usage in such a case is "tayf" with a light pronunciation, as a verbal noun from "taafa yatifu". Al-Kisa'i said: it is a light form like mayyit and mayt. Al-Nahhas said: its meaning in the language is what is imagined in the heart or seen in sleep, and likewise the meaning of ta'if. Abu Hatim said: I asked al-Asma'i about "tayyif", and he said: there is no fay'il among verbal nouns. Al-Nahhas said: it is not a verbal noun, but it has the meaning of ta'if. It was also said: al-tayf and al-ta'if are two different meanings: the first is imagination, and the second is Satan himself. The first comes from "taafa al-khayal yatifu tayfan", and they did not say from this "ta'if". Al-Suhayli said: because it is an imagining with no reality, but as for His saying ﴿Then there came upon it a visitation from your Lord﴾ (al-Qalam: 19), it is not called tayf there, because it is truly an active participle. Al-Zajjaj said: "tuftu 'alayhim atufu," so "taafa al-khayal yatifu."

Hassan said:
So leave this, but who is the phantom (la-tayf)
That keeps me awake when the night prayer has passed?

The whispering was called tayf because it is a passing thought from Satan which resembles the passing of imagination. ﴿Then they are seeing﴾, by means of remembrance, that is: they are awake (muntabihun). It is said: [they are] upon insight (ala basirah).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr read "tadhdhakkaru" with shaddah on the dhal. Al-Nahhas said: there is no basis for it in Arabic.

His saying: ﴿And their brothers extend them in error﴾. It is said: the meaning is: and the brothers of the devils, who are the wicked among the misguided humans, with the pronoun in "their brothers" referring to Satan mentioned earlier, and what is meant by it is the category, so it is permissible to return the plural pronoun to it. ﴿They extend them in error﴾, that is: the devils extend them in error and become a support for them. The wicked among humans were called the brothers of the devils because they accept from them and follow them. It is also said that what is meant by "the brothers" are the devils, and by the pronoun the wicked among humans, so the predicate applies to the one it belongs to.

Al-Zajjaj said: there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the speech, and the meaning is: "And those you invoke besides Him cannot help you nor help themselves." ﴿And their brothers extend them in error﴾, because the disbelievers are the brothers of the devils. ﴿Then they do not refrain﴾. Al-iqsar is ceasing from a thing, that is: the devils do not fall short in extending the disbelievers in error. It is said: "fi l-ghayy" is connected to His saying ﴿they extend them﴾, and it is said: it is connected to "the brothers." Al-ghayy is ignorance.

Nafi' read "yumiddunahum" with a damma on the letter of present tense and a kasra on the mim. The rest read with a fatha on the letter of present tense and a damma on the mim. Both are dialects: it is said "madda" and "amadda". Makki said: madda is more common. Abu 'Ubayd and a group of the people of language said: it is said that when one thing increases another by itself, one says "madda-hu", and when it increases it by means of something else, one says "amadda-hu," as in ﴿Your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand of the angels﴾ (Al 'Imran: 125). It is also said: one says "madadtu" in evil and "amdadtu" in good.

'Asim al-Jahdari read "yumadunahum fi l-ghayy".

'Isa ibn 'Umar read "thumma la yaqsuruna" with a fatha on the ya, a damma on the sad and a light qaf.

His saying: ﴿And when you do not bring them a sign, they say: "Why have you not devised it?"﴾. Ijtaba al-shay' means he gathered it for himself, that is, he collected it. That is: why did you not gather it (ijtama'ta), i.e., fabricate it (iftitalan) from your own self? It is said: the meaning is: you invented it. It is said: "ijtabaytu al-kalam": I appropriated it, invented it, and originated it when you bring it from your own self. They used to say this statement to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when revelation was delayed. So Allah commanded him to answer them with His saying: ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me﴾, that is: I am not one of those who brings signs from himself, as you claim. ﴿Say: "I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord"﴾; so what He revealed to me and sent down upon me, I have conveyed to you. And ﴿insights﴾ is the plural of basirah, that is: this Qur'an sent down upon me is ﴿insights from your Lord﴾ by which whoever accepts it sees clearly. It is said: the insights are proofs and demonstrations.

Al-Zajjaj said: the insights are paths. ﴿And guidance and mercy for a people who believe﴾ is coordinated with "insights," that is: this Qur'an is insights and guidance by which the believers are guided, and mercy for them.

His saying: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent﴾. Allah, glorified is He, commanded them to listen to the Qur'an and be silent for it when it is recited, so that they may benefit from it and reflect upon what is in it of wisdoms and benefits. It is said: this command is specific to the time of prayer when the imam recites. You are not unaware that the wording is broader than this, and a general ruling is not restricted to its occasion; so listening and silence during the recitation of the Qur'an are in every state and in whatever manner that is obligatory for the listener. It is also said: this is specific to the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ recitation of the Qur'an without others, and there is no basis for that. ﴿That you may be shown mercy﴾, that is: you may attain mercy and succeed in it by complying with the command of Allah, glorified is He.

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded him to remember Him within himself, for concealment is more conducive to sincerity and more inviting to acceptance. It is said: what is meant by the remembrance here is what is more general than the Qur'an and other forms of remembrance by which Allah is mentioned.

Al-Nahhas said: there is no disagreement about the meaning of ﴿And remember your Lord within yourself﴾, that it is supplication. It is also said: it is specific to the Qur'an, that is: recite the Qur'an with reflection and contemplation. ﴿Humbly and in fear﴾ are accusative as states, that is: humbly and fearfully. Al-khifah is fear; its root is khawfah, the waw was changed to ya because of the kasra before it. Al-Farra' related that it is said in the plural of khifah: khiyaf. Al-Jawhari said: al-khifah is fear, its plural is khiyaf, and its root is waw, that is: khawf.

﴿And below the loud voice in speech﴾, that is: below the spoken aloud speech. It is coordinated with what precedes it, that is: humbly, fearfully, and speaking with a speech which is below loudness. ﴿In the mornings and the evenings﴾ is connected to "remember," that is: at the times of the mornings and the times of the evenings. Al-ghuduww is the plural of ghadwah, and al-aseel is the plural of aseel. Al-Zajjaj and al-Akhfash said: [the plural of aseel is] aasal, like yamin and ayman. It is said: al-aasal is the plural of usul, and usul is the plural of aseel, so on this view it is a plural of a plural; this was stated by al-Farra'.

Al-Jawhari said: al-aseel is the time from after 'asr until maghrib, and its plural is usul, aasal and asa'il, as if it were the plural of aseelah.

The poet said:
By my life, you are the house whose people are most noble,
And sitting in its courtyards in the evenings.

It is also pluralized as usalan, like ba'ir and bu'ran. Abu Mijlaz read "wa-l-iysal," which is a verbal noun.

He singled out these two times for their nobility, and what is meant is the continuity of remembrance of Allah. ﴿And do not be among the heedless﴾, that is: heedless of the remembrance of Allah.

﴿Indeed, those who are near your Lord do not disdain His worship﴾. What is meant by them are the angels. Al-Qurtubi said: by consensus.

Al-Zajjaj said: He said "near your Lord," while Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is in every place, because they are close to His mercy, and everyone close to the mercy of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is near Him. Others said: because they are in a place where nothing takes effect except the command of Allah. It is said: they are the messengers of Allah, as one says "near the caliph there is a large army." It is also said: this is by way of honoring and dignifying them. The meaning of ﴿they exalt Him﴾ is: they magnify Him and declare Him free of every defect. ﴿And to Him they prostrate﴾, that is: they specify Him with the worship of prostration, which is the most noble worship. It is also said: what is meant by prostration is humility and submission. In the mention of the exalted assembly there is an indirect address to the children of Adam.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Bukhari, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, al-Nahhas in his Nasikh, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il transmitted from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr regarding His saying ﴿Take what is easy﴾ to the end of the verse, that he said: "This verse was not revealed except concerning the differences among people," and in another wording: "Allah commanded His Prophet ﷺ to take what is easy from the dispositions of people."

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn 'Umar regarding His saying ﴿Take what is easy﴾ that he said: "Allah commanded His Prophet to take what is easy from the dispositions of people."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh transmitted from al-Sha'bi, who said: "When Allah sent down ﴿Take what is easy and enjoin what is customary and turn away from the ignorant﴾, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'I do not know until I ask the one who knows.' He went and then returned and said: 'Indeed Allah commands you to pardon the one who wronged you, to give to the one who withheld from you, and to join ties with the one who severed them.'"

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted something similar from Jabir.

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Qays ibn Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, he said: 'By Allah, I will mutilate seventy of them.' Then Jibril came to him with this verse."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from 'A'ishah regarding His saying ﴿Take what is easy﴾ that she said: "It is what is pardoned for you of noble characteristics."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying ﴿Take what is easy﴾ that he said: "Take what is pardoned of their wealth; whatever they bring you of something, take it. This was before Surat Bara'ah was revealed with the obligations of charity and their details."

Ibn Jarir and al-Nahhas in his Nasikh transmitted from al-Suddi regarding the verse, that he said: "The surplus of wealth was abrogated by zakat."

Ibn Jarir transmitted from Ibn Zayd, who said: "When ﴿Take what is easy﴾ to the end of the verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'How [will it be] with anger, O Lord?' Then ﴿And if an incitement from Satan incites you﴾ was revealed."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh transmitted from Mujahid regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, those who fear Allah﴾ that he said: "They are the believers."

Al-Shawkani's Fath al-Qadir, on surah 7, verses 200–206 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿When a whisper from Satan touches them﴾, that he said: "It is anger."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The ṭayf is anger."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿remember﴾, that he said: "When they slip, they repent."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, that he said: "The ṭā'if is the stirring (al-lammah) from Satan."

﴿Remember, and then they see clearly﴾: he says, "Then they are restrained from disobedience, adhering to the command of Allah and disobedient to Satan." ﴿And their brothers﴾: he said, "They are the brothers of the devils." ﴿Who draw them further into error, then they do not hold back﴾: he said, "Neither do mankind refrain from the evil deeds they commit, nor do the devils cease from them." And ﴿When you do not bring them a sign, they say: "Why did you not devise it?"﴾: he says, "Why did you not invent it? Why did you not receive it and bring it into being?"

Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him (Ibn Abbas) ﴿And their brothers draw them further into error﴾: he said, "They are the jinn who inspire their allies among mankind." ﴿Then they do not hold back﴾: he says, "They do not tire." ﴿When you do not bring them a sign, they say: "Why did you not devise it?"﴾: he says, "Why did you not fabricate it of your own accord?"

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated from Abu Hurayrah, regarding His words ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited﴾ (the verse), that he said: "It was revealed concerning raising the voices while behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in prayer."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, that he said: "It means in the obligatory prayer."

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from him, who said: "The Prophet ﷺ prayed, and some people behind him recited and mixed (their recitation), (p-523) so the verse ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited﴾ (the verse) was revealed." This is concerning the prescribed prayer.

He said: "Even if we do not listen to one who recites quietly rather than aloud."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi something similar.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Mujahid something similar.

Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal something similar.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Mas'ud something similar as well. Something like this has been related from a group of the early generations (al-salaf), and they stated explicitly that this verse was revealed concerning the recitation of the prayer by the imam.

Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated from al-Hasan regarding the verse, that he said: "At the obligatory prayer and at remembrance."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, that he said: "In the prayer and when the revelation descends."

al-Bayhaqi narrated from him regarding the verse that he said: "This is in the prayer."

Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And remember your Lord within yourself﴾ (the verse), that he said: "Allah commanded him to remember Him and forbade him from heedlessness. As for ﴿in the mornings﴾, it is the Subh prayer, and ﴿and the evenings﴾ is in the afternoon."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu Sakhr, who said: "The evenings (al-asal) are between Zuhr and Asr."

Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Zayd regarding the verse, that he said: "Do not speak aloud of it ﴿in the mornings and evenings﴾, in the early day and the late day."

Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid ﴿in the mornings﴾, that he said: "The end of dawn is the Subh prayer, and al-asal is the end of the afternoon, the Asr prayer."

The ahadith and reports from the Companions concerning prostration of recitation (sujud al-tilawah), the number of places where prostration is performed, the manner of prostration and what is said in it are comprehensively found in the books of hadith and fiqh, so we will not lengthen the discussion by citing them here.
