It is also said: this is specific to the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ recitation of the Qur'an without others, and there is no basis for that. ﴿That you may be shown mercy﴾, that is: you may attain mercy and succeed in it by complying with the command of Allah, glorified is He.

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded him to remember Him within himself, for concealment is more conducive to sincerity and more inviting to acceptance. It is said: what is meant by the remembrance here is what is more general than the Qur'an and other forms of remembrance by which Allah is mentioned.

Al-Nahhas said: there is no disagreement about the meaning of ﴿And remember your Lord within yourself﴾, that it is supplication. It is also said: it is specific to the Qur'an, that is: recite the Qur'an with reflection and contemplation. ﴿Humbly and in fear﴾ are accusative as states, that is: humbly and fearfully. Al-khifah is fear; its root is khawfah, the waw was changed to ya because of the kasra before it. Al-Farra' related that it is said in the plural of khifah: khiyaf. Al-Jawhari said: al-khifah is fear, its plural is khiyaf, and its root is waw, that is: khawf.

﴿And below the loud voice in speech﴾, that is: below the spoken aloud speech. It is coordinated with what precedes it, that is: humbly, fearfully, and speaking with a speech which is below loudness. ﴿In the mornings and the evenings﴾ is connected to "remember," that is: at the times of the mornings and the times of the evenings. Al-ghuduww is the plural of ghadwah, and al-aseel is the plural of aseel. Al-Zajjaj and al-Akhfash said: [the plural of aseel is] aasal, like yamin and ayman. It is said: al-aasal is the plural of usul, and usul is the plural of aseel, so on this view it is a plural of a plural; this was stated by al-Farra'.

Al-Jawhari said: al-aseel is the time from after 'asr until maghrib, and its plural is usul, aasal and asa'il, as if it were the plural of aseelah.

The poet said:
By my life, you are the house whose people are most noble,
And sitting in its courtyards in the evenings.

It is also pluralized as usalan, like ba'ir and bu'ran. Abu Mijlaz read "wa-l-iysal," which is a verbal noun.

He singled out these two times for their nobility, and what is meant is the continuity of remembrance of Allah. ﴿And do not be among the heedless﴾, that is: heedless of the remembrance of Allah.

﴿Indeed, those who are near your Lord do not disdain His worship﴾. What is meant by them are the angels. Al-Qurtubi said: by consensus.

Al-Zajjaj said: He said "near your Lord," while Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is in every place, because they are close to His mercy, and everyone close to the mercy of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is near Him. Others said: because they are in a place where nothing takes effect except the command of Allah. It is said: they are the messengers of Allah, as one says "near the caliph there is a large army." It is also said: this is by way of honoring and dignifying them. The meaning of ﴿they exalt Him﴾ is: they magnify Him and declare Him free of every defect. ﴿And to Him they prostrate﴾, that is: they specify Him with the worship of prostration, which is the most noble worship. It is also said: what is meant by prostration is humility and submission. In the mention of the exalted assembly there is an indirect address to the children of Adam.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Bukhari, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, al-Nahhas in his Nasikh, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il transmitted from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr regarding His saying ﴿Take what is easy﴾ to the end of the verse, that he said: "This verse was not revealed except concerning the differences among people," and in another wording: "Allah commanded His Prophet ﷺ to take what is easy from the dispositions of people."

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn 'Umar regarding His saying ﴿Take what is easy﴾ that he said: "Allah commanded His Prophet to take what is easy from the dispositions of people."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh transmitted from al-Sha'bi, who said: "When Allah sent down ﴿Take what is easy and enjoin what is customary and turn away from the ignorant﴾, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'I do not know until I ask the one who knows.' He went and then returned and said: 'Indeed Allah commands you to pardon the one who wronged you, to give to the one who withheld from you, and to join ties with the one who severed them.'"

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted something similar from Jabir.

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Qays ibn Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, he said: 'By Allah, I will mutilate seventy of them.' Then Jibril came to him with this verse."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from 'A'ishah regarding His saying ﴿Take what is easy﴾ that she said: "It is what is pardoned for you of noble characteristics."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying ﴿Take what is easy﴾ that he said: "Take what is pardoned of their wealth; whatever they bring you of something, take it. This was before Surat Bara'ah was revealed with the obligations of charity and their details."

Ibn Jarir and al-Nahhas in his Nasikh transmitted from al-Suddi regarding the verse, that he said: "The surplus of wealth was abrogated by zakat."

Ibn Jarir transmitted from Ibn Zayd, who said: "When ﴿Take what is easy﴾ to the end of the verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'How [will it be] with anger, O Lord?' Then ﴿And if an incitement from Satan incites you﴾ was revealed."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh transmitted from Mujahid regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, those who fear Allah﴾ that he said: "They are the believers."

Al-Shawkani's Fath al-Qadir, on surah 7, verses 200–206 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿When a whisper from Satan touches them﴾, that he said: "It is anger."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The ṭayf is anger."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿remember﴾, that he said: "When they slip, they repent."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, that he said: "The ṭā'if is the stirring (al-lammah) from Satan."

﴿Remember, and then they see clearly﴾: he says, "Then they are restrained from disobedience, adhering to the command of Allah and disobedient to Satan." ﴿And their brothers﴾: he said, "They are the brothers of the devils." ﴿Who draw them further into error, then they do not hold back﴾: he said, "Neither do mankind refrain from the evil deeds they commit, nor do the devils cease from them." And ﴿When you do not bring them a sign, they say: "Why did you not devise it?"﴾: he says, "Why did you not invent it? Why did you not receive it and bring it into being?"

Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him (Ibn Abbas) ﴿And their brothers draw them further into error﴾: he said, "They are the jinn who inspire their allies among mankind." ﴿Then they do not hold back﴾: he says, "They do not tire." ﴿When you do not bring them a sign, they say: "Why did you not devise it?"﴾: he says, "Why did you not fabricate it of your own accord?"

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated from Abu Hurayrah, regarding His words ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited﴾ (the verse), that he said: "It was revealed concerning raising the voices while behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in prayer."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, that he said: "It means in the obligatory prayer."

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from him, who said: "The Prophet ﷺ prayed, and some people behind him recited and mixed (their recitation), (p-523) so the verse ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited﴾ (the verse) was revealed." This is concerning the prescribed prayer.

He said: "Even if we do not listen to one who recites quietly rather than aloud."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi something similar.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Mujahid something similar.

Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal something similar.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Mas'ud something similar as well. Something like this has been related from a group of the early generations (al-salaf), and they stated explicitly that this verse was revealed concerning the recitation of the prayer by the imam.

Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated from al-Hasan regarding the verse, that he said: "At the obligatory prayer and at remembrance."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, that he said: "In the prayer and when the revelation descends."

al-Bayhaqi narrated from him regarding the verse that he said: "This is in the prayer."

Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And remember your Lord within yourself﴾ (the verse), that he said: "Allah commanded him to remember Him and forbade him from heedlessness. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu Sakhr, who said: "The evenings (al-asal) are between Zuhr and Asr."

Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Zayd regarding the verse, that he said: "Do not speak aloud of it ﴿in the mornings and evenings﴾, in the early day and the late day."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 7, verses 200–206 (part 1 of 2):

His saying: ﴿Take what is easy﴾. When Allah had enumerated the states of the polytheists, their foolish opinions and the misguidance of their efforts, He commanded His Messenger ﷺ to take what is easy (al-'afw) from their dispositions. It is said: "I took my right al-'afwa," meaning easily: (p-٥٢١) without difficulty. This is a type of the facilitation which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command, as is established in the Sahih that he would say: "Make things easy and do not make them difficult; give good news and do not repel." The meaning of al-'afw here is the opposite of hardship. It is also said that the meaning is: take what is easy from their charities, and do not be harsh with them regarding them, nor take what is burdensome for them. This was before the obligation of zakat was revealed. ﴿And enjoin what is customary﴾, that is, what is good (bi-l-ma'ruf).

'Isa ibn 'Umar read "bi-l-'urufi" with two dammas, and both are dialectal variants. Al-'urf, al-ma'ruf and al-'arifah all mean every good quality which the intellects approve and to which the souls are at rest. From this is the saying of the poet:

Whoever does good will not lack its rewarder;
Good customs do not perish between Allah and the people.

﴿And turn away from the ignorant﴾, that is: if you have established the proof concerning their matter by what is customary and they do not act upon it, then turn away from them, do not dispute with them, and do not match their foolishness, in return for what proceeds from them of contention and foolishness. It has been said: this verse is among what was abrogated by the verse of the sword; this was stated by 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd and 'Ata'. It has also been said: it is muhkam (not abrogated); this was stated by Mujahid and Qatadah.

His saying: ﴿And if an incitement from Satan incites you﴾. Al-nazgh is whispering, and likewise al-naghz and al-nakhs (prodding).

Al-Zajjaj said: al-nazgh is the least movement, and "from Satan" is the least whispering. The root of al-nazgh is corruption; it is said: "nazgha baynana," meaning he sowed corruption between us. It is also said that al-nazgh is misguidance (al-igwa'), and the meanings are close. Allah, glorified is He, commanded His Prophet ﷺ that when he perceives anything of Satan's whispering, he should seek refuge in Allah. It is also said that when His saying ﴿Take what is easy﴾ was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ said: "How, O Lord, [will it be] with anger?" and then this was revealed. The clause ﴿Indeed He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾ is the reason for His command to seek refuge, that is: seek refuge in Him and take refuge with Him, for He hears that from you and knows it.

The clause ﴿Indeed, those who fear Allah, when an apparition from Satan touches them, remember﴾ confirms the content of what precedes it: that is, the affair and state of those who fear Allah is that they remember what Allah commanded of seeking refuge in Him and taking refuge with Him when an apparition from Satan touches them, even if it is slight.

The people of Basra read "tayf", and likewise the people of Makkah. The people of Madinah and Kufa read "ta'if". Sa'id ibn Jubayr read "tayyif" with shaddah.

Al-Nahhas said: the Arabic usage in such a case is "tayf" with a light pronunciation, as a verbal noun from "taafa yatifu". Al-Kisa'i said: it is a light form like mayyit and mayt. Al-Nahhas said: its meaning in the language is what is imagined in the heart or seen in sleep, and likewise the meaning of ta'if. Abu Hatim said: I asked al-Asma'i about "tayyif", and he said: there is no fay'il among verbal nouns. Al-Nahhas said: it is not a verbal noun, but it has the meaning of ta'if. It was also said: al-tayf and al-ta'if are two different meanings: the first is imagination, and the second is Satan himself. The first comes from "taafa al-khayal yatifu tayfan", and they did not say from this "ta'if". Al-Suhayli said: because it is an imagining with no reality, but as for His saying ﴿Then there came upon it a visitation from your Lord﴾ (al-Qalam: 19), it is not called tayf there, because it is truly an active participle. Al-Zajjaj said: "tuftu 'alayhim atufu," so "taafa al-khayal yatifu."

Hassan said:
So leave this, but who is the phantom (la-tayf)
That keeps me awake when the night prayer has passed?

The whispering was called tayf because it is a passing thought from Satan which resembles the passing of imagination. ﴿Then they are seeing﴾, by means of remembrance, that is: they are awake (muntabihun). It is said: [they are] upon insight (ala basirah).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr read "tadhdhakkaru" with shaddah on the dhal. Al-Nahhas said: there is no basis for it in Arabic.

His saying: ﴿And their brothers extend them in error﴾. It is said: the meaning is: and the brothers of the devils, who are the wicked among the misguided humans, with the pronoun in "their brothers" referring to Satan mentioned earlier, and what is meant by it is the category, so it is permissible to return the plural pronoun to it. ﴿They extend them in error﴾, that is: the devils extend them in error and become a support for them. The wicked among humans were called the brothers of the devils because they accept from them and follow them. It is also said that what is meant by "the brothers" are the devils, and by the pronoun the wicked among humans, so the predicate applies to the one it belongs to.

Al-Zajjaj said: there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the speech, and the meaning is: "And those you invoke besides Him cannot help you nor help themselves." ﴿And their brothers extend them in error﴾, because the disbelievers are the brothers of the devils. ﴿Then they do not refrain﴾. Al-iqsar is ceasing from a thing, that is: the devils do not fall short in extending the disbelievers in error. It is said: "fi l-ghayy" is connected to His saying ﴿they extend them﴾, and it is said: it is connected to "the brothers." Al-ghayy is ignorance.

Nafi' read "yumiddunahum" with a damma on the letter of present tense and a kasra on the mim. The rest read with a fatha on the letter of present tense and a damma on the mim. Both are dialects: it is said "madda" and "amadda". Makki said: madda is more common. Abu 'Ubayd and a group of the people of language said: it is said that when one thing increases another by itself, one says "madda-hu", and when it increases it by means of something else, one says "amadda-hu," as in ﴿Your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand of the angels﴾ (Al 'Imran: 125). It is also said: one says "madadtu" in evil and "amdadtu" in good.

'Asim al-Jahdari read "yumadunahum fi l-ghayy".

'Isa ibn 'Umar read "thumma la yaqsuruna" with a fatha on the ya, a damma on the sad and a light qaf.

His saying: ﴿And when you do not bring them a sign, they say: "Why have you not devised it?"﴾. Ijtaba al-shay' means he gathered it for himself, that is, he collected it. That is: why did you not gather it (ijtama'ta), i.e., fabricate it (iftitalan) from your own self? It is said: the meaning is: you invented it. It is said: "ijtabaytu al-kalam": I appropriated it, invented it, and originated it when you bring it from your own self. They used to say this statement to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when revelation was delayed. So Allah commanded him to answer them with His saying: ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me﴾, that is: I am not one of those who brings signs from himself, as you claim. ﴿Say: "I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord"﴾; so what He revealed to me and sent down upon me, I have conveyed to you. And ﴿insights﴾ is the plural of basirah, that is: this Qur'an sent down upon me is ﴿insights from your Lord﴾ by which whoever accepts it sees clearly. It is said: the insights are proofs and demonstrations.

Al-Zajjaj said: the insights are paths. ﴿And guidance and mercy for a people who believe﴾ is coordinated with "insights," that is: this Qur'an is insights and guidance by which the believers are guided, and mercy for them.

His saying: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent﴾. Allah, glorified is He, commanded them to listen to the Qur'an and be silent for it when it is recited, so that they may benefit from it and reflect upon what is in it of wisdoms and benefits. Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him (Ibn Abbas) ﴿And their brothers draw them further into error﴾: he said, "They are the jinn who inspire their allies among mankind." ﴿Then they do not hold back﴾: he says, "They do not tire." ﴿When you do not bring them a sign, they say: "Why did you not devise it?"﴾: he says, "Why did you not fabricate it of your own accord?"

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated from Abu Hurayrah, regarding His words ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited﴾ (the verse), that he said: "It was revealed concerning raising the voices while behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in prayer."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, that he said: "It means in the obligatory prayer."

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from him, who said: "The Prophet ﷺ prayed, and some people behind him recited and mixed (their recitation), (p-523) so the verse ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited﴾ (the verse) was revealed." This is concerning the prescribed prayer.

He said: "Even if we do not listen to one who recites quietly rather than aloud."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi something similar.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Mujahid something similar.

Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal something similar.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Mas'ud something similar as well. Something like this has been related from a group of the early generations (al-salaf), and they stated explicitly that this verse was revealed concerning the recitation of the prayer by the imam.

Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated from al-Hasan regarding the verse, that he said: "At the obligatory prayer and at remembrance."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, that he said: "In the prayer and when the revelation descends."

al-Bayhaqi narrated from him regarding the verse that he said: "This is in the prayer."

As for ﴿in the mornings﴾, it is the Subh prayer, and ﴿and the evenings﴾ is in the afternoon."

Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Zayd regarding the verse, that he said: "Do not speak aloud of it ﴿in the mornings and evenings﴾, in the early day and the late day."

Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid ﴿in the mornings﴾, that he said: "The end of dawn is the Subh prayer, and al-asal is the end of the afternoon, the Asr prayer."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 7, verses 200–206 (part 1 of 2):

His saying: ﴿Take what is easy﴾. When Allah had enumerated the states of the polytheists, their foolish opinions and the misguidance of their efforts, He commanded His Messenger ﷺ to take what is easy (al-'afw) from their dispositions. It is said: "I took my right al-'afwa," meaning easily: (p-٥٢١) without difficulty. This is a type of the facilitation which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command, as is established in the Sahih that he would say: "Make things easy and do not make them difficult; give good news and do not repel." The meaning of al-'afw here is the opposite of hardship. It is also said that the meaning is: take what is easy from their charities, and do not be harsh with them regarding them, nor take what is burdensome for them. This was before the obligation of zakat was revealed. ﴿And enjoin what is customary﴾, that is, what is good (bi-l-ma'ruf).

'Isa ibn 'Umar read "bi-l-'urufi" with two dammas, and both are dialectal variants. Al-'urf, al-ma'ruf and al-'arifah all mean every good quality which the intellects approve and to which the souls are at rest. From this is the saying of the poet:

Whoever does good will not lack its rewarder;
Good customs do not perish between Allah and the people.

﴿And turn away from the ignorant﴾, that is: if you have established the proof concerning their matter by what is customary and they do not act upon it, then turn away from them, do not dispute with them, and do not match their foolishness, in return for what proceeds from them of contention and foolishness. It has been said: this verse is among what was abrogated by the verse of the sword; this was stated by 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd and 'Ata'. It has also been said: it is muhkam (not abrogated); this was stated by Mujahid and Qatadah.

His saying: ﴿And if an incitement from Satan incites you﴾. Al-nazgh is whispering, and likewise al-naghz and al-nakhs (prodding).

Al-Zajjaj said: al-nazgh is the least movement, and "from Satan" is the least whispering. The root of al-nazgh is corruption; it is said: "nazgha baynana," meaning he sowed corruption between us. It is also said that al-nazgh is misguidance (al-igwa'), and the meanings are close. Allah, glorified is He, commanded His Prophet ﷺ that when he perceives anything of Satan's whispering, he should seek refuge in Allah. It is also said that when His saying ﴿Take what is easy﴾ was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ said: "How, O Lord, [will it be] with anger?" and then this was revealed. The clause ﴿Indeed He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾ is the reason for His command to seek refuge, that is: seek refuge in Him and take refuge with Him, for He hears that from you and knows it.

The clause ﴿Indeed, those who fear Allah, when an apparition from Satan touches them, remember﴾ confirms the content of what precedes it: that is, the affair and state of those who fear Allah is that they remember what Allah commanded of seeking refuge in Him and taking refuge with Him when an apparition from Satan touches them, even if it is slight.

The people of Basra read "tayf", and likewise the people of Makkah. The people of Madinah and Kufa read "ta'if". Sa'id ibn Jubayr read "tayyif" with shaddah.

Al-Nahhas said: the Arabic usage in such a case is "tayf" with a light pronunciation, as a verbal noun from "taafa yatifu". Al-Kisa'i said: it is a light form like mayyit and mayt. Al-Nahhas said: its meaning in the language is what is imagined in the heart or seen in sleep, and likewise the meaning of ta'if. Abu Hatim said: I asked al-Asma'i about "tayyif", and he said: there is no fay'il among verbal nouns. Al-Nahhas said: it is not a verbal noun, but it has the meaning of ta'if. It was also said: al-tayf and al-ta'if are two different meanings: the first is imagination, and the second is Satan himself. The first comes from "taafa al-khayal yatifu tayfan", and they did not say from this "ta'if". Al-Suhayli said: because it is an imagining with no reality, but as for His saying ﴿Then there came upon it a visitation from your Lord﴾ (al-Qalam: 19), it is not called tayf there, because it is truly an active participle. Al-Zajjaj said: "tuftu 'alayhim atufu," so "taafa al-khayal yatifu."

Hassan said:
So leave this, but who is the phantom (la-tayf)
That keeps me awake when the night prayer has passed?

The whispering was called tayf because it is a passing thought from Satan which resembles the passing of imagination. ﴿Then they are seeing﴾, by means of remembrance, that is: they are awake (muntabihun). It is said: [they are] upon insight (ala basirah).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr read "tadhdhakkaru" with shaddah on the dhal. Al-Nahhas said: there is no basis for it in Arabic.

His saying: ﴿And their brothers extend them in error﴾. It is said: the meaning is: and the brothers of the devils, who are the wicked among the misguided humans, with the pronoun in "their brothers" referring to Satan mentioned earlier, and what is meant by it is the category, so it is permissible to return the plural pronoun to it. ﴿They extend them in error﴾, that is: the devils extend them in error and become a support for them. The wicked among humans were called the brothers of the devils because they accept from them and follow them. It is also said that what is meant by "the brothers" are the devils, and by the pronoun the wicked among humans, so the predicate applies to the one it belongs to.

Al-Zajjaj said: there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the speech, and the meaning is: "And those you invoke besides Him cannot help you nor help themselves." ﴿And their brothers extend them in error﴾, because the disbelievers are the brothers of the devils. ﴿Then they do not refrain﴾. Al-iqsar is ceasing from a thing, that is: the devils do not fall short in extending the disbelievers in error. It is said: "fi l-ghayy" is connected to His saying ﴿they extend them﴾, and it is said: it is connected to "the brothers." Al-ghayy is ignorance.

Nafi' read "yumiddunahum" with a damma on the letter of present tense and a kasra on the mim. The rest read with a fatha on the letter of present tense and a damma on the mim. Both are dialects: it is said "madda" and "amadda". Makki said: madda is more common. Abu 'Ubayd and a group of the people of language said: it is said that when one thing increases another by itself, one says "madda-hu", and when it increases it by means of something else, one says "amadda-hu," as in ﴿Your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand of the angels﴾ (Al 'Imran: 125). It is also said: one says "madadtu" in evil and "amdadtu" in good.

'Asim al-Jahdari read "yumadunahum fi l-ghayy".

'Isa ibn 'Umar read "thumma la yaqsuruna" with a fatha on the ya, a damma on the sad and a light qaf.

His saying: ﴿And when you do not bring them a sign, they say: "Why have you not devised it?"﴾. Ijtaba al-shay' means he gathered it for himself, that is, he collected it. That is: why did you not gather it (ijtama'ta), i.e., fabricate it (iftitalan) from your own self? It is said: the meaning is: you invented it. It is said: "ijtabaytu al-kalam": I appropriated it, invented it, and originated it when you bring it from your own self. They used to say this statement to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when revelation was delayed. So Allah commanded him to answer them with His saying: ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me﴾, that is: I am not one of those who brings signs from himself, as you claim. ﴿Say: "I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord"﴾; so what He revealed to me and sent down upon me, I have conveyed to you. And ﴿insights﴾ is the plural of basirah, that is: this Qur'an sent down upon me is ﴿insights from your Lord﴾ by which whoever accepts it sees clearly. It is said: the insights are proofs and demonstrations.

Al-Zajjaj said: the insights are paths. ﴿And guidance and mercy for a people who believe﴾ is coordinated with "insights," that is: this Qur'an is insights and guidance by which the believers are guided, and mercy for them.

His saying: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent﴾. Allah, glorified is He, commanded them to listen to the Qur'an and be silent for it when it is recited, so that they may benefit from it and reflect upon what is in it of wisdoms and benefits. It is said: this command is specific to the time of prayer when the imam recites. You are not unaware that the wording is broader than this, and a general ruling is not restricted to its occasion; so listening and silence during the recitation of the Qur'an are in every state and in whatever manner that is obligatory for the listener. It is also said: this is specific to the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ recitation of the Qur'an without others, and there is no basis for that. ﴿That you may be shown mercy﴾, that is: you may attain mercy and succeed in it by complying with the command of Allah, glorified is He.

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded him to remember Him within himself, for concealment is more conducive to sincerity and more inviting to acceptance. It is said: what is meant by the remembrance here is what is more general than the Qur'an and other forms of remembrance by which Allah is mentioned.

Al-Nahhas said: there is no disagreement about the meaning of ﴿And remember your Lord within yourself﴾, that it is supplication. It is also said: it is specific to the Qur'an, that is: recite the Qur'an with reflection and contemplation. ﴿Humbly and in fear﴾ are accusative as states, that is: humbly and fearfully. Al-khifah is fear; its root is khawfah, the waw was changed to ya because of the kasra before it. Al-Farra' related that it is said in the plural of khifah: khiyaf. Al-Jawhari said: al-khifah is fear, its plural is khiyaf, and its root is waw, that is: khawf.

﴿And below the loud voice in speech﴾, that is: below the spoken aloud speech. It is coordinated with what precedes it, that is: humbly, fearfully, and speaking with a speech which is below loudness. ﴿In the mornings and the evenings﴾ is connected to "remember," that is: at the times of the mornings and the times of the evenings. Al-ghuduww is the plural of ghadwah, and al-aseel is the plural of aseel. Al-Zajjaj and al-Akhfash said: [the plural of aseel is] aasal, like yamin and ayman. It is said: al-aasal is the plural of usul, and usul is the plural of aseel, so on this view it is a plural of a plural; this was stated by al-Farra'.

Al-Jawhari said: al-aseel is the time from after 'asr until maghrib, and its plural is usul, aasal and asa'il, as if it were the plural of aseelah.

The poet said:
By my life, you are the house whose people are most noble,
And sitting in its courtyards in the evenings.

It is also pluralized as usalan, like ba'ir and bu'ran. Abu Mijlaz read "wa-l-iysal," which is a verbal noun.

He singled out these two times for their nobility, and what is meant is the continuity of remembrance of Allah. ﴿And do not be among the heedless﴾, that is: heedless of the remembrance of Allah.

﴿Indeed, those who are near your Lord do not disdain His worship﴾. What is meant by them are the angels. Al-Qurtubi said: by consensus.

Al-Zajjaj said: He said "near your Lord," while Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is in every place, because they are close to His mercy, and everyone close to the mercy of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is near Him. Others said: because they are in a place where nothing takes effect except the command of Allah. It is said: they are the messengers of Allah, as one says "near the caliph there is a large army." It is also said: this is by way of honoring and dignifying them. The meaning of ﴿they exalt Him﴾ is: they magnify Him and declare Him free of every defect. ﴿And to Him they prostrate﴾, that is: they specify Him with the worship of prostration, which is the most noble worship. It is also said: what is meant by prostration is humility and submission. In the mention of the exalted assembly there is an indirect address to the children of Adam.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Bukhari, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, al-Nahhas in his Nasikh, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il transmitted from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr regarding His saying ﴿Take what is easy﴾ to the end of the verse, that he said: "This verse was not revealed except concerning the differences among people," and in another wording: "Allah commanded His Prophet ﷺ to take what is easy from the dispositions of people."

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn 'Umar regarding His saying ﴿Take what is easy﴾ that he said: "Allah commanded His Prophet to take what is easy from the dispositions of people."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh transmitted from al-Sha'bi, who said: "When Allah sent down ﴿Take what is easy and enjoin what is customary and turn away from the ignorant﴾, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'I do not know until I ask the one who knows.' He went and then returned and said: 'Indeed Allah commands you to pardon the one who wronged you, to give to the one who withheld from you, and to join ties with the one who severed them.'"

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted something similar from Jabir.

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Qays ibn Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, he said: 'By Allah, I will mutilate seventy of them.' Then Jibril came to him with this verse."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from 'A'ishah regarding His saying ﴿Take what is easy﴾ that she said: "It is what is pardoned for you of noble characteristics."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying ﴿Take what is easy﴾ that he said: "Take what is pardoned of their wealth; whatever they bring you of something, take it. This was before Surat Bara'ah was revealed with the obligations of charity and their details."

Ibn Jarir and al-Nahhas in his Nasikh transmitted from al-Suddi regarding the verse, that he said: "The surplus of wealth was abrogated by zakat."

Ibn Jarir transmitted from Ibn Zayd, who said: "When ﴿Take what is easy﴾ to the end of the verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'How [will it be] with anger, O Lord?' Then ﴿And if an incitement from Satan incites you﴾ was revealed."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh transmitted from Mujahid regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, those who fear Allah﴾ that he said: "They are the believers."

Al-Zajjaj said: "tuftu 'alayhim atufu," so "taafa al-khayal yatifu."

Hassan said:
So leave this, but who is the phantom (la-tayf)
That keeps me awake when the night prayer has passed?

The whispering was called tayf because it is a passing thought from Satan which resembles the passing of imagination. ﴿Then they are seeing﴾, by means of remembrance, that is: they are awake (muntabihun). It is said: [they are] upon insight (ala basirah).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr read "tadhdhakkaru" with shaddah on the dhal. Al-Nahhas said: there is no basis for it in Arabic.

His saying: ﴿And their brothers extend them in error﴾. It is said: the meaning is: and the brothers of the devils, who are the wicked among the misguided humans, with the pronoun in "their brothers" referring to Satan mentioned earlier, and what is meant by it is the category, so it is permissible to return the plural pronoun to it. ﴿They extend them in error﴾, that is: the devils extend them in error and become a support for them. The wicked among humans were called the brothers of the devils because they accept from them and follow them. It is also said that what is meant by "the brothers" are the devils, and by the pronoun the wicked among humans, so the predicate applies to the one it belongs to.

Al-Zajjaj said: there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the speech, and the meaning is: "And those you invoke besides Him cannot help you nor help themselves." ﴿And their brothers extend them in error﴾, because the disbelievers are the brothers of the devils. ﴿Then they do not refrain﴾. Al-iqsar is ceasing from a thing, that is: the devils do not fall short in extending the disbelievers in error. It is said: "fi l-ghayy" is connected to His saying ﴿they extend them﴾, and it is said: it is connected to "the brothers." Al-ghayy is ignorance.

Nafi' read "yumiddunahum" with a damma on the letter of present tense and a kasra on the mim. The rest read with a fatha on the letter of present tense and a damma on the mim. Both are dialects: it is said "madda" and "amadda". Makki said: madda is more common. Abu 'Ubayd and a group of the people of language said: it is said that when one thing increases another by itself, one says "madda-hu", and when it increases it by means of something else, one says "amadda-hu," as in ﴿Your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand of the angels﴾ (Al 'Imran: 125). It is also said: one says "madadtu" in evil and "amdadtu" in good.

'Asim al-Jahdari read "yumadunahum fi l-ghayy".

'Isa ibn 'Umar read "thumma la yaqsuruna" with a fatha on the ya, a damma on the sad and a light qaf.

His saying: ﴿And when you do not bring them a sign, they say: "Why have you not devised it?"﴾. Ijtaba al-shay' means he gathered it for himself, that is, he collected it. That is: why did you not gather it (ijtama'ta), i.e., fabricate it (iftitalan) from your own self? It is said: the meaning is: you invented it. It is said: "ijtabaytu al-kalam": I appropriated it, invented it, and originated it when you bring it from your own self. They used to say this statement to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when revelation was delayed. So Allah commanded him to answer them with His saying: ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me﴾, that is: I am not one of those who brings signs from himself, as you claim. ﴿Say: "I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord"﴾; so what He revealed to me and sent down upon me, I have conveyed to you. And ﴿insights﴾ is the plural of basirah, that is: this Qur'an sent down upon me is ﴿insights from your Lord﴾ by which whoever accepts it sees clearly. It is said: the insights are proofs and demonstrations.

Al-Zajjaj said: the insights are paths. ﴿And guidance and mercy for a people who believe﴾ is coordinated with "insights," that is: this Qur'an is insights and guidance by which the believers are guided, and mercy for them.

His saying: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent﴾. Allah, glorified is He, commanded them to listen to the Qur'an and be silent for it when it is recited, so that they may benefit from it and reflect upon what is in it of wisdoms and benefits. It is said: this command is specific to the time of prayer when the imam recites. You are not unaware that the wording is broader than this, and a general ruling is not restricted to its occasion; so listening and silence during the recitation of the Qur'an are in every state and in whatever manner that is obligatory for the listener. It is also said: this is specific to the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ recitation of the Qur'an without others, and there is no basis for that. ﴿That you may be shown mercy﴾, that is: you may attain mercy and succeed in it by complying with the command of Allah, glorified is He.

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded him to remember Him within himself, for concealment is more conducive to sincerity and more inviting to acceptance. It is said: what is meant by the remembrance here is what is more general than the Qur'an and other forms of remembrance by which Allah is mentioned.

Al-Nahhas said: there is no disagreement about the meaning of ﴿And remember your Lord within yourself﴾, that it is supplication. It is also said: it is specific to the Qur'an, that is: recite the Qur'an with reflection and contemplation. ﴿Humbly and in fear﴾ are accusative as states, that is: humbly and fearfully. Al-khifah is fear; its root is khawfah, the waw was changed to ya because of the kasra before it. Al-Farra' related that it is said in the plural of khifah: khiyaf. Al-Jawhari said: al-khifah is fear, its plural is khiyaf, and its root is waw, that is: khawf.

﴿And below the loud voice in speech﴾, that is: below the spoken aloud speech. It is coordinated with what precedes it, that is: humbly, fearfully, and speaking with a speech which is below loudness. ﴿In the mornings and the evenings﴾ is connected to "remember," that is: at the times of the mornings and the times of the evenings. It is said: al-aasal is the plural of usul, and usul is the plural of aseel, so on this view it is a plural of a plural; this was stated by al-Farra'.

Al-Jawhari said: al-aseel is the time from after 'asr until maghrib, and its plural is usul, aasal and asa'il, as if it were the plural of aseelah.

By my life, you are the house whose people are most noble,
And sitting in its courtyards in the evenings.

He singled out these two times for their nobility, and what is meant is the continuity of remembrance of Allah. ﴿And do not be among the heedless﴾, that is: heedless of the remembrance of Allah.

It is also said: this is by way of honoring and dignifying them. The meaning of ﴿they exalt Him﴾ is: they magnify Him and declare Him free of every defect. ﴿And to Him they prostrate﴾, that is: they specify Him with the worship of prostration, which is the most noble worship. It is also said: what is meant by prostration is humility and submission. In the mention of the exalted assembly there is an indirect address to the children of Adam.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Bukhari, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, al-Nahhas in his Nasikh, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il transmitted from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr regarding His saying ﴿Take what is easy﴾ to the end of the verse, that he said: "This verse was not revealed except concerning the differences among people," and in another wording: "Allah commanded His Prophet ﷺ to take what is easy from the dispositions of people."

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn 'Umar regarding His saying ﴿Take what is easy﴾ that he said: "Allah commanded His Prophet to take what is easy from the dispositions of people."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh transmitted from al-Sha'bi, who said: "When Allah sent down ﴿Take what is easy and enjoin what is customary and turn away from the ignorant﴾, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'I do not know until I ask the one who knows.' He went and then returned and said: 'Indeed Allah commands you to pardon the one who wronged you, to give to the one who withheld from you, and to join ties with the one who severed them.'"

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted something similar from Jabir.

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Qays ibn Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, he said: 'By Allah, I will mutilate seventy of them.' Then Jibril came to him with this verse."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from 'A'ishah regarding His saying ﴿Take what is easy﴾ that she said: "It is what is pardoned for you of noble characteristics."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying ﴿Take what is easy﴾ that he said: "Take what is pardoned of their wealth; whatever they bring you of something, take it. This was before Surat Bara'ah was revealed with the obligations of charity and their details."

Ibn Jarir and al-Nahhas in his Nasikh transmitted from al-Suddi regarding the verse, that he said: "The surplus of wealth was abrogated by zakat."

Ibn Jarir transmitted from Ibn Zayd, who said: "When ﴿Take what is easy﴾ to the end of the verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'How [will it be] with anger, O Lord?' Then ﴿And if an incitement from Satan incites you﴾ was revealed."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh transmitted from Mujahid regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, those who fear Allah﴾ that he said: "They are the believers."

Al-Shawkani's Fath al-Qadir, on surah 7, verses 200–206 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿When a whisper from Satan touches them﴾, that he said: "It is anger."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The ṭayf is anger."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿remember﴾, that he said: "When they slip, they repent."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, that he said: "The ṭā'if is the stirring (al-lammah) from Satan."

﴿Remember, and then they see clearly﴾: he says, "Then they are restrained from disobedience, adhering to the command of Allah and disobedient to Satan." ﴿And their brothers﴾: he said, "They are the brothers of the devils." ﴿Who draw them further into error, then they do not hold back﴾: he said, "Neither do mankind refrain from the evil deeds they commit, nor do the devils cease from them." And ﴿When you do not bring them a sign, they say: "Why did you not devise it?"﴾: he says, "Why did you not invent it? Why did you not receive it and bring it into being?"

Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him (Ibn Abbas) ﴿And their brothers draw them further into error﴾: he said, "They are the jinn who inspire their allies among mankind." ﴿Then they do not hold back﴾: he says, "They do not tire." ﴿When you do not bring them a sign, they say: "Why did you not devise it?"﴾: he says, "Why did you not fabricate it of your own accord?"

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated from Abu Hurayrah, regarding His words ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited﴾ (the verse), that he said: "It was revealed concerning raising the voices while behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in prayer."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, that he said: "It means in the obligatory prayer."

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from him, who said: "The Prophet ﷺ prayed, and some people behind him recited and mixed (their recitation), (p-523) so the verse ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited﴾ (the verse) was revealed." This is concerning the prescribed prayer.

He said: "Even if we do not listen to one who recites quietly rather than aloud."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi something similar.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Mujahid something similar.

Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal something similar.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Mas'ud something similar as well. Something like this has been related from a group of the early generations (al-salaf), and they stated explicitly that this verse was revealed concerning the recitation of the prayer by the imam.

Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated from al-Hasan regarding the verse, that he said: "At the obligatory prayer and at remembrance."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, that he said: "In the prayer and when the revelation descends."

al-Bayhaqi narrated from him regarding the verse that he said: "This is in the prayer."

Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And remember your Lord within yourself﴾ (the verse), that he said: "Allah commanded him to remember Him and forbade him from heedlessness. As for ﴿in the mornings﴾, it is the Subh prayer, and ﴿and the evenings﴾ is in the afternoon."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu Sakhr, who said: "The evenings (al-asal) are between Zuhr and Asr."

Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Zayd regarding the verse, that he said: "Do not speak aloud of it ﴿in the mornings and evenings﴾, in the early day and the late day."

Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid ﴿in the mornings﴾, that he said: "The end of dawn is the Subh prayer, and al-asal is the end of the afternoon, the Asr prayer."

The ahadith and reports from the Companions concerning prostration of recitation (sujud al-tilawah), the number of places where prostration is performed, the manner of prostration and what is said in it are comprehensively found in the books of hadith and fiqh, so we will not lengthen the discussion by citing them here.

It is said: "I took my right al-'afwa," meaning easily: (p-٥٢١) without difficulty. This is a type of the facilitation which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command, as is established in the Sahih that he would say: "Make things easy and do not make them difficult; give good news and do not repel." The meaning of al-'afw here is the opposite of hardship. It is also said that the meaning is: take what is easy from their charities, and do not be harsh with them regarding them, nor take what is burdensome for them. 'Isa ibn 'Umar read "bi-l-'urufi" with two dammas, and both are dialectal variants. Al-'urf, al-ma'ruf and al-'arifah all mean every good quality which the intellects approve and to which the souls are at rest. From this is the saying of the poet:

Whoever does good will not lack its rewarder;
Good customs do not perish between Allah and the people.

﴿And turn away from the ignorant﴾, that is: if you have established the proof concerning their matter by what is customary and they do not act upon it, then turn away from them, do not dispute with them, and do not match their foolishness, in return for what proceeds from them of contention and foolishness. It has been said: this verse is among what was abrogated by the verse of the sword; this was stated by 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd and 'Ata'. It has also been said: it is muhkam (not abrogated); this was stated by Mujahid and Qatadah.

The meaning of ﴿they exalt Him﴾ is: they magnify Him and declare Him free of every defect. ﴿And to Him they prostrate﴾, that is: they specify Him with the worship of prostration, which is the most noble worship. It is also said: what is meant by prostration is humility and submission. In the mention of the exalted assembly there is an indirect address to the children of Adam.

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn 'Umar regarding His saying ﴿Take what is easy﴾ that he said: "Allah commanded His Prophet to take what is easy from the dispositions of people."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh transmitted from al-Sha'bi, who said: "When Allah sent down ﴿Take what is easy and enjoin what is customary and turn away from the ignorant﴾, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'I do not know until I ask the one who knows.' He went and then returned and said: 'Indeed Allah commands you to pardon the one who wronged you, to give to the one who withheld from you, and to join ties with the one who severed them.'"

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted something similar from Jabir.

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Qays ibn Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, he said: 'By Allah, I will mutilate seventy of them.' Then Jibril came to him with this verse."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying ﴿Take what is easy﴾ that he said: "Take what is pardoned of their wealth; whatever they bring you of something, take it. This was before Surat Bara'ah was revealed with the obligations of charity and their details."

Ibn Jarir and al-Nahhas in his Nasikh transmitted from al-Suddi regarding the verse, that he said: "The surplus of wealth was abrogated by zakat."

Ibn Jarir transmitted from Ibn Zayd, who said: "When ﴿Take what is easy﴾ to the end of the verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'How [will it be] with anger, O Lord?' Then ﴿And if an incitement from Satan incites you﴾ was revealed."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh transmitted from Mujahid regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, those who fear Allah﴾ that he said: "They are the believers."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿When a whisper from Satan touches them﴾, that he said: "It is anger."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The ṭayf is anger."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿remember﴾, that he said: "When they slip, they repent."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, that he said: "The ṭā'if is the stirring (al-lammah) from Satan."

﴿Remember, and then they see clearly﴾: he says, "Then they are restrained from disobedience, adhering to the command of Allah and disobedient to Satan." ﴿And their brothers﴾: he said, "They are the brothers of the devils." ﴿Who draw them further into error, then they do not hold back﴾: he said, "Neither do mankind refrain from the evil deeds they commit, nor do the devils cease from them." And ﴿When you do not bring them a sign, they say: "Why did you not devise it?"﴾: he says, "Why did you not invent it? Why did you not receive it and bring it into being?"

Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him (Ibn Abbas) ﴿And their brothers draw them further into error﴾: he said, "They are the jinn who inspire their allies among mankind." ﴿Then they do not hold back﴾: he says, "They do not tire." ﴿When you do not bring them a sign, they say: "Why did you not devise it?"﴾: he says, "Why did you not fabricate it of your own accord?"

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 7, verses 200–206 (part 1 of 2):

His saying: ﴿Take what is easy﴾. When Allah had enumerated the states of the polytheists, their foolish opinions and the misguidance of their efforts, He commanded His Messenger ﷺ to take what is easy (al-'afw) from their dispositions. It is said: "I took my right al-'afwa," meaning easily: (p-٥٢١) without difficulty. This is a type of the facilitation which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command, as is established in the Sahih that he would say: "Make things easy and do not make them difficult; give good news and do not repel." The meaning of al-'afw here is the opposite of hardship. It is also said that the meaning is: take what is easy from their charities, and do not be harsh with them regarding them, nor take what is burdensome for them. This was before the obligation of zakat was revealed. ﴿And enjoin what is customary﴾, that is, what is good (bi-l-ma'ruf).

'Isa ibn 'Umar read "bi-l-'urufi" with two dammas, and both are dialectal variants. Al-'urf, al-ma'ruf and al-'arifah all mean every good quality which the intellects approve and to which the souls are at rest. From this is the saying of the poet:

Whoever does good will not lack its rewarder;
Good customs do not perish between Allah and the people.

﴿And turn away from the ignorant﴾, that is: if you have established the proof concerning their matter by what is customary and they do not act upon it, then turn away from them, do not dispute with them, and do not match their foolishness, in return for what proceeds from them of contention and foolishness. It has been said: this verse is among what was abrogated by the verse of the sword; this was stated by 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd and 'Ata'. It has also been said: it is muhkam (not abrogated); this was stated by Mujahid and Qatadah.

His saying: ﴿And if an incitement from Satan incites you﴾. Al-nazgh is whispering, and likewise al-naghz and al-nakhs (prodding).

Al-Zajjaj said: al-nazgh is the least movement, and "from Satan" is the least whispering. The root of al-nazgh is corruption; it is said: "nazgha baynana," meaning he sowed corruption between us. It is also said that al-nazgh is misguidance (al-igwa'), and the meanings are close. Allah, glorified is He, commanded His Prophet ﷺ that when he perceives anything of Satan's whispering, he should seek refuge in Allah. It is also said that when His saying ﴿Take what is easy﴾ was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ said: "How, O Lord, [will it be] with anger?" and then this was revealed. The clause ﴿Indeed He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾ is the reason for His command to seek refuge, that is: seek refuge in Him and take refuge with Him, for He hears that from you and knows it.

The clause ﴿Indeed, those who fear Allah, when an apparition from Satan touches them, remember﴾ confirms the content of what precedes it: that is, the affair and state of those who fear Allah is that they remember what Allah commanded of seeking refuge in Him and taking refuge with Him when an apparition from Satan touches them, even if it is slight.

The people of Basra read "tayf", and likewise the people of Makkah. The people of Madinah and Kufa read "ta'if". Sa'id ibn Jubayr read "tayyif" with shaddah.

Al-Nahhas said: the Arabic usage in such a case is "tayf" with a light pronunciation, as a verbal noun from "taafa yatifu". Al-Kisa'i said: it is a light form like mayyit and mayt. Al-Nahhas said: its meaning in the language is what is imagined in the heart or seen in sleep, and likewise the meaning of ta'if. Abu Hatim said: I asked al-Asma'i about "tayyif", and he said: there is no fay'il among verbal nouns. Al-Nahhas said: it is not a verbal noun, but it has the meaning of ta'if. It was also said: al-tayf and al-ta'if are two different meanings: the first is imagination, and the second is Satan himself. The first comes from "taafa al-khayal yatifu tayfan", and they did not say from this "ta'if". Al-Suhayli said: because it is an imagining with no reality, but as for His saying ﴿Then there came upon it a visitation from your Lord﴾ (al-Qalam: 19), it is not called tayf there, because it is truly an active participle. Al-Zajjaj said: "tuftu 'alayhim atufu," so "taafa al-khayal yatifu."

Hassan said:
So leave this, but who is the phantom (la-tayf)
That keeps me awake when the night prayer has passed?

The whispering was called tayf because it is a passing thought from Satan which resembles the passing of imagination. ﴿Then they are seeing﴾, by means of remembrance, that is: they are awake (muntabihun). It is said: [they are] upon insight (ala basirah).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr read "tadhdhakkaru" with shaddah on the dhal. Al-Nahhas said: there is no basis for it in Arabic.

His saying: ﴿And their brothers extend them in error﴾. It is said: the meaning is: and the brothers of the devils, who are the wicked among the misguided humans, with the pronoun in "their brothers" referring to Satan mentioned earlier, and what is meant by it is the category, so it is permissible to return the plural pronoun to it. ﴿They extend them in error﴾, that is: the devils extend them in error and become a support for them. The wicked among humans were called the brothers of the devils because they accept from them and follow them. It is also said that what is meant by "the brothers" are the devils, and by the pronoun the wicked among humans, so the predicate applies to the one it belongs to.

Al-Zajjaj said: there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the speech, and the meaning is: "And those you invoke besides Him cannot help you nor help themselves." ﴿And their brothers extend them in error﴾, because the disbelievers are the brothers of the devils. ﴿Then they do not refrain﴾. Al-iqsar is ceasing from a thing, that is: the devils do not fall short in extending the disbelievers in error. It is said: "fi l-ghayy" is connected to His saying ﴿they extend them﴾, and it is said: it is connected to "the brothers." Al-ghayy is ignorance.

Nafi' read "yumiddunahum" with a damma on the letter of present tense and a kasra on the mim. The rest read with a fatha on the letter of present tense and a damma on the mim. Both are dialects: it is said "madda" and "amadda". Makki said: madda is more common. Abu 'Ubayd and a group of the people of language said: it is said that when one thing increases another by itself, one says "madda-hu", and when it increases it by means of something else, one says "amadda-hu," as in ﴿Your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand of the angels﴾ (Al 'Imran: 125). It is also said: one says "madadtu" in evil and "amdadtu" in good.

'Asim al-Jahdari read "yumadunahum fi l-ghayy".

'Isa ibn 'Umar read "thumma la yaqsuruna" with a fatha on the ya, a damma on the sad and a light qaf.

His saying: ﴿And when you do not bring them a sign, they say: "Why have you not devised it?"﴾. Ijtaba al-shay' means he gathered it for himself, that is, he collected it. That is: why did you not gather it (ijtama'ta), i.e., fabricate it (iftitalan) from your own self? It is said: the meaning is: you invented it. It is said: "ijtabaytu al-kalam": I appropriated it, invented it, and originated it when you bring it from your own self. They used to say this statement to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when revelation was delayed. So Allah commanded him to answer them with His saying: ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me﴾, that is: I am not one of those who brings signs from himself, as you claim. ﴿Say: "I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord"﴾; so what He revealed to me and sent down upon me, I have conveyed to you. And ﴿insights﴾ is the plural of basirah, that is: this Qur'an sent down upon me is ﴿insights from your Lord﴾ by which whoever accepts it sees clearly. It is said: the insights are proofs and demonstrations.

Al-Zajjaj said: the insights are paths. ﴿And guidance and mercy for a people who believe﴾ is coordinated with "insights," that is: this Qur'an is insights and guidance by which the believers are guided, and mercy for them.

His saying: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent﴾. Allah, glorified is He, commanded them to listen to the Qur'an and be silent for it when it is recited, so that they may benefit from it and reflect upon what is in it of wisdoms and benefits. It is said: this command is specific to the time of prayer when the imam recites. You are not unaware that the wording is broader than this, and a general ruling is not restricted to its occasion; so listening and silence during the recitation of the Qur'an are in every state and in whatever manner that is obligatory for the listener. It is also said: this is specific to the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ recitation of the Qur'an without others, and there is no basis for that. ﴿That you may be shown mercy﴾, that is: you may attain mercy and succeed in it by complying with the command of Allah, glorified is He.

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded him to remember Him within himself, for concealment is more conducive to sincerity and more inviting to acceptance. It is said: what is meant by the remembrance here is what is more general than the Qur'an and other forms of remembrance by which Allah is mentioned.

Al-Nahhas said: there is no disagreement about the meaning of ﴿And remember your Lord within yourself﴾, that it is supplication. It is also said: it is specific to the Qur'an, that is: recite the Qur'an with reflection and contemplation. ﴿Humbly and in fear﴾ are accusative as states, that is: humbly and fearfully. Al-khifah is fear; its root is khawfah, the waw was changed to ya because of the kasra before it. Al-Farra' related that it is said in the plural of khifah: khiyaf. Al-Jawhari said: al-khifah is fear, its plural is khiyaf, and its root is waw, that is: khawf.

﴿And below the loud voice in speech﴾, that is: below the spoken aloud speech. It is coordinated with what precedes it, that is: humbly, fearfully, and speaking with a speech which is below loudness. ﴿In the mornings and the evenings﴾ is connected to "remember," that is: at the times of the mornings and the times of the evenings. Al-ghuduww is the plural of ghadwah, and al-aseel is the plural of aseel. Al-Zajjaj and al-Akhfash said: [the plural of aseel is] aasal, like yamin and ayman. It is said: al-aasal is the plural of usul, and usul is the plural of aseel, so on this view it is a plural of a plural; this was stated by al-Farra'.

Al-Jawhari said: al-aseel is the time from after 'asr until maghrib, and its plural is usul, aasal and asa'il, as if it were the plural of aseelah.

The poet said:
By my life, you are the house whose people are most noble,
And sitting in its courtyards in the evenings.

It is also pluralized as usalan, like ba'ir and bu'ran. Abu Mijlaz read "wa-l-iysal," which is a verbal noun.

He singled out these two times for their nobility, and what is meant is the continuity of remembrance of Allah. ﴿And do not be among the heedless﴾, that is: heedless of the remembrance of Allah.

﴿Indeed, those who are near your Lord do not disdain His worship﴾. What is meant by them are the angels. Al-Qurtubi said: by consensus.

Al-Zajjaj said: He said "near your Lord," while Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is in every place, because they are close to His mercy, and everyone close to the mercy of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is near Him. Others said: because they are in a place where nothing takes effect except the command of Allah. It is said: they are the messengers of Allah, as one says "near the caliph there is a large army." It is also said: this is by way of honoring and dignifying them. The meaning of ﴿they exalt Him﴾ is: they magnify Him and declare Him free of every defect. ﴿And to Him they prostrate﴾, that is: they specify Him with the worship of prostration, which is the most noble worship. It is also said: what is meant by prostration is humility and submission. In the mention of the exalted assembly there is an indirect address to the children of Adam.

The ahadith and reports from the Companions concerning prostration of recitation (sujud al-tilawah), the number of places where prostration is performed, the manner of prostration and what is said in it are comprehensively found in the books of hadith and fiqh, so we will not lengthen the discussion by citing them here.
